from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class EigenDecompositionVisualIntuition(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title
        title = Text("Eigen Decomposition: Visual Intuition", font_size=36)
        title.to_edge(UP)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine you have a rotating shape that deforms under a transformation.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Create a unit circle to represent a shape
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        circle.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="What if I told you there are special directions in which this shape will merely stretch or shrink, without changing its orientation?") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(circle), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Show some regular vectors that rotate
        regular_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 1.5, buff=0, color=YELLOW)
        regular_vec.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="These special directions are defined by eigenvectors. Let us explore how matrices transform vectors.") as tracker:
            self.play(GrowArrow(regular_vec), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Define a transformation matrix A
        matrix_A = [[2, 1], [1, 2]]
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Consider this transformation matrix A.") as tracker:
            matrix_tex = MathTex(r"A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}")
            matrix_tex.to_corner(UR)
            self.play(Write(matrix_tex), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Transform the circle to show general deformation
        with self.voiceover(text="When we apply this matrix to our shape, it stretches and rotates in complex ways.") as tracker:
            self.play(ApplyMatrix(matrix_A, circle), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Clear and focus on eigenvectors
        self.play(FadeOut(circle), FadeOut(regular_vec))
        
        # Draw coordinate axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=8,
            y_length=6,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "numbers_to_exclude": []}
        )
        axes.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="But some vectors behave specially. Watch what happens to this vector.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(axes), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Create eigenvector 1 (pointing along y=x)
        eigen_v1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, UR * 2, buff=0, color=GREEN, stroke_width=4)
        eigen_v1.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        v1_label = MathTex(r"\mathbf{v}", color=GREEN).next_to(eigen_v1.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here is a vector pointing along the line y equals x.") as tracker:
            self.play(GrowArrow(eigen_v1), Write(v1_label), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Apply transformation to eigenvector - it only scales!
        transformed_v1 = Arrow(ORIGIN, UR * 6, buff=0, color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        transformed_v1.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="When we apply matrix A, notice something remarkable. This vector does not rotate. It only stretches.") as tracker:
            self.play(Transform(eigen_v1, transformed_v1), run_time=2)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Show the eigenvalue
        eigenvalue_label = MathTex(r"\lambda = 3", color=RED)
        eigenvalue_label.next_to(transformed_v1.get_end(), UR, buff=0.2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="It stretches by a factor of 3. This scaling factor is called the eigenvalue.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(eigenvalue_label), run_time=1.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Show the equation A v = lambda v
        eq1 = MathTex(r"A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}")
        eq1.to_corner(UL)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This is the fundamental eigenvalue equation. A times v equals lambda times v.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(eq1), run_time=1.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Fade out first eigenvector, show second
        self.play(FadeOut(eigen_v1), FadeOut(v1_label), FadeOut(eigenvalue_label))
        
        # Create eigenvector 2 (pointing along y=-x)
        eigen_v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, UL * 2, buff=0, color=GREEN, stroke_width=4)
        eigen_v2.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        v2_label = MathTex(r"\mathbf{v}", color=GREEN).next_to(eigen_v2.get_end(), UL, buff=0.1)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here is another eigenvector, pointing along y equals negative x.") as tracker:
            self.play(GrowArrow(eigen_v2), Write(v2_label), run_time=1.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Apply transformation to second eigenvector
        transformed_v2 = Arrow(ORIGIN, UL * 2 * 0.33, buff=0, color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        transformed_v2.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This one also does not rotate, but it shrinks. Its eigenvalue is 1.") as tracker:
            self.play(Transform(eigen_v2, transformed_v2), run_time=2)
        
        eigenvalue2_label = MathTex(r"\lambda = 1", color=RED)
        eigenvalue2_label.next_to(transformed_v2.get_end(), UL, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Write(eigenvalue2_label))
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Show characteristic equation
        self.play(FadeOut(eigen_v2), FadeOut(v2_label), FadeOut(eigenvalue2_label), FadeOut(eq1))
        
        char_eq = MathTex(r"\det(A - \lambda I) = 0")
        char_eq.to_corner(UL)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="To find eigenvalues, we solve this characteristic equation. The determinant of A minus lambda I equals zero.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(char_eq), run_time=2)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Show expanded form
        expanded = MathTex(r"\det\begin{bmatrix} 2-\lambda & 1 \\ 1 & 2-\lambda \end{bmatrix} = 0")
        expanded.next_to(char_eq, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="For our matrix, this becomes the determinant of a 2 by 2 matrix.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(expanded), run_time=1.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Show solutions
        solutions = MathTex(r"(\lambda - 3)(\lambda - 1) = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 3, 1")
        solutions.next_to(expanded, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Solving gives us our eigenvalues: 3 and 1. Just as we observed geometrically.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(solutions), run_time=1.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Summary
        self.play(FadeOut(char_eq), FadeOut(expanded), FadeOut(solutions), FadeOut(matrix_tex))

            self.play(Create(axes), Write(axes_labels), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Non-convex function: combination of sine and quadratic
        def loss_func(x):
            return 0.5 * (x/2)**2 - np.cos(2*x) * 0.5 + 1

        with self.voiceover(text="Unlike convex functions with a single global minimum, non-convex landscapes contain multiple local minima, saddle points, and flat regions.") as tracker:

        minima_x = [-2.2, 0, 2.2]

                    if abs(grad) < 0.05:

                # Draw path

                path.set_points_as_corners(path_points)

        with self.voiceover(text="To overcome these challenges, we employ several strategies. Smart initialization sets us on better paths.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(challenges_title), FadeOut(challenges), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(Write(strategies_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(strategy1), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Momentum helps us roll through shallow local minima and saddle points.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(strategy2), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Adaptive learning rates and random restarts improve our chances of finding the global optimum.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(strategy3), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Write(strategy4), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Momentum visualization

        # Restore graph

        )

        subtitle = Text("Finding the Slope of a Curve at a Point", font_size=28, color=GRAY)
        subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Ever wondered how we can find the slope of a curve at any given point, even though it bends and twists? The answer lies in the concept of the derivative, which we will explore through the lens of secant slopes!") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))
        
        # Set up coordinate axes
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 9, 1],

        )
        axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="x", y_label="y")
        
        # Define the function f(x) = x^2
        def func(x):
            return x**2
        
        # Plot the function
        graph = axes.plot(func, x_range=[0, 3], color=BLUE, stroke_width=3)
        graph_label = axes.get_graph_label(graph, label="f(x) = x^2", x_val=2.5, direction=UP)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's consider the function f of x equals x squared. We want to find the slope of this curve at a specific point, say x equals 1.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(axes), Write(axes_labels), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Create(graph), Write(graph_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        # Fixed point at x = 1
        x_fixed = 1
        point_fixed = axes.input_to_graph_point(x_fixed, graph)
        dot_fixed = Dot(point_fixed, color=YELLOW, radius=0.08)
        label_fixed = MathTex(r"P", color=YELLOW).next_to(dot_fixed, DOWN + LEFT, buff=0.15)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here's point P at x equals 1. The y-coordinate is f of 1, which equals 1.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(dot_fixed), Write(label_fixed), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Show secant lines with decreasing dx values
        dx_values = [1.5, 0.8, 0.4, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05]

        for i, dx in enumerate(dx_values):

                secant_line_color=GREEN,
                secant_line_length=8,

                dy_line_color=ORANGE,

            secant_groups.append(secant_group)

        # Show the slope formula
        slope_formula = MathTex(r"\text{slope} = \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}", font_size=32)
        slope_formula.to_corner(UL, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The slope of this secant line is the change in y divided by the change in x, which we call h.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(slope_formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Animate through decreasing dx values

messages.content: You are an expert mathematical animator and pedagogical engineer using Manim Community Edition and manim-voiceover with AOSSpeechService. Write executable, self-contained Python code that synchronizes mathematical animations with spoken educational explanations.

I'm learning advanced optimization to upper-level undergrads. Create a multi-scene animation visualizing gradient descent on a non-convex loss with at least two minima. Show a 3D surface and a 2D contour, with gradient-descent paths for different learning rates, including momentum, so we can compare convergence and saddle-point escape. Include a side plot of gradient norm over iterations and a zoomed-in view of curvature near the minima, using numerical simulation to generate the trajectories. Provide intuitive explanations before the equations and enable smooth scene transitions that highlight the intuition behind each concept.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService


class GradientDescentVisualization(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Set up speech service
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # === TITLE SCENE ===
        with self.voiceover(text="Have you ever wondered how machine learning algorithms optimize their performance? Imagine trying to find the lowest point in a mountainous landscape with your eyes closed!") as tracker:
            title = Text("Gradient Descent Visualization", font_size=48, color=BLUE)
            subtitle = Text("Finding the Optimal Solution", font_size=32, color=GRAY)
            title_group = VGroup(title, subtitle).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
            self.play(Write(title_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This process is similar to how gradient descent works, guiding us towards the optimal solution. Let's dive into it!") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(title_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # === SETUP AXES AND LOSS FUNCTION ===
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 8, 1],
            x_length=10,
            y_length=6,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GRAY},
        )
        
        axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="w (weight)", y_label="L(w) (loss)")
        
        # Loss function: f(w) = 0.5 * w^2 (simple quadratic)
        loss_graph = axes.plot(
            lambda x: 0.5 * x**2,
            x_range=[-3.5, 3.5],
            color=BLUE,
            stroke_width=3
        )
        
        loss_label = MathTex(r"L(w) = \frac{1}{2}w^2", color=BLUE, font_size=36)
        loss_label.next_to(loss_graph.get_top(), RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here we have a loss function, which measures how bad our model's predictions are. Our goal is to find the weight value that minimizes this loss.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(axes), Write(axes_labels), run_time=2)
            self.play(Create(loss_graph), Write(loss_label), run_time=2)
        
        # === INITIAL POINT ===
        # Start at w = 3
        w_start = 3
        start_point = axes.c2p(w_start, 0.5 * w_start**2)
        
        initial_dot = Dot(start_point, color=RED, radius=0.1)
        initial_label = MathTex(r"w_0 = 3", color=RED, font_size=30)
        initial_label.next_to(initial_dot, UR, buff=0.2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's start at an initial weight of 3. We can see this point is far from the minimum, so our loss is quite high.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(initial_dot), Write(initial_label), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # === SHOW GRADIENT (SLOPE) ===
        # Gradient at w=3: df/dw = w = 3
        gradient_value = w_start
        
        # Draw tangent line to show gradient
        tangent_line = axes.get_secant_slope_group(
            x=3,
            graph=loss_graph,
            dx=0.01,
            secant_line_length=4,
            secant_line_color=YELLOW,
        )
        
        gradient_arrow = Arrow(
            start=axes.c2p(w_start, 0.5 * w_start**2),
            end=axes.c2p(w_start + 0.8, 0.5 * w_start**2 + gradient_value * 0.8),
            color=YELLOW,
            buff=0,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        gradient_label = MathTex(r"\nabla L = w = 3", color=YELLOW, font_size=28)
        gradient_label.next_to(gradient_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The gradient tells us which direction the function increases most steeply. At w equals 3, the gradient equals 3, pointing uphill.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(gradient_arrow), Write(gradient_label), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # === UPDATE FORMULA ===
        update_formula = MathTex(r"w_{new} = w_{old} - \eta \cdot \nabla L", font_size=36)
        update_formula.to_corner(UL, buff=0.5)
        
        lr_formula = MathTex(r"\eta = 0.3", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
        lr_formula.next_to(update_formula, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="To minimize the loss, we update our weight using this formula. We subtract the gradient times a learning rate. Let's use a learning rate of 0.3.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(update_formula), Write(lr_formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # === FIRST UPDATE ===
        lr = 0.3
        w_new = w_start - lr * gradient_value
        new_point = axes.c2p(w_new, 0.5 * w_new**2)
        
        new_dot = Dot(new_point, color=GREEN, radius=0.1)
        new_label = MathTex(r"w_1 = " + f"{w_new:.2f}", color=GREEN, font_size=30)
        new_label.next_to(new_dot, UR, buff=0.2)
        
        # Arrow showing the update step
        step_arrow = Arrow(initial_dot.get_center(), new_dot.get_center(), color=GREEN, buff=0.1)
        
        calculation = MathTex(r"3 - 0.3 \times 3 = 2.1", font_size=28, color=GREEN)
        calculation.next_to(lr_formula, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="So our new weight is 3 minus 0.3 times 3, which equals 2.1. We moved down the loss curve!") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(gradient_arrow), FadeOut(gradient_label), run_time=0.5)
            self.play(Create(step_arrow), FadeIn(new_dot), Write(new_label), Write(calculation), run_time=tracker.duration - 0.5)
        
        # === MULTIPLE ITERATIONS ===
        points = [initial_dot, new_dot]
        labels = [initial_label, new_label]
        current_w = w_new
        
        point_colors = [ORANGE, PURPLE, PINK, TEAL]
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's continue this process for a few more iterations, following the gradient down the curve.") as tracker:
            for i, color in enumerate(point_colors[:4]):
                # Calculate gradient at current point
                grad = current_w
                w_next = current_w - lr * grad
                
                next_point_coords = axes.c2p(w_next, 0.5 * w_next**2)
                next_dot = Dot(next_point_coords, color=color, radius=0.08)
                
                next_label = MathTex(f"w_{{ {i+2} }} = {w_next:.3f}", font_size=24, color=color)
                next_label.next_to(next_dot, UR if i % 2 == 0 else DR, buff=0.15)
                
                step = Arrow(points[-1].get_center(), next_dot.get_center(), color=color, buff=0.05, stroke_width=3)
                
                self.play(Create(step), FadeIn(next_dot), Write(next_label), run_time=0.8)
                
                points.append(next_dot)
                labels.append(next_label)
                current_w = w_next
        
        # === PATH TRACE ===
        # Draw the full path as a dashed line
        path_points = [p.get_center() for p in points]
        path_line = VMobject()
        path_line.set_points_as_corners(path_points)
        path_line.set_stroke(color=YELLOW, width=3, opacity=0.8)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Notice how the steps get smaller as we approach the minimum. This is because the gradient becomes gentler near the bottom of the curve.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(path_line), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # === MINIMUM POINT ===
        min_point = axes.c2p(0, 0)
        min_dot = Dot(min_point, color=GOLD, radius=0.12)
        min_label = MathTex(r"w^* = 0\text{ (minimum)}", color=GOLD, font_size=32)
        min_label.next_to(min_dot, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        min_circle = Circle(radius=0.3, color=GOLD, stroke_width=2)
        min_circle.move_to(min_dot)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Eventually, we reach the minimum at w equals 0, where the loss is zero. This is the optimal solution!") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(min_dot), Write(min_label), Create(min_circle), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # === CLEANUP AND SUMMARY ===
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's review what we learned.") as tracker:
            # Fade out most elements, keep only key elements
            all_labels = VGroup(*[l for l in labels], initial_label, new_label, loss_label, min_label)
            all_dots = VGroup(*points[2:], min_dot)
            self.play(
                FadeOut(all_labels),
                FadeOut(all_dots),
                FadeOut(calculation),
                FadeOut(lr_formula),
                FadeOut(update_formula),
                FadeOut(path_line),
                FadeOut(min_circle),
                FadeOut(step_arrow),
                FadeOut(initial_dot),
                run_time=1
            )
        
        # === LEARNING OUTCOMES ===
        outcome1 = Text("1. Gradient descent iteratively adjusts parameters", font_size=28)
        outcome2 = Text("by following the negative gradient", font_size=28)
        outcome3 = Text("2. The path converges to the optimal solution", font_size=28)
        outcome4 = Text("where the loss is minimized", font_size=28)
        
        outcomes = VGroup(outcome1, outcome2, outcome3, outcome4)
        outcomes.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        outcomes.to_edge(LEFT, buff=1)
        
        # Keep axes and graph visible
        with self.voiceover(text="Gradient descent works by iteratively adjusting parameters in the direction opposite to the gradient. The learning rate controls how big each step is. With each iteration, we get closer to the optimal solution.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                axes.animate.scale(0.6).to_corner(DR, buff=0.5),
                loss_graph.animate.scale(0.6).to_corner(DR, buff=0.5),
                FadeIn(outcomes),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        # Show the final formula
        final_formula = MathTex(r"w_{new} = w_{old} - \eta \cdot \nabla f(w_{old})", font_size=40, color=BLUE)
        final_formula.next_to(outcomes, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        final_box = SurroundingRectangle(final_formula, color=YELLOW, buff=0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Remember this fundamental equation. It's the heart of optimization in machine learning.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(final_formula), Create(final_box), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === FINALE ===
        with self.voiceover(text="Thank you for watching! Now you understand how gradient descent guides machine learning models toward optimal performance.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(final_formula),
                FadeOut(final_box),
                FadeOut(outcomes),
                FadeOut(axes),
                FadeOut(loss_graph),
                run_time=1
            )
            
            thanks = Text("Thank You!", font_size=56, color=BLUE)
            self.play(Write(thanks), run_time=1)
        
        self.wait(2)
```

        sorted_edges = sorted(edges_data, key=lambda x: x[2])
        
        # Create sorted list display
        sort_title = Text("Edges Sorted by Weight:", font_size=26, color=GREEN)
        sort_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Transform(problem_title, sort_title))
        
        # Create table of sorted edges
        table_items = []
        for i, (n1, n2, w) in enumerate(sorted_edges):
            edge_text = Text(f"{n1}-{n2}: {w}", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
            table_items.append(edge_text)
        
        # Arrange in two columns
        left_col = VGroup(*table_items[:5])
        left_col.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.25)
        left_col.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        left_col.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        right_col = VGroup(*table_items[5:])
        right_col.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.25)
        right_col.to_edge(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        right_col.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="First, we sort all edges by weight. The edge from D to E has the smallest weight of 1, followed by A to D with weight 2, and so on.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(all_nodes), FadeOut(all_edges), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(FadeIn(left_col), FadeIn(right_col), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Now show the algorithm step by step
        step_title = Text("Building the MST Step by Step", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        step_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(left_col), FadeOut(right_col), Transform(problem_title, step_title))
        
        # Redraw the graph
        self.play(FadeIn(all_nodes), FadeIn(all_edges))
        
        # Track connected components for cycle detection
        parent = {n: n for n in vertices.keys()}
        
        def find(x):
            if parent[x] != x:
                parent[x] = find(parent[x])
            return parent[x]
        
        def union(x, y):
            px, py = find(x), find(y)
            if px != py:
                parent[px] = py
        
        # MST edges storage
        mst_edges = []
        total_weight = 0
        
        # Info display
        info_box = RoundedRectangle(width=4, height=1.5, corner_radius=0.2, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=0.8)
        info_box.to_edge(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        info_box.shift(UP * 1.5)
        
        total_text = Text("Total Cost: 0", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        total_text.move_to(info_box.get_center() + UP * 0.3)
        
        edges_text = Text("Edges Added: 0", font_size=18, color=GREEN)
        edges_text.move_to(info_box.get_center() + DOWN * 0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(info_box), Write(total_text), Write(edges_text))
        
        # Process each edge
        step_num = 1
        for n1, n2, w in sorted_edges:
            edge_key = tuple(sorted([n1, n2]))
            line = edge_lines[edge_key]
            weight_label = edge_weights[edge_key]
            
            # Highlight current edge being considered
            highlight_line = Line(vertices[n1], vertices[n2], color=YELLOW, stroke_width=6)
            
            with self.voiceover(text=f"Step {step_num}: Consider edge {n1} to {n2} with weight {w}.") as tracker:
                self.play(Create(highlight_line), run_time=tracker.duration)
            
            # Check if adding this edge creates a cycle
            if find(n1) != find(n2):
                # No cycle - add to MST
                union(n1, n2)
                mst_edges.append((n1, n2, w))
                total_weight += w
                
                with self.voiceover(text=f"Nodes {n1} and {n2} are in different sets, so adding this edge won't create a cycle. We include it in our MST.") as tracker:
                    # Animate adding to MST
                    self.play(
                        line.animate.set_color(GREEN).set_stroke(width=5),
                        weight_label.animate.set_color(GREEN),
                        FadeOut(highlight_line),
                        run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7
                    )
                    # Update info
                    new_total = Text(f"Total Cost: {total_weight}", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
                    new_total.move_to(info_box.get_center() + UP * 0.3)
                    new_edges = Text(f"Edges Added: {len(mst_edges)}", font_size=18, color=GREEN)
                    new_edges.move_to(info_box.get_center() + DOWN * 0.2)
                    self.play(
                        Transform(total_text, new_total),
                        Transform(edges_text, new_edges),
                        run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3
                    )
            else:
                # Would create a cycle - reject
                with self.voiceover(text=f"Nodes {n1} and {n2} are already connected. Adding this edge would create a cycle, so we skip it.") as tracker:
                    # Flash red to indicate rejection
                    self.play(
                        line.animate.set_color(RED),
                        weight_label.animate.set_color(RED),
                        run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4
                    )
                    self.play(
                        line.animate.set_color(GRAY),
                        weight_label.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
                        FadeOut(highlight_line),
                        run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6
                    )
            
            step_num += 1
            
            # Stop if we have n-1 edges
            if len(mst_edges) == len(vertices) - 1:
                break
        
        # Final result
        with self.voiceover(text=f"We've successfully built the Minimum Spanning Tree with {len(mst_edges)} edges and a total cost of {total_weight}.") as tracker:
            # Pulse the MST edges
            self.play(
                *[line.animate.set_color(GREEN).set_stroke(width=6) for (n1, n2, _) in mst_edges 
                  for edge_key, line in edge_lines.items() if edge_key == tuple(sorted([n1, n2]))],
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5
            )
            self.play(
                *[line.animate.set_stroke(width=4) for (n1, n2, _) in mst_edges 
                  for edge_key, line in edge_lines.items() if edge_key == tuple(sorted([n1, n2]))],
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5
            )
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Summary
        self.play(FadeOut(info_box), FadeOut(total_text), FadeOut(edges_text), FadeOut(problem_title))
        
        # Create summary
        summary_title = Text("Key Takeaways", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
        summary_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        takeaways = [
            "1. Sort all edges by weight",
            "2. Add smallest edge that doesn't form a cycle",
            "3. Use Union-Find to detect cycles",
            "4. Stop when we have V-1 edges",
        ]
        
        takeaway_objs = [Text(t, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for t in takeaways]
        takeaway_group = VGroup(*takeaway_objs)
        takeaway_group.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        takeaway_group.shift(UP * 0.5)
        
        # Final MST visualization on the side
        mst_highlight = []
        for n1, n2, w in mst_edges:
            p1 = vertices[n1]
            p2 = vertices[n2]
            glow_line = Line(p1, p2, color=GREEN, stroke_width=8, stroke_opacity=0.5)
            mst_highlight.append(glow_line)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="To summarize: Kruskal's Algorithm sorts edges by weight, then greedily adds the smallest edges while avoiding cycles using the Union-Find data structure. We stop when we have exactly V minus 1 edges, where V is the number of vertices.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(summary_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(*[FadeIn(t) for t in takeaway_objs], run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(*[FadeIn(m) for m in mst_highlight], run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Final fade out
        self.play(FadeOut(summary_title), FadeOut(takeaway_group), FadeOut(all_nodes), 
                  FadeOut(all_edges), FadeOut(*mst_highlight))
        
        # Closing
        closing = Text("Kruskal's Algorithm: Efficient MST Construction", font_size=32, color=BLUE)
        thanks = Text("Thanks for watching!", font_size=24, color=GRAY)
        thanks.next_to(closing, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Kruskal's Algorithm efficiently finds the Minimum Spanning Tree with a time complexity of E log E, where E is the number of edges. Thanks for watching!") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(closing), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(FadeIn(thanks), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(closing), FadeOut(thanks))
```

messages.content: You are an expert mathematical animator and pedagogical engineer using Manim Community Edition and manim-voiceover with AOSSpeechService. Write executable, self-contained Python code that synchronizes mathematical animations with spoken educational explanations.

I need a visual explanation of the spectral theorem for linear algebra, aimed at advanced undergrads.
Show a symmetric matrix acting on 3D vectors, with eigenvectors as fixed directions and arrows colored by component contributions.
Animate the decomposition of any vector into its eigenbasis and the corresponding projections, then illustrate how the transformation acts as a scale along those axes.
Include multiple scenes: original vector field, basis change, and a side-by-side comparison of original and transformed shapes.
I want intuitive motion first, then derive the formula on screen with a visual derivation of the diagonalization process.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService


class SpectralTheoremScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup speech service
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # ========== INTRODUCTION ==========
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine you have a complex system where everything seems chaotic. Yet, with the right perspective, you discover there's an underlying structure waiting to be uncovered.") as tracker:
            # Title appears
            title = Text("The Spectral Theorem", font_size=48, color=BLUE)
            subtitle = Text("for Symmetric Matrices", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
            title_group = VGroup(title, subtitle).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
            self.play(Write(title_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This captivating journey leads us to the core of the Spectral Theorem for Symmetric Matrices, a powerful tool that reveals the hidden harmony within matrices!") as tracker:
            self.play(title_group.animate.scale(0.6).to_edge(UP), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ========== DEFINITION OF SYMMETRIC MATRIX ==========
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's begin with the foundation. A symmetric matrix is a square matrix that equals its own transpose. If A is symmetric, then A equals A transpose.") as tracker:
            # Symmetric matrix definition
            sym_def = MathTex(r"A = A^{T}", font_size=44)
            sym_text = Text("A is symmetric", font_size=28, color=YELLOW)
            sym_group = VGroup(sym_def, sym_text).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
            sym_group.move_to(ORIGIN)
            self.play(Write(sym_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Visually, this means the matrix is a mirror image across its main diagonal. Let's see an example.") as tracker:
            self.play(sym_group.animate.to_edge(LEFT, buff=1.5), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            
            # Example symmetric matrix using simple numbers
            sym_matrix = Matrix([
                ["2", "3", "1"],
                ["3", "5", "4"],
                ["1", "4", "6"]
            ])
            sym_matrix.scale(0.8)
            sym_matrix.next_to(sym_group, RIGHT, buff=1.5)
            self.play(Create(sym_matrix), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        # Fade out and prepare for main theorem
        self.play(FadeOut(sym_group), FadeOut(sym_matrix))
        
        # ========== THE SPECTRAL THEOREM STATEMENT ==========
        with self.voiceover(text="Now, here is the Spectral Theorem in all its elegance. Every real symmetric matrix can be decomposed into a product of three special matrices.") as tracker:
            theorem_title = Text("The Spectral Theorem", font_size=36, color=GREEN)
            theorem_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.8)
            self.play(Write(theorem_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            
            # Main decomposition formula
            decomposition = MathTex(r"A = Q", r"\Lambda", r"Q^{T}", font_size=52)
            decomposition.set_color_by_tex(r"\Lambda", RED)
            decomposition.move_to(ORIGIN)
            self.play(Write(decomposition), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # ========== BREAKING DOWN THE COMPONENTS ==========
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's break down what each component represents. First, Q is an orthogonal matrix whose columns are the eigenvectors of A.") as tracker:
            # Move decomposition up
            self.play(decomposition.animate.shift(UP * 1.5), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            
            # Label Q
            q_label = MathTex(r"Q = [v_1, v_2, ... , v_n]", font_size=32)
            q_desc = Text("orthogonal matrix of eigenvectors", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
            q_group = VGroup(q_label, q_desc).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
            q_group.move_to(ORIGIN + DOWN * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(q_group), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The key property of Q is that Q transpose times Q equals the identity matrix. This means the eigenvectors are orthonormal.") as tracker:
            # Orthogonality property
            ortho_eq = MathTex(r"Q^{T} Q = I", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            ortho_eq.next_to(q_group, DOWN, buff=0.4)
            self.play(Write(ortho_eq), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Next, Lambda is a diagonal matrix containing the eigenvalues of A along its diagonal.") as tracker:
            # Fade out q_group and ortho_eq
            self.play(FadeOut(q_group), FadeOut(ortho_eq), run_time=0.5)
            
            # Lambda explanation
            lambda_label = MathTex(r"\Lambda = diag(\lambda_1, \lambda_2, ..., \lambda_n)", font_size=32)
            lambda_desc = Text("diagonal matrix of eigenvalues", font_size=24, color=RED)
            lambda_group = VGroup(lambda_label, lambda_desc).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
            lambda_group.move_to(ORIGIN + DOWN * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(lambda_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Show diagonal matrix visually
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Visually, Lambda has the eigenvalues on the diagonal and zeros everywhere else.") as tracker:
            # Create a simple diagonal matrix with placeholders
            diag_matrix = Matrix([
                ["l1", "0", "0"],
                ["0", "l2", "0"],
                ["0", "0", "l3"]
            ])
            diag_matrix.scale(0.8)
            diag_matrix.next_to(lambda_group, DOWN, buff=0.3)
            
            # Color the diagonal differently
            entries = diag_matrix.get_entries()
            entries[0].set_color(RED)  # l1
            entries[4].set_color(RED)  # l2
            entries[8].set_color(RED)  # l3
            
            self.play(Create(diag_matrix), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # ========== SIGNIFICANCE OF ORTHOGONALITY ==========
        with self.voiceover(text="Now, let's understand why orthogonality is so crucial. When eigenvectors are orthogonal, they form a perfect coordinate system.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(lambda_group),
                FadeOut(diag_matrix),
                FadeOut(theorem_title),
                run_time=0.5
            )
            
            # Center the decomposition again
            self.play(decomposition.animate.move_to(ORIGIN + UP * 1), run_time=0.5)
            
            # Create visual of orthogonal vectors
            axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], x_length=6, y_length=6)
            axes.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
            
            # Two orthogonal vectors
            v1 = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(2.5, 0), color=BLUE, buff=0)
            v2 = Arrow(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, 2.5), color=RED, buff=0)
            
            v1_label = MathTex(r"v_1", font_size=28, color=BLUE).next_to(v1, RIGHT)
            v2_label = MathTex(r"v_2", font_size=28, color=RED).next_to(v2, UP)
            
            orthog_visual = VGroup(axes, v1, v2, v1_label, v2_label)
            orthog_visual.scale(0.7)
            orthog_visual.to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.8)
            
            self.play(Create(axes), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2), Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="These perpendicular eigenvectors create a new basis where the transformation becomes simple stretching along each axis.") as tracker:
            # Show right angle marker
            right_angle = RightAngle(v1, v2, length=0.3, color=YELLOW)
            self.play(Create(right_angle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
            # Add dot product explanation
            dot_eq = MathTex(r"v_i \cdot v_j = 0 \text{ for } i \neq j", font_size=28)
            dot_eq.next_to(orthog_visual, RIGHT, buff=0.5)
            self.play(Write(dot_eq), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # ========== EIGENVALUE EQUATION ==========
        with self.voiceover(text="Recall the fundamental eigenvalue equation. A times v equals lambda times v.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(orthog_visual),
                FadeOut(dot_eq),
                FadeOut(right_angle),
                FadeOut(decomposition),
                run_time=0.5
            )
            
            eigen_eq = MathTex(r"Av = \lambda v", font_size=48)
            eigen_eq.move_to(ORIGIN)
            self.play(Write(eigen_eq), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="For symmetric matrices, this equation has real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors. This is the magic of the Spectral Theorem.") as tracker:
            prop1 = MathTex(r"\bullet \lambda_i \in \mathbb{R}", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
            prop2 = MathTex(r"\bullet v_i \perp v_j", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
            
            properties = VGroup(prop1, prop2).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            properties.next_to(eigen_eq, DOWN, buff=0.6)
            self.play(Write(properties), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # ========== COMPLETE DECOMPOSITION VISUAL ==========
        with self.voiceover(text="Putting it all together, we see the full decomposition. The symmetric matrix A equals Q Lambda Q transpose.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(eigen_eq), FadeOut(properties), run_time=0.5)
            
            # Show full decomposition with matrices
            full_decomp = MathTex(r"A = Q", r"\Lambda", r"Q^{T}", font_size=44)
            full_decomp.set_color_by_tex(r"\Lambda", RED)
            full_decomp.move_to(ORIGIN + UP * 0.5)
            self.play(Write(full_decomp), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
            # Labels below
            label_a = VGroup(
                Text("symmetric", font_size=20, color=BLUE), 
                MathTex(r"A = A^{T}", font_size=20)
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
            
            label_q1 = VGroup(
                Text("orthogonal", font_size=20, color=GREEN), 
                MathTex(r"Q^{T}Q = I", font_size=20)
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
            
            label_lambda = VGroup(
                Text("diagonal", font_size=20, color=RED), 
                Text("eigenvalues", font_size=20)
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
            
            label_q2 = VGroup(
                Text("orthogonal", font_size=20, color=GREEN), 
                MathTex(r"Q^{T}Q = I", font_size=20)
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
            
            labels = VGroup(label_a, label_q1, label_lambda, label_q2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
            labels.next_to(full_decomp, DOWN, buff=0.6)
            
            self.play(Write(labels), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # ========== WHY THIS MATTERS ==========
        with self.voiceover(text="Why does this matter? The Spectral Theorem tells us that symmetric matrices are diagonalizable by an orthogonal transformation.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(labels), run_time=0.3)
            
            # Key insight
            insight = Text("Symmetric matrices are always diagonalizable!", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
            insight.next_to(full_decomp, DOWN, buff=0.6)
            self.play(Write(insight), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This means we can always find a coordinate system where the transformation is just stretching along orthogonal axes.") as tracker:
            # Additional insights in two columns
            insights_left = VGroup(
                Text("- Real eigenvalues", font_size=24),
                Text("- Orthogonal eigenvectors", font_size=24),
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            
            insights_right = VGroup(
                Text("- Perfect for PCA", font_size=24),
                Text("- Physical symmetries", font_size=24),
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            
            insights = VGroup(insights_left, insights_right).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.5)
            insights.next_to(insight, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(insights), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # ========== SUMMARY ==========
        with self.voiceover(text="To summarize what you've learned today: You can now state the Spectral Theorem clearly.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(insights),
                FadeOut(insight),
                FadeOut(full_decomp),
                run_time=0.5
            )
            
            summary1 = Text("1. State the Spectral Theorem", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
            summary1.move_to(ORIGIN + UP * 1.5)
            self.play(Write(summary1), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        self.wait(0.2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="You can compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors of symmetric matrices effectively.") as tracker:
            summary2 = Text("2. Compute eigenvalues & eigenvectors", font_size=28, color=GREEN)
            summary2.next_to(summary1, DOWN, buff=0.4)
            self.play(Write(summary2), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="And you can appreciate the significance of orthogonality in this beautiful decomposition.") as tracker:
            summary3 = Text("3. Appreciate orthogonality", font_size=28, color=RED)
            summary3.next_to(summary2, DOWN, buff=0.4)
            self.play(Write(summary3), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # ========== FINAL FORMULA ==========
        with self.voiceover(text="Remember this elegant formula. A equals Q Lambda Q transpose. This is the heart of the Spectral Theorem for symmetric matrices.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(summary1),
                FadeOut(summary2),
                FadeOut(summary3),
                run_time=0.5
            )
            
            final_formula = MathTex(r"A = Q", r"\Lambda", r"Q^{T}", font_size=60)
            final_formula.set_color_by_tex(r"\Lambda", RED)
            final_formula.move_to(ORIGIN)
            
            # Add a box around it
            box = SurroundingRectangle(final_formula, color=YELLOW, buff=0.3)

from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService
import numpy as np


class GradientDescentAnimation(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Set up speech service

            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # ============== SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION ==============
        with self.voiceover(text="Have you ever wondered how deep learning models learn from data? In this lecture, we will uncover the magic of gradient descent, the backbone of most optimization algorithms in machine learning. You will see it in action, and by the end, you will understand its significance in training models.") as tracker:
            # Title screen

            self.play(Write(title), Write(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.8)
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.2)
            
        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))
        
        # ============== SECTION 2: THE LOSS FUNCTION ==============
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's begin with a simple question. How do we find the minimum of a function? Imagine you're standing on a hillside and want to reach the bottom. This is exactly what gradient descent does.") as tracker:
            # Create axes for the parabola
            axes = Axes(
                x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
                y_range=[-1, 10, 2],
                x_length=10,
                y_length=6,
                axis_config={"include_numbers": True}
            )
            axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="x", y_label="f(x)")
            
            # Plot f(x) = x^2
            parabola = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[-3, 3], color=BLUE)
            func_label = MathTex(r"f(x) = x^2", color=BLUE, font_size=36)
            func_label.to_corner(UR, buff=0.8)
            
            self.play(Create(axes), Write(axes_labels), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Create(parabola), Write(func_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.2)
            
        # ============== SECTION 3: THE GRADIENT CONCEPT ==============
        with self.voiceover(text="At any point on this curve, the gradient tells us which way is uphill. The gradient is simply the derivative, which for x squared equals 2x. The negative gradient points downhill, toward the minimum.") as tracker:
            # Show the gradient formula
            grad_formula = MathTex(r"\frac{\partial f}{\partial x} = 2x", color=YELLOW, font_size=36)
            grad_formula.next_to(func_label, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            self.play(Write(grad_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
            # Show a tangent line at x = 2
            x_val = 2
            point_on_curve = axes.c2p(x_val, x_val**2)
            
            # Gradient at x=2 is 4
            tangent_line = axes.plot(
                lambda x: 4 * (x - x_val) + x_val**2,

            )
            
            # Add point
            dot = Dot(point_on_curve, color=RED, radius=0.1)
            point_label = MathTex("x=2", color=RED, font_size=24)
            point_label.next_to(dot, UP + RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            
            self.play(Create(dot), Write(point_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Create(tangent_line), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            
        self.play(FadeOut(tangent_line), FadeOut(point_label))
        
        # ============== SECTION 4: GRADIENT DESCENT STEPS ==============
        with self.voiceover(text="Now watch gradient descent in action. We start at point x equals 2. At each step, we move in the direction opposite to the gradient. The size of our step is controlled by the learning rate.") as tracker:
            # Show update equation
            update_eq = MathTex(r"x_{new} = x_{old} - \eta \cdot \nabla f(x)", 
                                 color=GREEN, font_size=32)
            update_eq.to_corner(UL, buff=0.3)
            lr_label = MathTex(r"\eta = \text{learning rate}", color=ORANGE, font_size=24)
            lr_label.next_to(update_eq, DOWN, buff=0.3)
            
            self.play(FadeIn(update_eq), FadeIn(lr_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            
            # Initialize gradient descent
            learning_rate = 0.3
            x_current = 2.0
            num_steps = 6
            
            all_points = VGroup(dot)
            path_lines = VGroup()
            
            self.play(dot.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(x_current, x_current**2)))
            
            for step in range(num_steps):
                # Calculate gradient at current point
                gradient = 2 * x_current
                x_new = x_current - learning_rate * gradient
                
                # Get positions
                old_pos = axes.c2p(x_current, x_current**2)
                new_pos = axes.c2p(x_new, x_new**2)
                
                # Draw arrow showing direction
                arrow = Arrow(old_pos, new_pos, color=GREEN, buff=0.05, stroke_width=3)
                arrow.scale(0.8)
                
                # Step label
                step_text = Text(f"Step {step + 1}", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
                step_text.to_corner(DL, buff=0.5)
                
                # Create new dot
                new_dot = Dot(new_pos, color=RED, radius=0.08)
                
                play_time = 0.8
                
                self.play(
                    Create(arrow),
                    FadeIn(new_dot),
                    FadeIn(step_text),
                    run_time=play_time * 0.5
                )
                
                # Move the main dot
                self.play(
                    dot.animate.move_to(new_pos),
                    run_time=play_time * 0.5
                )
                
                # Cleanup
                self.remove(arrow, new_dot, step_text)
                
                x_current = x_new
            
            # Final point
            final_label = MathTex(r"x \approx 0.01", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
            final_label.next_to(dot, UP + LEFT, buff=0.2)
            self.play(Write(final_label))
            
        # ============== SECTION 5: LEARNING RATE COMPARISON ==============
        self.play(FadeOut(update_eq), FadeOut(lr_label), FadeOut(final_label), FadeOut(grad_formula))
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The learning rate is crucial. Too small, and convergence is painfully slow. Too large, and we might overshoot and oscillate, or even diverge. Let's compare three different learning rates.") as tracker:
            # Clear and restart with comparison
            self.play(FadeOut(dot))

            lr_colors = [GREEN, ORANGE, PURPLE]
            lr_names = ["eta=0.1", "eta=0.5", "eta=0.9"]
            
            all_dots = []
            
            for i, (lr, color, name) in enumerate(zip(learning_rates, lr_colors, lr_names)):
                # Start position (offset for visibility)
                x_start = 2.5 - i * 0.1
                x_current = x_start
                
                # Create starting dot
                start_pos = axes.c2p(x_current, x_current**2)
                lr_dot = Dot(start_pos, color=color, radius=0.08)
                lr_text = MathTex(name, color=color, font_size=20)
                lr_text.next_to(axes.c2p(3.5, 8 - i*1.5), RIGHT, buff=0.2)
                
                self.play(FadeIn(lr_dot), FadeIn(lr_text), run_time=0.5)
                
                # Run a few gradient descent steps
                num_steps = 5
                for step in range(num_steps):
                    gradient = 2 * x_current
                    x_new = x_current - lr * gradient
                    
                    old_pos = axes.c2p(x_current, x_current**2)
                    new_pos = axes.c2p(x_new, x_new**2)
                    
                    # Draw path
                    path = Line(old_pos, new_pos, color=color, stroke_width=2)
                    
                    self.play(
                        Create(path),
                        lr_dot.animate.move_to(new_pos),
                        run_time=0.6
                    )
                    
                    x_current = x_new
                
                all_dots.append(lr_dot)
                
        with self.voiceover(text="Notice how the small learning rate of 0.1 converges slowly but surely. The medium rate of 0.5 finds a nice balance. With a rate of 0.9, we overshoot repeatedly, zigzagging toward the minimum.") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration)
            
        # ============== SECTION 6: KEY TAKEAWAYS ==============
        self.play(
            FadeOut(lr_title),
            FadeOut(parabola),
            FadeOut(axes),
            FadeOut(axes_labels),
            FadeOut(func_label),
            *[FadeOut(d) for d in all_dots]
        )
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's summarize what you have learned today. Gradient descent is an iterative optimization algorithm that finds the minimum of a function.") as tracker:
            takeaway1 = Text("1. Gradient Descent finds the minimum of functions", 
                          font_size=28, color=BLUE)
            takeaway1.to_edge(UP, buff=1)
            self.play(Write(takeaway1), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="At each step, it moves in the direction opposite to the gradient, scaled by the learning rate.") as tracker:
            takeaway2 = Text("2. Move opposite to the gradient: x_new = x_old - eta * gradient", 
                          font_size=26, color=GREEN)
            takeaway2.next_to(takeaway1, DOWN, buff=0.6)
            self.play(Write(takeaway2), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="The learning rate is a critical hyperparameter that controls the step size. Finding the right balance is essential for efficient convergence.") as tracker:
            takeaway3 = Text("3. Learning rate controls convergence speed and stability", 
                          font_size=26, color=ORANGE)
            takeaway3.next_to(takeaway2, DOWN, buff=0.6)
            self.play(Write(takeaway3), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
        with self.voiceover(text="Gradient descent is the foundation of how neural networks learn. Every time you train a model, gradient descent is navigating the error landscape to find the best parameters. Now you understand the magic behind the learning.") as tracker:
            takeaway4 = Text("4. Powers the training of deep learning models", 
                          font_size=26, color=PURPLE)
            takeaway4.next_to(takeaway3, DOWN, buff=0.6)
            self.play(Write(takeaway4), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
            # Box all takeaways
            all_takeaways = VGroup(takeaway1, takeaway2, takeaway3, takeaway4)
            box = SurroundingRectangle(all_takeaways, color=YELLOW, buff=0.3)
            self.play(Create(box), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Fade out everything
        self.play(
            FadeOut(takeaway1), FadeOut(takeaway2), FadeOut(takeaway3), FadeOut(takeaway4),
            FadeOut(box)
        )
        
        # Final message
        with self.voiceover(text="Thank you for watching. Gradient descent turns the complex problem of training neural networks into simple downhill walks. Keep learning!") as tracker:
            final_text = Text("Keep Learning!", font_size=48, color=BLUE)
            self.play(Write(final_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.wait(1)

import numpy as np
from manim import (
    Axes, MathTex, Text, VGroup, 
    Write, Create, FadeOut, Transform, 
    BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, RED, GRAY, PINK,
    PI, UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, DL
)
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService


class FourierSeriesScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title and intro
        title = Text("Fourier Series Convergence", font_size=40, color=BLUE)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Have you ever wondered how complex waveforms can be represented as simple sine and cosine waves? The answer lies in Fourier series!") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Show the general Fourier series formula
        fourier_formula = MathTex(
            r"f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n \cos(n\omega x) + b_n \sin(n\omega x)",
            font_size=32
        )
        fourier_formula.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="A Fourier series represents any periodic function as an infinite sum of sine and cosine terms.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(fourier_formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Show coefficient formulas
        coeff_group = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"a_n = \frac{1}{T} \int f(x) \cos(n\omega x) dx", font_size=28),
            MathTex(r"b_n = \frac{1}{T} \int f(x) \sin(n\omega x) dx", font_size=28)
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        coeff_group.next_to(fourier_formula, DOWN, buff=0.4)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The coefficients a-n and b-n are calculated using these integral formulas, capturing how much of each frequency is present.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(coeff_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Fade out formulas to make room for visualization
        with self.voiceover(text="Now, let's see this in action with a classic example: the square wave.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(fourier_formula),
                FadeOut(coeff_group),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        # Create axes for plotting
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-PI, PI, PI/2],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 0.5],
            x_length=10,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False},
        )
        axes.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        # Add axis labels

        y_label = MathTex("f(x)", font_size=24).next_to(axes.y_axis, UP)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here are our axes. We're going to approximate a square wave.") as tracker:
            self.play(

                Write(x_label),
                Write(y_label),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        # Define the square wave (target function)

            return 1 if (x % (2*PI)) < PI else -1
        
        # Plot target square wave (dashed)
        square_graph = axes.plot(
            lambda x: 1 if (x % (2*PI) + 2*PI) % (2*PI) < PI else -1,
            x_range=[-PI, PI],

            stroke_width=2,
            discontinuities=[-PI, 0, PI]

        # Now show Fourier approximations with increasing terms
        # For a square wave: f(x) = (4/pi) * sum of sin((2k+1)x)/(2k+1) for k=0 to n
        
        def fourier_approx(x, n_terms):
            result = 0
            for k in range(n_terms):
                n = 2 * k + 1  # odd harmonics only
                result += (4 / PI) * (1 / n) * np.sin(n * x)
            return result
        
        # Start with 1 term

        )
        
        term_label_5 = MathTex(r"n=9: \text{more terms}", font_size=24, color=ORANGE)

            )

        )

        term_label_15.next_to(term_label_5, DOWN, buff=0.2)

        # Section 5: Spectral Decomposition

        with self.voiceover(text="An elegant consequence of the spectral theorem is the spectral decomposition.") as tracker:

These concepts are fundamental to applications like principal component analysis, vibration analysis, quantum mechanics, and stability studies.") as tracker:

messages.content: You are an expert mathematical animator and pedagogical engineer using Manim Community Edition and manim-voiceover with AOSSpeechService. Write executable, self-contained Python code that synchronizes mathematical animations with spoken educational explanations.

I'm learning optimization to upper-undergraduate students with calculus and linear algebra background.

Provide intuition before the equations, then compare convergence for several learning rates; end with a real-world intuition.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class GradientDescentScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title
        title = Text("Gradient Descent Optimization", font_size=48, color=BLUE)
        subtitle = Text("The Heart of Machine Learning", font_size=28, color=GRAY)
        subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Have you ever wondered how algorithms learn to predict, recognize patterns, or even make decisions? The secret often lies in the power of optimization.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="At the center of this magic is a technique called gradient descent. Get ready to explore how this simple yet mighty algorithm helps us optimize functions in machine learning.") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))
        
        # Setup the loss function graph
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 9, 2],
            x_length=10,
            y_length=6,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "numbers_to_exclude": [0]}
        )
        axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="x", y_label="Loss")
        
        # Parabolic loss function: f(x) = x^2
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, color=BLUE, x_range=[-3, 3])
        curve_label = MathTex(r"f(x) = x^2", color=BLUE).scale(0.8)
        curve_label.next_to(curve, UP, buff=0.2).shift(RIGHT * 2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine you are trying to minimize a loss function, like this parabola representing f of x equals x squared. Your goal is to find the bottom of this valley where the loss is smallest.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(axes), Write(axes_labels), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Create(curve), Write(curve_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        # Gradient Descent Formula
        formula = MathTex(r"x_{next} = x_{current} - \eta \cdot \nabla f(x)", color=YELLOW)
        formula.scale(1.2)
        formula.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The gradient descent formula tells us how to update our position. x next equals x current minus the learning rate eta times the gradient of f at x.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Start gradient descent animation
        start_x = 2.5
        learning_rate = 0.3
        current_x = start_x
        
        # Starting point
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(current_x, current_x**2), color=RED, radius=0.15)
        point_label = MathTex(r"x_0", color=RED).scale(0.8)
        point_label.next_to(point, UR, buff=0.2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's start at position x zero. We want to move downhill to reduce the loss.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(point_label), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Gradient descent iterations
        trajectory = VMobject(color=RED, stroke_width=2)
        trajectory_points = [point.get_center()]
        
        for i in range(6):
            # Calculate gradient (derivative of x^2 is 2x)
            gradient = 2 * current_x
            
            # Calculate next position
            next_x = current_x - learning_rate * gradient
            next_y = next_x ** 2
            
            # Draw gradient arrow at current position
            arrow_start = axes.c2p(current_x, current_x**2)
            arrow_end = axes.c2p(current_x, current_x**2 - gradient * 0.3)
            gradient_arrow = Arrow(arrow_start, arrow_end, color=GREEN, buff=0)
            
            # Create tangent line
            slope = gradient
            tangent_line = axes.plot(
                lambda x, x0=current_x, y0=current_x**2, m=slope: m * (x - x0) + y0,
                color=GREEN,
                x_range=[current_x - 0.5, current_x + 0.5]
            )
            
            with self.voiceover(text=f"At position x {i}, the gradient is {gradient:.1f}. The negative gradient points downhill, so we move in that direction.") as tracker:
                self.play(Create(tangent_line), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
                self.play(Create(gradient_arrow), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
                self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.4)
            
            # Move to next position
            new_point = Dot(axes.c2p(next_x, next_y), color=RED, radius=0.15)
            new_label = MathTex(f"x_{{{i+1}}}", color=RED).scale(0.8)
            new_label.next_to(new_point, UR if next_x > 0 else UL, buff=0.2)
            
            # Create trajectory line
            trajectory_points.append(axes.c2p(next_x, next_y))
            trajectory.set_points_as_corners(trajectory_points)
            
            with self.voiceover(text=f"Taking a step with learning rate {learning_rate}, we arrive at x {i+1}.") as tracker:
                self.play(
                    Transform(point, new_point),
                    Transform(point_label, new_label),
                    FadeOut(gradient_arrow),
                    FadeOut(tangent_line),
                    Create(trajectory.copy().set_stroke(opacity=0.5)),
                    run_time=tracker.duration
                )
            
            current_x = next_x
            
            if abs(current_x) < 0.1:
                break
        
        minimum = Dot(axes.c2p(0, 0), color=YELLOW, radius=0.15)
        minimum_label = MathTex(r"Minimum", color=YELLOW).scale(0.8)
        minimum_label.next_to(minimum, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="We continue this process until we converge to the minimum of the function. This is the essence of gradient descent.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(minimum), Write(minimum_label), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clear for next section
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let's explore how the learning rate affects convergence.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(formula), FadeOut(point), FadeOut(point_label),
                FadeOut(minimum), FadeOut(minimum_label), FadeOut(curve_label),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        # Learning Rate Comparison Section
        lr_title = Text("Learning Rate Impact", font_size=40, color=BLUE)
        lr_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The learning rate is a crucial hyperparameter. Let's compare different values.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(lr_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Small learning rate
        small_lr_text = MathTex(r"\eta = 0.1", color=GREEN).scale(0.9)
        small_lr_text.next_to(axes, LEFT, buff=0.5).shift(UP * 2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="A small learning rate like 0.1 means small, cautious steps.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(small_lr_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Animate small learning rate
        current_x = 2.5
        small_points = VGroup()
        for i in range(10):
            gradient = 2 * current_x
            next_x = current_x - 0.1 * gradient
            p = Dot(axes.c2p(current_x, current_x**2), color=GREEN, radius=0.08)
            small_points.add(p)
            current_x = next_x
        
        with self.voiceover(text="It takes many steps to converge, but you're less likely to overshoot.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(small_points, lag_ratio=0.2), run_time=2)
        
        # Large learning rate
        large_lr_text = MathTex(r"\eta = 0.9", color=RED).scale(0.9)
        large_lr_text.next_to(axes, RIGHT, buff=0.5).shift(UP * 2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="A large learning rate like 0.9 takes big steps.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(large_lr_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Animate large learning rate (oscillating)
        current_x = 2.5
        large_points = VGroup()
        for i in range(6):
            gradient = 2 * current_x
            next_x = current_x - 0.9 * gradient
            p = Dot(axes.c2p(current_x, current_x**2), color=RED, radius=0.08)
            large_points.add(p)
            current_x = next_x
        
        with self.voiceover(text="You might overshoot the minimum and oscillate, or even diverge entirely.") as tracker:

For an introductory to intermediate audience (calculus/linear algebra), animate gradient descent on a non-convex loss and explain why it can overshoot or stall.
