I'm learning RL and want to see Population-Based Training in action alongside Bayesian optimization. Visualize a population of agents with evolving hyperparameters, their performance histories, selection and mutation events, and a coordinating BO loop that prunes and shares knowledge across trials.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class PopulationBasedTrainingVisualization(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title
        title = Text("Population Based Training", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
        subtitle = Text("Evolution of AI Agents", font_size=24, color=GRAY)
        title_group = VGroup(title, subtitle).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        title_group.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine you are an artificial intelligence that needs to adapt and evolve through generations. How would you visualize this process of trial and error, where the best strategies survive and the weaker ones are eliminated?") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(Write(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This is where Population Based Training comes into play!") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(title_group))
        
        # Define generation parameters
        num_generations = 4
        pop_size = 6
        
        # Create initial population (Generation 0)
        with self.voiceover(text="Population Based Training maintains a population of agents that evolve concurrently, all striving to improve performance.") as tracker:
            gen_label = Text("Generation 0", font_size=28, color=YELLOW).to_edge(UP, buff=1)
            self.play(Write(gen_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        # Create agents as circles with different performance values
        def create_agent_row(generation, performances, y_pos):
            agents = VGroup()
            performance_bars = VGroup()
            
            for i, perf in enumerate(performances):
                # Agent circle
                circle = Circle(radius=0.35, color=WHITE)
                circle.set_fill(BLUE if perf > 0.6 else RED if perf < 0.4 else YELLOW, opacity=0.7)
                label = Text(f"A{i+1}", font_size=16).move_to(circle.get_center())
                agent = VGroup(circle, label)
                
                # Performance bar
                bar = Rectangle(height=0.15, width=perf * 1.5, color=GREEN if perf > 0.5 else RED)
                bar.set_fill(GREEN if perf > 0.5 else RED, opacity=0.8)
                perf_text = Text(f"{perf:.2f}", font_size=14).next_to(bar, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
                bar_group = VGroup(bar, perf_text)
                
                agent_group = VGroup(agent, bar_group).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
                agents.add(agent_group)
            
            agents.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.6, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            agents.shift(LEFT * 2)
            
            return agents
        
        # Initial performances
        initial_perfs = [0.45, 0.52, 0.38, 0.61, 0.29, 0.55]
        agents_g0 = create_agent_row(0, initial_perfs, 0)
        
        # Color legend
        legend = VGroup(
            Text("Performance:", font_size=18, color=WHITE),
            VGroup(Circle(radius=0.2, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.7), Text("High >0.5", font_size=14)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1),
            VGroup(Circle(radius=0.2, color=YELLOW).set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.7), Text("Medium", font_size=14)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1),
            VGroup(Circle(radius=0.2, color=RED).set_fill(RED, opacity=0.7), Text("Low <0.4", font_size=14)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        legend.to_corner(DR, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Each agent has different hyperparameters and performance levels. The circles represent agents, and the bars show their fitness scores.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(agents_g0), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(FadeIn(legend), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        # Show selection process
        with self.voiceover(text="In PBT, weaker performing agents are identified and eliminated based on their fitness scores.") as tracker:
            # Highlight weakest agents
            weak_indices = [2, 4]  # Low performers (0.38, 0.29)
            weak_highlights = VGroup()
            for idx in weak_indices:
                agent = agents_g0[idx][0][0]  # Get circle
                highlight = SurroundingRectangle(agent, color=RED, buff=0.1)
                weak_highlights.add(highlight)
            self.play(Create(weak_highlights), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="These weaker agents will be replaced by copies of stronger performers.") as tracker:
            # Highlight strong agents
            strong_indices = [3, 5]  # (0.61, 0.55)
            strong_highlights = VGroup()
            for idx in strong_indices:
                agent = agents_g0[idx][0][0]
                highlight = SurroundingRectangle(agent, color=GREEN, buff=0.1)
                strong_highlights.add(highlight)
            self.play(Create(strong_highlights), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(weak_highlights), FadeOut(strong_highlights))
        
        # Transition to next generation
        with self.voiceover(text="Now watch as the population evolves to the next generation.") as tracker:
            gen_label_new = Text("Generation 1", font_size=28, color=YELLOW).to_edge(UP, buff=1)
            
            # Replace low performers with copies of high performers but with exploration
            new_perfs = [0.45, 0.52, 0.63, 0.61, 0.53, 0.55] 
            agents_g1 = create_agent_row(1, new_perfs, 0)
            
            # Mark copied agents
            copied_markers = VGroup()
            for idx in [2, 4]:  # Previously weak indices now improved
                marker = Text("COPY+", font_size=12, color=GREEN).next_to(agents_g1[idx][0], LEFT, buff=0.1)
                copied_markers.add(marker)
            
            self.play(
                FadeOut(agents_g0),
                ReplacementTransform(gen_label, gen_label_new),
                FadeIn(agents_g1),
                FadeIn(copied_markers),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Notice how the previously weak agents have been replaced with improved versions, exploring the parameter space near successful strategies.") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration)
        
        # Show exploration arrow
        with self.voiceover(text="This is the exploration step, where copied agents are perturbed to discover potentially better configurations.") as tracker:
            explore_arrow = Arrow(UP * 0.5, DOWN * 0.5, color=ORANGE).next_to(copied_markers, LEFT, buff=0.2)
            explore_label = Text("Explore", font_size=14, color=ORANGE).next_to(explore_arrow, LEFT, buff=0.1)
            explore_group = VGroup(explore_arrow, explore_label)
            self.play(Create(explore_group), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(copied_markers), FadeOut(explore_group))
        
        # Show continued evolution
        with self.voiceover(text="This process continues across multiple generations, with the population progressively improving.") as tracker:
            gen_label_2 = Text("Generation 2", font_size=28, color=YELLOW).to_edge(UP, buff=1)
            perfs_2 = [0.68, 0.72, 0.63, 0.75, 0.71, 0.65]
            agents_g2 = create_agent_row(2, perfs_2, 0)
            
            gen_label_3 = Text("Generation 3", font_size=28, color=YELLOW).to_edge(UP, buff=1)
            perfs_3 = [0.82, 0.79, 0.85, 0.88, 0.81, 0.77]
            agents_g3 = create_agent_row(3, perfs_3, 0)
            
            # Quick succession of generations
            self.play(
                FadeOut(agents_g1),
                ReplacementTransform(gen_label_new, gen_label_2),
                FadeIn(agents_g2),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3
            )
            self.wait(0.3)
            self.play(
                FadeOut(agents_g2),
                ReplacementTransform(gen_label_2, gen_label_3),
                FadeIn(agents_g3),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4
            )
        
        # Final population state
        with self.voiceover(text="After several generations, the population converges towards high-performing solutions through this survival of the fittest approach.") as tracker:
            # Add final check marks
            success_marks = VGroup()
            for i in range(6):
                check = Text("✓", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(agents_g3[i], RIGHT, buff=0.3)
                success_marks.add(check)
            self.play(FadeIn(success_marks), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(gen_label_3), FadeOut(legend), FadeOut(agents_g3), FadeOut(success_marks))
        
        # Summary
        with self.voiceover(text="Population Based Training enables parallel optimization, where multiple agents explore different hyperparameter configurations simultaneously. The best strategies are exploited while continuing to explore the search space.") as tracker:
            summary_title = Text("Key Concepts", font_size=32, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP, buff=1)
            
            concepts = VGroup(
                Text("• Parallel training of multiple agents", font_size=20),
                Text("• Selection based on performance", font_size=20),
                Text("• Copying successful strategies", font_size=20),
                Text("• Exploration through perturbation", font_size=20),
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4, aligned_edge=LEFT)
```

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class ConditionalDistributionsAndBayesTheorem(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title
        title = Text("Conditional Distributions & Bayes' Theorem", font_size=36)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Welcome! Today we'll explore conditional distributions and Bayes' Theorem.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Opener - Detective Theme
        detective_text = Text("Imagine you're a detective solving a mystery.", font_size=28)
        detective_text.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine you're a detective solving a mystery.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(detective_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        clue_text = Text("You have clues linking suspects to a crime.", font_size=24)
        clue_text.next_to(detective_text, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="You have clues linking suspects to a crime, but how do you determine who is most likely the culprit?") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(clue_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        question_text = Text("How do you find the most likely culprit?", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        question_text.next_to(clue_text, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This is where conditional distributions and Bayes' Theorem come into play.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(question_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(detective_text), FadeOut(clue_text), FadeOut(question_text))
        
        # Conditional Probability Definition
        section_title = Text("Conditional Probability", font_size=32, color=BLUE)
        section_title.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's start with conditional probability.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(section_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Conditional probability formula
        cond_formula = MathTex(r"P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}", font_size=40)
        cond_formula.next_to(section_title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The probability of event A given that B has occurred is written as P of A given B, equals P of A intersect B over P of B.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(cond_formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Explanation of terms
        explanation = VGroup(
            Text("P(A|B) = Probability of A given B occurred", font_size=20),
            Text("P(A ∩ B) = Joint probability of A and B", font_size=20),
            Text("P(B) = Probability of event B", font_size=20)
        )
        explanation.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3)
        explanation.next_to(cond_formula, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="P of A given B is the probability of A given that B has occurred. P of A intersect B is the joint probability, and P of B is the probability of event B.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(explanation), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(section_title), FadeOut(cond_formula), FadeOut(explanation))
        
        # Joint Probability Forms
        joint_title = Text("Joint Probability Forms", font_size=32, color=BLUE)
        joint_title.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let's look at joint probability.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(joint_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        joint_formulas = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"P(A \cap B) = P(A|B) \cdot P(B)", font_size=36),
            MathTex(r"P(A \cap B) = P(B|A) \cdot P(A)", font_size=36)
        )
        joint_formulas.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        joint_formulas.next_to(joint_title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="We can express joint probability in two ways: P of A intersect B equals P of A given B times P of B, or equivalently, P of B given A times P of A.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(joint_formulas), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(joint_title), FadeOut(joint_formulas))
        
        # Bayes' Theorem
        bayes_title = Text("Bayes' Theorem", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
        bayes_title.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Now for the main result: Bayes' Theorem.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(bayes_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        bayes_formula = MathTex(r"P(A|B) = \frac{P(B|A) \cdot P(A)}{P(B)}", font_size=44)
        bayes_formula.next_to(bayes_title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Bayes' Theorem states that P of A given B equals P of B given A times P of A, divided by P of B.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(bayes_formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Bayes components explanation
        bayes_terms = VGroup(
            Text("P(A|B) = Posterior (what we want to find)", font_size=20),
            Text("P(B|A) = Likelihood (evidence given hypothesis)", font_size=20),
            Text("P(A) = Prior (initial belief)", font_size=20),
            Text("P(B) = Marginal (total probability of evidence)", font_size=20)
        )
        bayes_terms.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.25)
        bayes_terms.next_to(bayes_formula, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here, P of A given B is called the posterior, what we want to find. P of B given A is the likelihood, P of A is our prior belief, and P of B is the marginal probability of the evidence.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(bayes_terms), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(bayes_title), FadeOut(bayes_formula), FadeOut(bayes_terms))
        
        # Practical Example
        example_title = Text("Practical Example", font_size=32, color=ORANGE)
        example_title.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's apply this to a real scenario.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(example_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Example setup
        example_text = VGroup(
            Text("A disease affects 1% of the population.", font_size=22),
            Text("A test is 95% accurate (true positive and true negative).", font_size=22),
            Text("If you test positive, what's the probability you have the disease?", font_size=22)
        )
        example_text.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        example_text.next_to(example_title, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Suppose a disease affects one percent of the population. A test is ninety-five percent accurate. If you test positive, what's the probability you actually have the disease?") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(example_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Solution step by step
        solution = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"P(\text{Disease}) = 0.01", font_size=28),
            MathTex(r"P(+|\text{Disease}) = 0.95", font_size=28),
            MathTex(r"P(+|\text{No Disease}) = 0.05", font_size=28),
            MathTex(r"P(+) = 0.95 \cdot 0.01 + 0.05 \cdot 0.99 = 0.059", font_size=26)
        )
        solution.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        solution.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        solution.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The prior probability of disease is zero point zero one. The likelihood of a positive test given disease is zero point nine five. The false positive rate is zero point zero five. And the total probability of a positive test is about zero point zero five nine.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(example_text))
            self.play(FadeIn(solution), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Final calculation
        final_calc = MathTex(r"P(\text{Disease}|+) = \frac{0.95 \cdot 0.01}{0.059} \approx 0.161", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        final_calc.next_to(solution, RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Applying Bayes' Theorem, the probability of having the disease given a positive test is only about sixteen percent. This counterintuitive result shows why Bayes' Theorem is so powerful.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(final_calc), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Surrounding box for the answer
        answer_box = SurroundingRectangle(final_calc, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(answer_box))
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(example_title), FadeOut(solution), FadeOut(final_calc), FadeOut(answer_box))
        
        # Summary / Takeaways
        summary_title = Text("Key Takeaways", font_size=32, color=PURPLE)
        summary_title.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's summarize the key takeaways.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(summary_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        takeaways = VGroup(
            Text("• Conditional probability updates beliefs with new evidence", font_size=22),
            Text("• Bayes' Theorem relates P(A|B) to P(B|A)", font_size=22),
            Text("• Prior + Likelihood → Posterior", font_size=22),
            Text("• Essential for medical testing, AI, and decision-making", font_size=22)
        )
        takeaways.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.35)
        takeaways.next_to(summary_title, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Conditional probability lets us update beliefs with new evidence. Bayes' Theorem connects P of A given B to P of B given A. We combine prior beliefs with likelihood to get our posterior. And this is essential for medical testing, artificial intelligence, and decision-making.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(takeaways), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Final fade
        with self.voiceover(text="Thank you for watching. Now go solve some mysteries with Bayes' Theorem!") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(summary_title), FadeOut(takeaways), run_time=tracker.duration)
```

```python
            self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Welcome to the world of Mixtures of Experts!") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))
        
        # Setup the scene - Input tokens on the left
        with self.voiceover(text="In today's lecture, you'll uncover how attention mechanisms can be visualized and how they enhance the performance of models in artificial intelligence.") as tracker:
            # Create input tokens
            input_tokens = VGroup(*[
                RoundedRectangle(height=0.6, width=1.2, corner_radius=0.1, fill_color=BLUE_E, fill_opacity=0.8)
                for _ in range(4)
            ]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
            input_tokens.to_edge(LEFT, buff=1.5)
            
            token_labels = VGroup(*[
                Text(f"Token {i+1}", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
                for i in range(4)
            ])
            for label, token in zip(token_labels, input_tokens):
                label.move_to(token.get_center())
            
            input_group = VGroup(input_tokens, token_labels)
            
            input_title = Text("Input", font_size=24, color=GRAY).next_to(input_group, UP, buff=0.3)
            
            self.play(
                LaggedStart(*[Create(t) for t in input_tokens], lag_ratio=0.2),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6
            )
            self.play(Write(token_labels), Write(input_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        # Router / Gating Network
        with self.voiceover(text="First, let's understand the core components. The input tokens flow into a router, also called a gating network.") as tracker:
            router = Circle(radius=0.7, fill_color=YELLOW_E, fill_opacity=0.9, stroke_color=YELLOW_D, stroke_width=3)
            router.next_to(input_tokens, RIGHT, buff=2)
            router_label = Text("Router\n(Gating)", font_size=14, color=BLACK).move_to(router.get_center())
            
            router_group = VGroup(router, router_label)
            
            # Arrows from input to router
            input_to_router = VGroup(*[
                Arrow(token.get_right(), router.get_left(), buff=0.1, color=GRAY, stroke_width=2)
                for token in input_tokens
            ])
            
            self.play(Create(router), Write(router_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(a) for a in input_to_router], lag_ratio=0.1), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        # Experts
        with self.voiceover(text="This router decides which expert should process each token. We have multiple experts, each specializing in different aspects.") as tracker:
            experts = VGroup(*[
                RoundedRectangle(height=0.8, width=1.4, corner_radius=0.15, 
                                fill_color=color, fill_opacity=0.9, stroke_color=color, stroke_width=2)
                for color in [GREEN_E, RED_E, PURPLE_E, TEAL_E]
            ]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
            experts.to_edge(RIGHT, buff=1.5)
            
            expert_labels = VGroup(*[
                Text(f"Expert {i+1}", font_size=16, color=WHITE)
                for i in range(4)
            ])
            for label, expert in zip(expert_labels, experts):
                label.move_to(expert.get_center())
            
            experts_title = Text("Experts", font_size=24, color=GRAY).next_to(experts, UP, buff=0.3)
            
            self.play(
                LaggedStart(*[Create(e) for e in experts], lag_ratio=0.15),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5
            )
            self.play(Write(expert_labels), Write(experts_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        # Router to Experts connections (attention weights visualization)
        with self.voiceover(text="Watch as the router assigns attention weights to each expert. Thicker arrows mean higher attention scores.") as tracker:
            # Create dynamic arrows with varying thickness based on attention weights
            attention_weights = [
                [0.7, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1],  # Token 1 -> Expert 1
                [0.2, 0.6, 0.1, 0.1],  # Token 2 -> Expert 2
                [0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 0.2],  # Token 3 -> Expert 3
                [0.1, 0.1, 0.2, 0.6],  # Token 4 -> Expert 4
            ]
            
            router_to_experts = VGroup()
            weight_indicators = VGroup()
            
            for i, token in enumerate(input_tokens):
                for j, expert in enumerate(experts):
                    weight = attention_weights[i][j]
                    stroke = max(1, weight * 8)
                    alpha = 0.3 + weight * 0.7
                    
                    # Color based on weight intensity
                    if weight > 0.5:
                        color = YELLOW
                    elif weight > 0.3:
                        color = ORANGE
                    else:
                        color = GRAY
                    
                    # Use Arrow instead of CurvedArrow with adjusted start/end points
                    start_point = router.get_right() + RIGHT * 0.1
                    end_point = expert.get_left() + LEFT * 0.1
                    # Add some vertical offset based on indices
                    y_offset = (i - j) * 0.15
                    start_point += UP * y_offset * 0.5
                    end_point += UP * y_offset * 0.5
                    
                    arrow = Arrow(
                        start_point, 
                        end_point,
                        color=color,
                        stroke_width=stroke,
                        max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.1,
                        max_stroke_width_to_length_ratio=10
                    )
                    arrow.set_opacity(alpha)
                    router_to_experts.add(arrow)
                    
                    # Weight label for high weights
                    if weight > 0.3:
                        mid_point = (start_point + end_point) / 2 + UP * 0.1
                        weight_label = Text(f"{weight:.1f}", font_size=12, color=YELLOW).move_to(mid_point)
                        weight_indicators.add(weight_label)
            
            self.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(a) for a in router_to_experts], lag_ratio=0.05), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(FadeIn(weight_indicators), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        # Attention mechanism explanation
        with self.voiceover(text="These attention weights determine how much each expert contributes to processing a specific token. Higher weights mean that expert has more relevant knowledge.") as tracker:
            # Highlight the strongest connections
            highlights = VGroup()
            for i in range(4):
                highlight = SurroundingRectangle(experts[i], color=YELLOW, buff=0.1, stroke_width=3)
                highlights.add(highlight)
            
            self.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(h) for h in highlights], lag_ratio=0.2), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.play(FadeOut(highlights))
        
        # Output combination
        with self.voiceover(text="After processing, the outputs from selected experts are combined, weighted by their attention scores, to produce the final result.") as tracker:
            output_box = RoundedRectangle(height=2.5, width=1.5, corner_radius=0.15, 
                                         fill_color=BLUE_D, fill_opacity=0.9)
            output_box.next_to(experts, RIGHT, buff=2)
            output_label = Text("Output", font_size=20, color=WHITE).move_to(output_box.get_center())
            
            # Arrows from experts to output
            expert_to_output = VGroup(*[
                Arrow(expert.get_right(), output_box.get_left(), buff=0.1, color=BLUE_B, stroke_width=3)
                for expert in experts
            ])
            
            self.play(Create(output_box), Write(output_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(a) for a in expert_to_output], lag_ratio=0.1), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        # Benefits section - two columns
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let's look at the key benefits of using Mixtures of Experts with attention.") as tracker:
            # Fade out the diagram slightly
            diagram = VGroup(input_group, router_group, experts, expert_labels, 
                           router_to_experts, weight_indicators, expert_to_output,
                           output_box, input_title, experts_title, output_label,
                           input_to_router)
            
            self.play(diagram.animate.set_opacity(0.2), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            
            # Create benefits title
            benefits_title = Text("Key Benefits", font_size=32, color=BLUE_D)
            benefits_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            # Two column layout
            left_col = VGroup(
                Text("• Specialized Knowledge", font_size=20, color=WHITE),
                Text("• Efficient Computation", font_size=20, color=WHITE),
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            
            right_col = VGroup(
                Text("• Scalable Architecture", font_size=20, color=WHITE),
                Text("• Dynamic Routing", font_size=20, color=WHITE),
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            
            benefits_content = VGroup(left_col, right_col).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.5)
            benefits_content.next_to(benefits_title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            
            self.play(Write(benefits_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(LaggedStart(*[Write(item) for item in left_col], lag_ratio=0.3), 
                     LaggedStart(*[Write(item) for item in right_col], lag_ratio=0.3),
                     run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        # Explain each benefit
        with self.voiceover(text="First, each expert can specialize in different knowledge domains, making the model more accurate.") as tracker:
            self.play(left_col[0].animate.scale(1.1).set_color(YELLOW), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(left_col[0].animate.scale(1/1.1).set_color(WHITE), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Second, we only activate a subset of experts per input, making computation efficient.") as tracker:
            self.play(left_col[1].animate.scale(1.1).set_color(YELLOW), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(left_col[1].animate.scale(1/1.1).set_color(WHITE), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Third, the architecture scales well - we can add more experts without significantly increasing computation per input.") as tracker:
            self.play(right_col[0].animate.scale(1.1).set_color(YELLOW), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(right_col[0].animate.scale(1/1.1).set_color(WHITE), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="And finally, dynamic routing through attention allows the model to adapt to different inputs on the fly.") as tracker:
            self.play(right_col[1].animate.scale(1.1).set_color(YELLOW), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(right_col[1].animate.scale(1/1.1).set_color(WHITE), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        # Summary
        with self.voiceover(text="To summarize: Mixtures of Experts uses attention mechanisms to dynamically route inputs to specialized experts, combining efficiency with powerful performance.") as tracker:
            summary_box = Rectangle(height=1.2, width=10, fill_color=BLUE_E, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_color=BLUE_D)
            summary_box.to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.5)
            summary_text = Text("MoE + Attention = Efficiency + Specialization", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
            summary_text.move_to(summary_box.get_center())
            
            self.play(Create(summary_box), Write(summary_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Thank you for watching! You now understand how Mixtures of Experts with attention work.") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(*self.mobjects))
        
        # Final screen
        final_text = Text("Mixtures of Experts\nAttention Visualization", font_size=36, color=BLUE_D)
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(final_text))
```

messages.content: You are an expert mathematical animator and pedagogical engineer using Manim Community Edition and manim-voiceover with AOSSpeechService. Write executable, self-contained Python code that synchronizes mathematical animations with spoken educational explanations.

I'm teaching an undergrad ML course and want a vivid visualization of Softplus and its variants. Show how the curve changes with parameters like beta and offset, compare with ReLU, and illustrate gradient flow during a simple backprop step on a tiny network.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService
import numpy as np


class ComparisonScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title and Introduction
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine you're building a neural network and have to choose an activation function. You might wonder which one will help your model learn better. Today, we will dive into the world of Softplus variants and ReLU, comparing their strengths and weaknesses. Why does it matter? Let's find out!") as tracker:
            title = Text("Softplus Variants and ReLU Comparison", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            subtitle = Text("Activation Functions in Neural Networks", font_size=24, color=GRAY)
            subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN)
            
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(Write(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.wait(0.5)
            self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))
        
        # Section 1: Softplus Function
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's start with the Softplus function. It's defined as the natural logarithm of one plus e to the power of x.") as tracker:
            # Softplus formula
            softplus_formula = MathTex(r"f(x) = \ln(1 + e^x)", font_size=40, color=BLUE)
            softplus_label = Text("Softplus Function", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
            softplus_label.next_to(softplus_formula, UP, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(softplus_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(softplus_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.wait(0.5)
            self.play(FadeOut(softplus_label), FadeOut(softplus_formula))
        
        # Softplus visualization
        with self.voiceover(text="Visually, Softplus is a smooth curve that approaches zero for very negative inputs and grows linearly for positive inputs. It's differentiable everywhere, which is great for gradient-based learning.") as tracker:
            axes1 = Axes(
                x_range=[-5, 5, 1],
                y_range=[-0.5, 5, 1],
                x_length=8,
                y_length=5,
                axis_config={"include_tip": True}
            )
            axes1_labels = axes1.get_axis_labels(x_label="x", y_label="f(x)")
            
            def softplus_func(x):
                return np.log(1 + np.exp(x))
            
            softplus_graph = axes1.plot(softplus_func, x_range=[-5, 5], color=BLUE, stroke_width=3)
            softplus_name = Text("Softplus", font_size=20, color=BLUE).next_to(axes1, UP)
            
            self.play(Create(axes1), Write(axes1_labels), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Create(softplus_graph), Write(softplus_name), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.wait(0.5)
            self.play(FadeOut(axes1), FadeOut(axes1_labels), FadeOut(softplus_graph), FadeOut(softplus_name))
        
        # Section 2: ReLU Function
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let's look at ReLU, which stands for Rectified Linear Unit. It's defined as the maximum of zero and x.") as tracker:
            # ReLU formula
            relu_formula = MathTex(r"f(x) = \max(0, x)", font_size=40, color=RED)
            relu_label = Text("ReLU Function", font_size=28, color=RED)
            relu_label.next_to(relu_formula, UP, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(relu_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(relu_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.wait(0.5)
            self.play(FadeOut(relu_label), FadeOut(relu_formula))
        
        # ReLU visualization
        with self.voiceover(text="ReLU is a piecewise linear function. For any negative input, it outputs zero. For positive inputs, it acts as an identity function. Notice the sharp corner at zero.") as tracker:
            axes2 = Axes(
                x_range=[-5, 5, 1],
                y_range=[-0.5, 5, 1],
                x_length=8,
                y_length=5,
                axis_config={"include_tip": True}
            )
            axes2_labels = axes2.get_axis_labels(x_label="x", y_label="f(x)")
            
            def relu_func(x):
                return max(0, x)
            
            relu_graph = axes2.plot(relu_func, x_range=[-5, 5], color=RED, stroke_width=3)
            relu_name = Text("ReLU", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(axes2, UP)
            
            self.play(Create(axes2), Write(axes2_labels), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Create(relu_graph), Write(relu_name), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.wait(0.5)
            self.play(FadeOut(axes2), FadeOut(axes2_labels), FadeOut(relu_graph), FadeOut(relu_name))
        
        # Section 3: Side-by-side comparison
        with self.voiceover(text="When we overlay both functions, you can see how Softplus smoothly approximates ReLU. Softplus is always slightly above ReLU, but they converge for large positive values.") as tracker:
            axes3 = Axes(
                x_range=[-5, 5, 1],
                y_range=[-0.5, 5, 1],
                x_length=10,
                y_length=6,
                axis_config={"include_tip": True}
            )
            axes3_labels = axes3.get_axis_labels(x_label="x", y_label="f(x)")
            
            softplus_graph2 = axes3.plot(softplus_func, x_range=[-5, 5], color=BLUE, stroke_width=3)
            relu_graph2 = axes3.plot(relu_func, x_range=[-5, 5], color=RED, stroke_width=3)
            
            softplus_legend = MathTex(r"\ln(1+e^x)", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
            relu_legend = MathTex(r"\max(0,x)", font_size=20, color=RED)
            
            legend_group = VGroup(softplus_legend, relu_legend)
            legend_group.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            legend_group.to_corner(UR, buff=0.5)
            
            # Add dots to indicate the corner point
            corner_dot = Dot(axes3.c2p(0, 0), color=RED, radius=0.08)
            
            self.play(Create(axes3), Write(axes3_labels), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Create(softplus_graph2), Create(relu_graph2), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(Write(legend_group), FadeIn(corner_dot), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.wait(0.5)
            self.play(FadeOut(axes3), FadeOut(axes3_labels), FadeOut(softplus_graph2), 
                     FadeOut(relu_graph2), FadeOut(legend_group), FadeOut(corner_dot))
        
        # Section 4: Derivatives
        with self.voiceover(text="The derivative of Softplus is the sigmoid function: one over one plus e to the negative x. This gives smooth gradients everywhere.") as tracker:
            deriv_softplus = MathTex(r"f'(x) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-x}} = \sigma(x)", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            deriv_label1 = Text("Softplus Derivative (Sigmoid)", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
            deriv_label1.next_to(deriv_softplus, UP, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(deriv_label1), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(deriv_softplus), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.wait(0.3)
            self.play(FadeOut(deriv_label1), FadeOut(deriv_softplus))
        
        with self.voiceover(text="ReLU's derivative is simple: zero for negative inputs and one for positive inputs. However, it's undefined at exactly zero, which can cause issues during training.") as tracker:
            deriv_relu = MathTex(r"f'(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & x < 0 \\ 1 & x > 0 \\ \text{undefined} & x = 0 \end{cases}", font_size=36, color=RED)
            deriv_label2 = Text("ReLU Derivative", font_size=24, color=RED)
            deriv_label2.next_to(deriv_relu, UP, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(deriv_label2), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(deriv_relu), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.wait(0.3)
            self.play(FadeOut(deriv_label2), FadeOut(deriv_relu))
        
        # Section 5: Pros and Cons - Two columns layout
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's compare their advantages and disadvantages. Softplus is smooth and differentiable everywhere, but it's computationally expensive and can have vanishing gradients for negative inputs.") as tracker:
            # Softplus pros/cons
            softplus_title = Text("Softplus", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
            sp_pros = VGroup(
                Text("✓ Smooth everywhere", font_size=20, color=GREEN),
                Text("✓ Differentiable everywhere", font_size=20, color=GREEN),
                Text("✓ No sharp corners", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
            )
            sp_cons = VGroup(
                Text("✗ Computationally expensive", font_size=20, color=RED_D),
                Text("✗ Vanishing gradients (x << 0)", font_size=20, color=RED_D),
                Text("✗ Outputs never exactly zero", font_size=20, color=RED_D)
            )
            
            sp_pros.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.2)
            sp_cons.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.2)
            
            sp_column = VGroup(softplus_title, sp_pros, sp_cons)
            sp_column.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
            sp_pros.align_to(softplus_title, LEFT)
            sp_cons.align_to(softplus_title, LEFT)
            
            self.play(Write(softplus_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Write(sp_pros), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Write(sp_cons), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.wait(0.3)
            self.play(FadeOut(sp_column))
        
        with self.voiceover(text="ReLU is computationally efficient and helps with sparse activation, but it has the dying ReLU problem where neurons can get stuck outputting zero.") as tracker:
            # ReLU pros/cons
            relu_title = Text("ReLU", font_size=28, color=RED)
            relu_pros = VGroup(
                Text("✓ Computationally efficient", font_size=20, color=GREEN),
                Text("✓ Sparse activation", font_size=20, color=GREEN),
                Text("✓ No vanishing gradient (x > 0)", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
            )
            relu_cons = VGroup(
                Text("✗ Dying ReLU problem", font_size=20, color=RED_D),
                Text("✗ Not differentiable at zero", font_size=20, color=RED_D),
                Text("✗ No negative outputs", font_size=20, color=RED_D)
            )
            
            relu_pros.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.2)
            relu_cons.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.2)
            
            relu_column = VGroup(relu_title, relu_pros, relu_cons)
            relu_column.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
            relu_pros.align_to(relu_title, LEFT)
            relu_cons.align_to(relu_title, LEFT)
            
            self.play(Write(relu_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Write(relu_pros), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Write(relu_cons), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.wait(0.3)
            self.play(FadeOut(relu_column))
        
        # Section 6: Variants
```

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService


class RLBayesianOptimization(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )

        # Title and opener visual
        title = Text("RL Optimization With Bayesian Methods", font_size=36)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)

        opener = Text("Navigating a maze, improving at every turn.", font_size=22)
        opener.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.6)

        with self.voiceover(text="""Imagine you're navigating a maze, trying to find the quickest and most efficient way out. What if you could learn from your past experiences in a way that improves your decisions at each turn? This is the essence of reinforcement learning paired with the powerful principles of Bayesian methods, guiding you to optimize your strategies!""") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(title), FadeIn(opener), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # Objectives
        obj_title = Text("Objectives", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        obj_title.next_to(title, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.6)
        objs = VGroup(
            Text("• Understand Bayesian methods in RL.", font_size=20),
            Text("• Apply Bayes' theorem to update beliefs.", font_size=20),
            Text("• Explore expected value & variance.", font_size=20),
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.25)
        objs.next_to(obj_title, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.25)

        with self.voiceover(text="""By the end of this lecture, you will understand the role of Bayesian methods in reinforcement learning optimization, learn how to apply Bayes' theorem to update beliefs in RL settings, and explore expected value and variance in this context.""") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(opener), FadeIn(obj_title), FadeIn(objs), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # Assumptions
        assump_title = Text("Assumptions", font_size=28, color=YELLOW)
        assump_title.next_to(title, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.6)
        assump = VGroup(
            Text("• You know basic RL concepts.", font_size=20),
            Text("• You understand probability & Bayes' theorem.", font_size=20),
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.25)
        assump.next_to(assump_title, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.25)

        with self.voiceover(text="""We assume you are familiar with basic reinforcement learning concepts and the basics of probability and Bayes' theorem.""") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(obj_title), FadeOut(objs), FadeIn(assump_title), FadeIn(assump), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # Bayes' Theorem
        bayes_label = Text("Bayes' Theorem", font_size=28, color=GREEN)
        bayes_label.next_to(title, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.6)
        bayes = MathTex(r"P(H|E) = \frac{P(E|H)\,P(H)}{P(E)}", font_size=28)
        bayes.next_to(bayes_label, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3)

        with self.voiceover(text="""At the heart of Bayesian optimization lies Bayes' theorem. It tells us how to update our belief about a hypothesis H after observing evidence E.""") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(assump_title), FadeOut(assump), FadeIn(bayes_label), Write(bayes), run_time=tracker.duration)

        explanation = Text("Posterior = (Likelihood × Prior) / Evidence", font_size=20)
        explanation.next_to(bayes, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3)

        with self.voiceover(text="""The posterior probability equals the likelihood times the prior, divided by the evidence.""") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(explanation), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # Expected Value
        ev_label = Text("Expected Value", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        ev_label.next_to(title, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.6)
        ev = MathTex(r"E(X) = \sum_{x} x \cdot P(x)", font_size=28)
        ev.next_to(ev_label, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3)

        with self.voiceover(text="""In RL optimization, we often care about expected rewards. The expected value of a random variable X is the sum of each outcome multiplied by its probability.""") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(bayes_label), FadeOut(bayes), FadeOut(explanation), FadeIn(ev_label), Write(ev), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # Variance
        var_label = Text("Variance", font_size=28, color=RED)
        var_label.next_to(ev, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.5)
        var = MathTex(r"\mathrm{Var}(X) = E(X^2) - \big(E(X)\big)^2", font_size=28)
        var.next_to(var_label, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3)

        with self.voiceover(text="""Variance measures the spread of possible rewards around the mean. It is the expected value of the squared variable minus the square of the expected value.""") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(var_label), Write(var), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # RL Diagram
        state = Square(side_length=1).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5).shift(LEFT * 3.5)
        state_txt = Text("State", font_size=16).move_to(state)
        action = Square(side_length=1).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.5)
        action_txt = Text("Action", font_size=16).move_to(action)
        reward = Circle(radius=0.6).set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.5).shift(RIGHT * 3.5)
        reward_txt = Text("Reward", font_size=16).move_to(reward)

        a1 = Arrow(state.get_right(), action.get_left(), buff=0.1)
        a2 = Arrow(action.get_right(), reward.get_left(), buff=0.1)
        a3 = Arrow(reward.get_bottom() + DOWN * 0.4, state.get_bottom() + DOWN * 0.4, buff=0.1)
        a3_txt = Text("Bayesian Update", font_size=18, color=ORANGE).next_to(a3, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        diagram = VGroup(state, state_txt, action, action_txt, reward, reward_txt, a1, a2, a3, a3_txt)

        with self.voiceover(text="""In reinforcement learning, an agent observes a state, takes an action, and receives a reward. Bayesian methods let us update our belief about the best policy after each reward.""") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(ev_label), FadeOut(ev), FadeOut(var_label), FadeOut(var),
                Create(state), FadeIn(state_txt),
                Create(action), FadeIn(action_txt),
                Create(reward), FadeIn(reward_txt),
                Create(a1), Create(a2), Create(a3), FadeIn(a3_txt),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )

        # Learning Outcomes
        lo_title = Text("Learning Outcomes", font_size=28, color=PURPLE)
        lo_title.next_to(title, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.6)
        los = VGroup(
            Text("• Refine RL decisions with Bayesian methods.", font_size=20),
            Text("• Explore practical applications and examples.", font_size=20),
            Text("• Implement basic Bayesian updates in RL.", font_size=20),
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.25)
        los.next_to(lo_title, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.25)

        with self.voiceover(text="""You will see how Bayesian methods can refine decision-making in reinforcement learning, explore practical applications, and be able to implement basic Bayesian updates in RL scenarios.""") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(diagram), FadeIn(lo_title), FadeIn(los), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # Closing
        closing = Text("Let's optimize with Bayes!", font_size=28, color=TEAL)
        closing.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=1.0)

            self.play(FadeOut(lo_title), FadeOut(los), FadeIn(closing), run_time=tracker.duration)
```

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class ListwiseLossScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title
        title = Text("Listwise Loss", font_size=48, color=PURPLE)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let's explore Listwise Loss, which considers the entire ranking at once.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Context explanation
        context = Text("Ranking: Order the entire list optimally", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        context.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Unlike pairwise approaches, listwise losses optimize the entire ranked list simultaneously.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(context), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(context))
        
        # Example: Multiple documents to rank
        docs_title = Text("Query: Best Machine Learning Books", font_size=28, color=YELLOW)
        docs_title.move_to(UP * 1.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Consider ranking books for a query about machine learning.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(docs_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # List of documents
        doc_boxes = VGroup()
        doc_labels = ["Book A", "Book B", "Book C", "Book D"]
        colors = [GREEN, GREEN, YELLOW, RED]
        relevances = ["High", "High", "Medium", "Low"]
        
        for i, (label, color, rel) in enumerate(zip(doc_labels, colors, relevances)):
            box = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=0.6, color=color, fill_opacity=0.3)
            text = Text(label, font_size=20)
            rel_text = Text(f"({rel})", font_size=16, color=color)
            group = VGroup(box, text, rel_text)
            group.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
            group.move_to(LEFT * 3 + UP * (0.8 - i * 1))
            doc_boxes.add(group)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="We have four books with different relevance levels: two highly relevant, one medium, and one low.") as tracker:
            self.play(*[FadeIn(box) for box in doc_boxes], run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Show the entire list matters
        list_arrow = Arrow(UP * 2, DOWN * 3, color=BLUE, buff=0)
        list_arrow.move_to(RIGHT * 1)
        list_text = Text("Optimize\nentire list", font_size=22, color=BLUE)
        list_text.next_to(list_arrow, RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Listwise loss considers all items together to find the optimal ranking.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(list_arrow), FadeIn(list_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Clear example
        self.play(
            FadeOut(docs_title), 
            FadeOut(doc_boxes), 
            FadeOut(list_arrow), 
            FadeOut(list_text)
        )
        
        # Formula introduction
        formula_title = Text("Cross-Entropy Listwise Loss", font_size=36, color=PURPLE_B)
        formula_title.move_to(UP * 2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="A common listwise loss uses cross-entropy over the probability distribution.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(formula_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # The formula
        formula = MathTex(
            r"L_{\text{Listwise}} = -\sum_{i=1}^{N} y_i \cdot \log(P(y_i))",
            font_size=36
        )
        formula.move_to(UP * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here is the formula. It equals negative sum over all items of true probability times log of predicted probability.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Break down components
        y_term = MathTex(r"y_i", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
        y_term.move_to(LEFT * 3 + DOWN * 1)
        y_explain = Text("True relevance\ndistribution", font_size=20, color=GREEN)
        y_explain.next_to(y_term, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Y i represents the true relevance distribution, often one-hot encoded.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(y_term), FadeIn(y_explain), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.2)
        
        p_term = MathTex(r"P(y_i)", font_size=32, color=BLUE)
        p_term.move_to(RIGHT * 3 + DOWN * 1)
        p_explain = Text("Predicted\nprobability", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        p_explain.next_to(p_term, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="P of Y i is the predicted probability from a softmax over model scores.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(p_term), FadeIn(p_explain), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Show softmax
        self.play(FadeOut(y_term), FadeOut(y_explain), FadeOut(p_term), FadeOut(p_explain))
        
        softmax_formula = MathTex(
            r"P(y_i) = \frac{\exp(f(x_i))}{\sum_{j=1}^{N} \exp(f(x_j))}",
            font_size=32
        )
        softmax_formula.move_to(DOWN * 1.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This probability comes from applying softmax to the model's scores.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(softmax_formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Key insight
        self.play(FadeOut(softmax_formula))
        
        insight = Text("Optimizes entire ranking, not just pairs", font_size=30, color=ORANGE)
        insight.next_to(formula, DOWN, buff=1.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The key advantage is optimizing the entire ranking structure, capturing dependencies between all items.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(insight), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Comparison section
        self.play(FadeOut(formula), FadeOut(formula_title), FadeOut(insight))
        
        comp_title = Text("Pairwise vs Listwise", font_size=40, color=BLUE)
        comp_title.move_to(UP * 2.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's compare these approaches.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(comp_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Two columns
        left_col = VGroup()
        right_col = VGroup()
        
        pw_title = Text("Pairwise", font_size=28, color=GREEN)
        pw_title.move_to(LEFT * 3.5 + UP * 1.5)
        left_col.add(pw_title)
        
        pw_points = [
            "• Compares pairs",
            "• Local decisions",
            "• Simpler to train",
            "• May miss global structure"
        ]
        
        for i, point in enumerate(pw_points):
            txt = Text(point, font_size=22)
            txt.move_to(LEFT * 3.5 + UP * (0.5 - i * 0.6))
            left_col.add(txt)
        
        lw_title = Text("Listwise", font_size=28, color=PURPLE)
        lw_title.move_to(RIGHT * 3.5 + UP * 1.5)
        right_col.add(lw_title)
        
        lw_points = [
            "• Considers full list",
            "• Global optimization", 
            "• Better ranking quality",
            "• More complex"
        ]
        
        for i, point in enumerate(lw_points):
            txt = Text(point, font_size=22)
            txt.move_to(RIGHT * 3.5 + UP * (0.5 - i * 0.6))
            right_col.add(txt)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Pairwise compares individual pairs with local decisions, making it simpler but potentially missing global patterns. Listwise considers the full list for global optimization, yielding better ranking quality but with more complexity.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeIn(left_col),
                FadeIn(right_col),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # When to use each
        self.play(FadeOut(left_col), FadeOut(right_col), FadeOut(comp_title))
        
        when_title = Text("When to Use Each?", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)
        when_title.move_to(UP * 2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="When should you use each approach?") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(when_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        use_pw = Text("Use Pairwise: Large datasets, partial labels", font_size=26, color=GREEN)
        use_pw.move_to(UP * 0.5)
        
        use_lw = Text("Use Listwise: High-quality ranking, smaller lists", font_size=26, color=PURPLE)
        use_lw.move_to(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Use pairwise for large datasets with partial labels. Use listwise when ranking quality is critical and lists are manageable.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(use_pw), FadeIn(use_lw), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Final summary
        self.play(FadeOut(when_title), FadeOut(use_pw), FadeOut(use_lw))
        
        summary = Text("Summary", font_size=40, color=BLUE)
        summary.move_to(UP * 2)
        
        sum1 = Text("• Pairwise: Compare items in pairs", font_size=28)
        sum1.move_to(UP * 0.5)
        
        sum2 = Text("• Listwise: Optimize entire ranking", font_size=28)
        sum2.move_to(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        sum3 = Text("• Choose based on data size & quality needs", font_size=28)
        sum3.move_to(DOWN * 1.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="To summarize: pairwise compares items in pairs, listwise optimizes the entire ranking. Choose based on your data size and quality requirements.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeIn(summary),
                FadeIn(sum1),
                FadeIn(sum2),
                FadeIn(sum3),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Final fade
        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(summary), FadeOut(sum1), FadeOut(sum2), FadeOut(sum3))
```

```python
        with self.voiceover(text="TPUs are Google's creation, optimized for neural network operations.") as tracker:
            neural_icon = VGroup()

        with self.voiceover(text="Then we have FPGAs, Field Programmable Gate Arrays, which can be reconfigured for different tasks.") as tracker:
            fpga_box = RoundedRectangle(width=2.5, height=1.2, corner_radius=0.2, color=PURPLE, fill_opacity=0.3)

        with self.voiceover(text="ASICs provide the highest performance and efficiency for their dedicated tasks.") as tracker:
            # Simpler chip icon without problematic numpy comparisons

            self.play(FadeIn(chip_icon), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Applications
        with self.voiceover(text="Now, let's see where hardware acceleration makes a real impact.") as tracker:
            self.play(

        with self.voiceover(text="Hardware acceleration powers many applications we use daily.") as tracker:

            self.play(Create(gaming_icon), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="In artificial intelligence, TPUs and GPUs train complex neural networks.") as tracker:
            ai_icon = VGroup()
            brain = Circle(radius=0.5, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.3)

            ai_label.next_to(brain, DOWN, buff=0.2)
            ai_icon.add(ai_label)

            self.play(Create(ai_icon), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="In cryptocurrency mining, ASICs perform billions of hash calculations per second.") as tracker:
            crypto_icon = VGroup()

            crypto_label = Text("Cryptocurrency", font_size=16)
            crypto_label.next_to(coin, DOWN, buff=0.2)
            crypto_icon.add(crypto_label)
            crypto_icon.next_to(ai_icon, RIGHT, buff=1.5)
            
            self.play(Create(crypto_icon), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="And in scientific computing, accelerators speed up simulations and data analysis.") as tracker:
            science_icon = VGroup()
            flask = VGroup()
            base = Polygon(LEFT * 0.3, RIGHT * 0.3, DOWN * 0.1, color=TEAL)
            neck = Rectangle(width=0.15, height=0.4, color=TEAL, fill_opacity=0.3)
            neck.next_to(base, UP, buff=0)
            flask.add(base, neck)
            bubble1 = Circle(radius=0.08, color=TEAL, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to(base.get_center() + LEFT * 0.1)
            bubble2 = Circle(radius=0.06, color=TEAL, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to(base.get_center() + RIGHT * 0.1)
            flask.add(bubble1, bubble2)
            science_icon.add(flask)
            science_label = Text("Scientific Computing", font_size=16)
            science_label.next_to(flask, DOWN, buff=0.2)
            science_icon.add(science_label)
            science_icon.next_to(crypto_icon, RIGHT, buff=1.5)
            
            self.play(Create(science_icon), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Summary
        with self.voiceover(text="To summarize what we've learned today.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(gaming_icon), FadeOut(ai_icon), FadeOut(crypto_icon), FadeOut(science_icon),
                FadeOut(apps_title),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Hardware acceleration uses specialized processors to speed up specific tasks.") as tracker:
            summary_title = Text("Key Takeaways", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
            summary_title.next_to(title_group, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            self.play(Write(summary_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="GPUs, TPUs, FPGAs, and ASICs each serve unique purposes in modern computing.") as tracker:
            takeaway1 = Text("• GPUs for graphics and parallel computing", font_size=20)
            takeaway2 = Text("• TPUs for AI and neural networks", font_size=20)
            takeaway3 = Text("• FPGAs for flexible, reconfigurable tasks", font_size=20)
            takeaway4 = Text("• ASICs for maximum performance on specific tasks", font_size=20)
            
            takeaways = VGroup(takeaway1, takeaway2, takeaway3, takeaway4)

            self.play(Write(takeaway1), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.25)

        with self.voiceover(text="From gaming to AI to scientific research, hardware accelerators are the engines behind modern high-performance computing.") as tracker:
```

messages.content: You are an expert mathematical animator and pedagogical engineer using Manim Community Edition and manim-voiceover with AOSSpeechService. Write executable, self-contained Python code that synchronizes mathematical animations with spoken educational explanations.

I'm teaching data pipelines and want to visualize how pinned memory speeds data transfer to the device. Include prefetching, DMA transfers, memory pools, and a live throughput/idle-time chart with a hypothetical dataset.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class DataPipelineScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title introduction
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine you're managing an assembly line where materials flow seamlessly from one process to another. Each step needs to be quick and efficient, especially when you're dealing with large datasets.") as tracker:
            title = Text("Data Pipelines & Pinned Memory", font_size=40)
            subtitle = Text("Optimizing Data Flow", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
            subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.3)
            title_group = VGroup(title, subtitle)
            title_group.center()
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Clear title for main content
        with self.voiceover(text="This is the magic of data pipelines, especially when optimized with pinned memory. Let's dive in and see how it all works.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(title_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # SECTION 1: Assembly Line Analogy
        with self.voiceover(text="First, let's visualize a data pipeline as an assembly line. Data enters at one end, gets processed through multiple stages, and exits as useful information.") as tracker:
            # Create assembly line stages
            stages = VGroup()
            stage_names = ["Ingest", "Clean", "Transform", "Analyze", "Store"]
            colors = [GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, BLUE, PURPLE]
            
            for i, (name, color) in enumerate(zip(stage_names, colors)):
                box = RoundedRectangle(height=1.2, width=1.8, corner_radius=0.2, color=color, fill_opacity=0.2)
                label = Text(name, font_size=18, color=color)
                label.move_to(box.get_center())
                stage = VGroup(box, label)
                if i > 0:
                    stage.next_to(stages[-1], RIGHT, buff=0.8)
                stages.add(stage)
            
            stages.center().shift(UP * 0.5)
            
            # Arrows between stages
            arrows = VGroup()
            for i in range(len(stages) - 1):
                arrow = Arrow(stages[i].get_right(), stages[i+1].get_left(), buff=0.1, color=WHITE)
                arrows.add(arrow)
            
            self.play(*[FadeIn(s) for s in stages], run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(*[GrowArrow(a) for a in arrows], run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        # Data flow animation
        with self.voiceover(text="Watch how data packets move through each stage. Each stage performs a specific transformation on the data before passing it to the next.") as tracker:
            data_packets = VGroup()
            for i in range(4):
                packet = Circle(radius=0.15, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.8)
                packet.move_to(stages[0].get_left())
                packet.shift(LEFT * 0.5 + DOWN * 0.3 + UP * (i * 0.2))
                data_packets.add(packet)
            
            self.play(FadeIn(data_packets), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            
            # Animate flow through pipeline
            for stage_idx in range(len(stages) - 1):
                for packet in data_packets:
                    self.play(
                        packet.animate.move_to(stages[stage_idx + 1].get_center()),
                        run_time=0.3
                    )
        
        self.play(FadeOut(data_packets))
        
        # Pipeline label
        with self.voiceover(text="This is a data pipeline. The key benefit is that each stage can process data independently, enabling parallel processing and efficient resource utilization.") as tracker:
            pipeline_label = Text("Data Pipeline", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
            pipeline_label.next_to(stages, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            self.play(Write(pipeline_label), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # SECTION 2: The Problem - Pageable vs Pinned Memory
        with self.voiceover(text="Now, let's address a critical bottleneck. When data moves between CPU and GPU, or through different processing units, memory transfer speed matters immensely.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(pipeline_label),
                stages.animate.shift(UP * 2).scale(0.6),
                arrows.animate.shift(UP * 2).scale(0.6),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here's the problem. Regular memory, called pageable memory, can be swapped out to disk by the operating system. This causes delays when the GPU tries to access it.") as tracker:
            # Create memory representation
            cpu_box = RoundedRectangle(height=2, width=2.5, corner_radius=0.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.2)
            cpu_label = Text("CPU Memory", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
            cpu_label.next_to(cpu_box, UP, buff=0.2)
            cpu = VGroup(cpu_box, cpu_label)
            cpu.shift(LEFT * 3 + DOWN * 0.5)
            
            gpu_box = RoundedRectangle(height=2, width=2.5, corner_radius=0.2, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.2)
            gpu_label = Text("GPU Memory", font_size=20, color=RED)
            gpu_label.next_to(gpu_box, UP, buff=0.2)
            gpu = VGroup(gpu_box, gpu_label)
            gpu.shift(RIGHT * 3 + DOWN * 0.5)
            
            self.play(FadeIn(cpu), FadeIn(gpu), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            
            # Pageable memory blocks
            pageable_blocks = VGroup()
            for i in range(3):
                for j in range(4):
                    block = Square(side_length=0.3, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=1)
                    block.move_to(cpu_box.get_center())
                    block.shift(LEFT * 0.6 + UP * 0.5 + RIGHT * (j * 0.4) + DOWN * (i * 0.4))
                    pageable_blocks.add(block)
            
            self.play(FadeIn(pageable_blocks), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        # Show slow transfer
        with self.voiceover(text="When transferring from pageable memory, the system may need to wait while pages are retrieved from disk. This creates unpredictable delays.") as tracker:
            slow_arrow = Arrow(cpu_box.get_right(), gpu_box.get_left(), buff=0.3, color=YELLOW)
            slow_label = Text("SLOW", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)
            slow_label.next_to(slow_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
            
            self.play(GrowArrow(slow_arrow), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(FadeIn(slow_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            
            # Animate slow transfer with some blocks getting stuck
            transfer_blocks = pageable_blocks.copy()
            for i, block in enumerate(transfer_blocks[:4]):
                if i == 2:
                    # Simulate page fault - block pauses
                    self.play(block.animate.set_color(GRAY), run_time=0.3)
                    self.wait(0.5)
                    self.play(block.animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=0.3)
                self.play(block.animate.move_to(gpu_box.get_center() + LEFT * 0.6 + UP * 0.5 + RIGHT * ((i % 4) * 0.4)), run_time=0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(transfer_blocks), FadeOut(slow_arrow), FadeOut(slow_label))
        
        # SECTION 3: Pinned Memory Solution
        with self.voiceover(text="This is where pinned memory comes to the rescue. Pinned memory, also called page-locked memory, stays resident in RAM and cannot be swapped out.") as tracker:
            # Highlight pinned memory blocks
            pinned_blocks = VGroup()
            for i in range(3):
                for j in range(4):
                    block = Square(side_length=0.3, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=2)
                    block.move_to(cpu_box.get_center())
                    block.shift(LEFT * 0.6 + UP * 0.5 + RIGHT * (j * 0.4) + DOWN * (i * 0.4))
                    pin = Text("P", font_size=14, color=WHITE)
                    pin.move_to(block.get_center())
                    pinned_group = VGroup(block, pin)
                    pinned_blocks.add(pinned_group)
            
            self.play(Transform(pageable_blocks, pinned_blocks), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            
            # Add pinned memory label
            pinned_label = Text("Pinned (Page-Locked) Memory", font_size=18, color=GREEN)
            pinned_label.next_to(cpu_box, DOWN, buff=0.3)
            self.play(FadeIn(pinned_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Because pinned memory is always available in RAM, transfers to the GPU are much faster and more predictable. The data path is optimized.") as tracker:
            fast_arrow = Arrow(cpu_box.get_right(), gpu_box.get_left(), buff=0.3, color=GREEN, stroke_width=4)
            fast_label = Text("FAST", font_size=16, color=GREEN)
            fast_label.next_to(fast_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
            
            self.play(GrowArrow(fast_arrow), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(FadeIn(fast_label), run_time=0.3)
            
            # Fast transfer animation
            fast_blocks = VGroup()
            for i in range(3):
                for j in range(4):
                    block = Square(side_length=0.3, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=2)
                    block.move_to(gpu_box.get_center())
                    block.shift(LEFT * 0.6 + UP * 0.5 + RIGHT * (j * 0.4) + DOWN * (i * 0.4))
                    fast_blocks.add(block)
            
            self.play(FadeIn(fast_blocks, shift=RIGHT), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        # SECTION 4: Benefits Summary
        with self.voiceover(text="Pinned memory offers three key benefits. First, higher bandwidth. Second, asynchronous transfers that overlap computation. And third, predictable performance without page faults.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(cpu), FadeOut(gpu), FadeOut(pageable_blocks),
                FadeOut(pinned_label), FadeOut(fast_arrow), FadeOut(fast_label),
                FadeOut(fast_blocks), FadeOut(stages), FadeOut(arrows),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3
            )
            
            # Benefits list in two columns
```

```python
        ) as tracker:

        self.wait(0.3)

        # ===== SECTION 1: Misspecification Demo =====
        ax = Axes(

        data_coords = [
            (-2.5, 6.2), (-2, 4.3), (-1.5, 2.8), (-1, 1.2), (-0.5, 0.3),
            (0, 0.1), (0.5, 0.4), (1, 1.3), (1.5, 2.9), (2, 4.1), (2.5, 6.3)
        ]
        dots = VGroup(*[
            Dot(ax.c2p(x, y), radius=0.06, color=BLUE)
            for x, y in data_coords
        ])
        
        # Linear model line y = (4/3)x + 3
        linear_line = Line(ax.c2p(-3, -1), ax.c2p(3, 7), color=RED, stroke_width=3)
        linear_label = Text("Linear Model", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(

        true_curve = ax.plot(lambda x: x**2, x_range=[-2.5, 2.5], color=GREEN, stroke_width=2)

            ax.c2p(1.8, 3.2), RIGHT, buff=0.2
        )
        
        right_panel = VGroup(
            Text("Reality: Complex", font_size=20, color=GREEN),

        with self.voiceover(
```
