            axes.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
            
            x_label = MathTex(r"\text{Gradient Value}", font_size=24).next_to(axes.x_axis, DOWN)
            y_label = MathTex(r"\text{Frequency}", font_size=24).next_to(axes.y_axis, LEFT)
            
            # Create histogram bars (normal-like distribution)
            bar_heights = [1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 7, 4, 2, 1]
            bar_positions = [-2, -1.5, -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2]
            bars = VGroup()
            
            for pos, height in zip(bar_positions, bar_heights):
                bar = Rectangle(
                    width=0.4,
                    height=height * 0.4,
                    fill_color=BLUE,
                    fill_opacity=0.7,
                    stroke_color=WHITE,
                    stroke_width=1
                )
                bar.move_to(axes.c2p(pos, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
                bars.add(bar)
            
            ideal_text = Text("Ideal: Balanced Gradients", font_size=22, color=GREEN)
            ideal_text.next_to(axes, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(grad_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Create(bars), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(ideal_text), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(grad_title), FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(x_label), FadeOut(y_label), 
                 FadeOut(bars), FadeOut(ideal_text))
        
        # Section 4: Vanishing Gradients
        with self.voiceover(text="One common problem is vanishing gradients. When gradients become extremely small, weights in early layers barely update, causing the network to stop learning. Notice how the distribution is skewed toward zero.") as tracker:
            vanish_title = Text("Problem: Vanishing Gradients", font_size=32, color=RED)
            vanish_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            axes2 = Axes(
                x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
                y_range=[0, 10, 2],
                axis_config={"include_tip": False, "font_size": 20},
                x_length=8,
                y_length=4
            )
            axes2.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
            
            x_label2 = MathTex(r"\text{Gradient Value}", font_size=24).next_to(axes2.x_axis, DOWN)
            y_label2 = MathTex(r"\text{Frequency}", font_size=24).next_to(axes2.y_axis, LEFT)
            
            # Skewed distribution toward zero
            vanish_heights = [10, 6, 3, 1, 0.5, 1, 3, 6, 10]
            vanish_bars = VGroup()
            
            for pos, height in zip(bar_positions, vanish_heights):
                bar = Rectangle(
                    width=0.4,
                    height=min(height * 0.4, 3.8),
                    fill_color=RED,
                    fill_opacity=0.7,
                    stroke_color=WHITE,
                    stroke_width=1
                )
                bar.move_to(axes2.c2p(pos, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
                vanish_bars.add(bar)
            
            warning_text = Text("Warning: Gradients near zero!", font_size=22, color=RED)
            warning_text.next_to(axes2, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(vanish_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Create(axes2), Write(x_label2), Write(y_label2), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Create(vanish_bars), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(warning_text), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(vanish_title), FadeOut(axes2), FadeOut(x_label2), FadeOut(y_label2),
                 FadeOut(vanish_bars), FadeOut(warning_text))
        
        # Section 5: Exploding Gradients
        with self.voiceover(text="Conversely, exploding gradients occur when values become excessively large. This causes unstable updates and can make training diverge. The distribution shows extreme values far from zero.") as tracker:
            explode_title = Text("Problem: Exploding Gradients", font_size=32, color=RED)
            explode_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            axes3 = Axes(
                x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
                y_range=[0, 6, 2],
                axis_config={"include_tip": False, "font_size": 20},
                x_length=8,
                y_length=4
            )
            axes3.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
            
            x_label3 = MathTex(r"\text{Gradient Value}", font_size=24).next_to(axes3.x_axis, DOWN)
            y_label3 = MathTex(r"\text{Frequency}", font_size=24).next_to(axes3.y_axis, LEFT)
            
            # Distribution with outliers at extremes
            explode_heights = [6, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 6]
            explode_bars = VGroup()
            
            for pos, height in zip(bar_positions, explode_heights):
                bar = Rectangle(
                    width=0.4,
                    height=height * 0.4,
                    fill_color=ORANGE,
                    fill_opacity=0.7,
                    stroke_color=WHITE,
                    stroke_width=1
                )
                bar.move_to(axes3.c2p(pos, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)
                explode_bars.add(bar)
            
            warning_text2 = Text("Warning: Extreme gradient values!", font_size=22, color=ORANGE)
            warning_text2.next_to(axes3, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(explode_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Create(axes3), Write(x_label3), Write(y_label3), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Create(explode_bars), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(warning_text2), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(explode_title), FadeOut(axes3), FadeOut(x_label3), FadeOut(y_label3),
                 FadeOut(explode_bars), FadeOut(warning_text2))
        
        # Section 6: Solutions and Best Practices
        with self.voiceover(text="To address these issues, several techniques help maintain healthy gradient distributions. Batch normalization stabilizes activations. Proper weight initialization sets appropriate starting values. Gradient clipping prevents exploding gradients. And residual connections provide shortcut paths for gradient flow.") as tracker:
            solutions_title = Text("Solutions for Healthy Gradients", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
            solutions_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            solutions = VGroup(
                Text("• Batch Normalization", font_size=26, color=BLUE),
                Text("• Weight Initialization", font_size=26, color=BLUE),
                Text("• Gradient Clipping", font_size=26, color=BLUE),
                Text("• Residual Connections", font_size=26, color=BLUE)
            )
            solutions.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.5)
            solutions.shift(LEFT * 2)
            
            # Visual icons for each solution
            batch_norm_box = SurroundingRectangle(solutions[0], color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
            init_arrow = Arrow(UP, DOWN, color=GREEN).next_to(solutions[1], RIGHT, buff=0.5)
            clip_bracket = MathTex(r"|\nabla| < \text{threshold}", font_size=24, color=RED).next_to(solutions[2], RIGHT, buff=0.3)
            skip_line = Line(LEFT * 0.5, RIGHT * 0.5, color=ORANGE).next_to(solutions[3], RIGHT, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(solutions_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            
            for i, sol in enumerate(solutions):
                self.play(Write(sol), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.15)
                if i == 0:
                    self.play(Create(batch_norm_box), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.05)
                elif i == 1:
                    self.play(GrowArrow(init_arrow), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.05)
                elif i == 2:
                    self.play(Write(clip_bracket), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.05)
                elif i == 3:
                    self.play(Create(skip_line), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.05)
            
            self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(solutions_title), FadeOut(solutions), FadeOut(batch_norm_box),
                 FadeOut(init_arrow), FadeOut(clip_bracket), FadeOut(skip_line))
        
        # Final Summary
        with self.voiceover(text="To summarize: understanding gradient distribution is essential for training deep neural networks effectively. By monitoring gradients and applying appropriate techniques, you can ensure stable and efficient learning throughout your network.") as tracker:
            summary_title = Text("Key Takeaways", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)
            summary_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            takeaways = VGroup(
                Text("1. Gradients flow backward via the chain rule", font_size=24),
                Text("2. Well-distributed gradients enable stable training", font_size=24),
                Text("3. Watch for vanishing and exploding gradients", font_size=24),
                Text("4. Use normalization, proper initialization, and clipping", font_size=24)
            )
            takeaways.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.5)
            takeaways.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(summary_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(FadeIn(takeaways), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.wait(1)
        
        # End screen
        self.play(FadeOut(summary_title), FadeOut(takeaways))
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Thank you for watching. Apply these concepts to optimize your neural network training.") as tracker:
            end_text = Text("Happy Learning!", font_size=48, color=BLUE)
            self.play(Write(end_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
            self.wait(0.5)

messages.content: You are an expert mathematical animator and pedagogical engineer using Manim Community Edition and manim-voiceover with AOSSpeechService. Write executable, self-contained Python code that synchronizes mathematical animations with spoken educational explanations.

I'm teaching sequence models and want a visual of the causal constraint in convolutions. Show a filter sliding over tokens with a masked future window, illustrating how only past tokens contribute. Compare with an ungated version to emphasize information leakage, and include a step-by-step masking animation.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService


class CausalConstraintInConvolutions(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Set up speech service
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Colors
        color_input = BLUE
        color_kernel = RED
        color_output = GREEN
        color_past = YELLOW
        color_future = GRAY
        
        # ============================================
        # INTRODUCTION
        # ============================================
        title = Text("Causal Constraint in Convolutions", font_size=48)
        subtitle = Text("Subject: AI", font_size=28, color=GRAY)
        subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="Imagine a signal that carries vital information, where every moment counts. "
                 "What if your model could only rely on past data to make predictions? "
                 "This scenario highlights the essence of causal constraints in convolutions. "
                 "Today, you will dive into the fascinating world of causal convolution and uncover how it shapes predictive models!"
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle))
        
        # ============================================
        # STANDARD CONVOLUTION REVIEW
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(
            text="Let us begin with the standard convolution formula. "
                 "Convolution combines an input signal with a kernel to produce an output."
        ) as tracker:
            conv_formula = MathTex(
                r"y[n] = (x * w)[n] = \sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty} x[m] \, w[n - m]",
                font_size=40
            )
            self.play(Write(conv_formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="Here, x is the input signal, w is the kernel or filter, and y is the output. "
                 "Notice that the summation ranges over all integers, from negative infinity to positive infinity."
        ) as tracker:
            # Label the parts
            x_label = MathTex(r"x = \text{input}", font_size=24, color=color_input)
            w_label = MathTex(r"w = \text{kernel}", font_size=24, color=color_kernel)
            y_label = MathTex(r"y = \text{output}", font_size=24, color=color_output)
            
            labels_group = VGroup(x_label, w_label, y_label).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1)
            labels_group.next_to(conv_formula, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            
            self.play(FadeIn(labels_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        self.play(FadeOut(conv_formula), FadeOut(labels_group))
        
        # ============================================
        # VISUAL: Standard Convolution (The Problem)
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(
            text="Let us visualize this. Imagine we want to compute the output at time n equals 3. "
                 "In standard convolution, the kernel looks at samples both before and after position n."
        ) as tracker:
            # Create a timeline
            timeline = NumberLine(
                x_range=[0, 7, 1],
                length=6,
                include_numbers=True,
                numbers_to_include=[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
                font_size=20
            )
            timeline.to_edge(UP, buff=1)
            
            time_label = Text("Time index n", font_size=20)
            time_label.next_to(timeline, DOWN, buff=0.2)
            
            self.play(Create(timeline), FadeIn(time_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        # Input signal squares
        input_vals = [2, 3, 1, 4, 2, 5, 3]
        input_squares = VGroup()
        for i, val in enumerate(input_vals):
            sq = Square(side_length=0.4, fill_color=color_input, fill_opacity=0.6)
            num = MathTex(str(val), font_size=16)
            group = VGroup(sq, num)
            group.move_to(timeline.n2p(i) + DOWN * 0.8)
            input_squares.add(group)
        
        input_label = MathTex(r"x[n]", font_size=24, color=color_input)
        input_label.next_to(input_squares, LEFT, buff=0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="Here is our input signal x. Each square represents a sample at a specific time index."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(input_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(AnimationGroup(*[FadeIn(sq) for sq in input_squares], lag_ratio=0.1), 
                     run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Show kernel centered at n=3
        kernel_size = 3
        center_idx = 3
        kernel_squares = VGroup()
        kernel_weights = [0.5, 1.0, 0.5]
        
        for i, w in enumerate(kernel_weights):
            idx = center_idx - 1 + i
            sq = Square(side_length=0.4, fill_color=color_kernel, fill_opacity=0.6)
            num = MathTex(str(w), font_size=16)
            group = VGroup(sq, num)
            group.move_to(timeline.n2p(idx) + DOWN * 0.8)
            kernel_squares.add(group)
        
        kernel_label = MathTex(r"w", font_size=24, color=color_kernel)
        kernel_label.next_to(kernel_squares, RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        # Highlight position n=3
        current_arrow = Arrow(
            timeline.n2p(center_idx) + UP * 0.3,
            timeline.n2p(center_idx) + UP * 0.8,
            color=YELLOW,
            buff=0
        )
        current_label = MathTex(r"n=3", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        current_label.next_to(current_arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="To compute the output at n equals 3, a standard convolution kernel of size 3 "
                 "would look at inputs from n equals 2, n equals 3, and n equals 4."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeIn(current_arrow), 
                FadeIn(current_label),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4
            )
            self.play(
                FadeIn(kernel_label),
                AnimationGroup(*[TransformFromCopy(input_squares[center_idx - 1 + i], kernel_squares[i]) 
                                for i in range(kernel_size)]),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6
            )
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # THE PROBLEM: Using future data
        future_brace = Brace(input_squares[4], DOWN, color=RED)
        future_text = Text("FUTURE data!", font_size=16, color=RED)
        future_text.next_to(future_brace, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="But wait! At time n equals 3, we can access samples from n equals 2 and n equals 3, "
                 "but n equals 4 is in the future. We should not be able to see it yet! "
                 "This is the fundamental problem with standard convolution for prediction tasks."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(
                Create(future_brace),
                FadeIn(future_text),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(timeline), FadeOut(time_label),
            FadeOut(input_squares), FadeOut(input_label),
            FadeOut(kernel_squares), FadeOut(kernel_label),
            FadeOut(current_arrow), FadeOut(current_label),
            FadeOut(future_brace), FadeOut(future_text)
        )
        
        # ============================================
        # CAUSAL CONSTRAINT INTRODUCTION
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(
            text="This is where the causal constraint comes in. "
                 "A causal system is one where the output at any time depends only on present and past inputs, "
                 "never on future inputs."
        ) as tracker:
            causal_title = Text("Causal Constraint", font_size=40, color=YELLOW)
            causal_def = Text(
                "Output depends only on present and past inputs",
                font_size=24,
                color=GRAY
            )
            causal_def.next_to(causal_title, DOWN, buff=0.3)
            
            self.play(Write(causal_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(causal_def), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        self.play(FadeOut(causal_title), FadeOut(causal_def))
        
        # ============================================
        # CAUSAL CONSTRAINT FORMULA
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(
            text="Mathematically, we enforce causality by requiring that the kernel weights are zero "
                 "for all negative indices."
        ) as tracker:
            causal_formula = MathTex(
                r"w[n] = 0 \quad \text{for} \quad n < 0",
                font_size=44,
                color=YELLOW
            )
            self.play(Write(causal_formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="This simple constraint ensures that when we compute the convolution, "
                 "we never use input samples from the future."

        )
        
        # ============================================

        self.wait(0.3)
        self.play(FadeOut(nn_title))
        
        # Applications list
        with self.voiceover(

        ) as tracker:
            app2 = Text("2. Time Series Forecasting", font_size=28, color=GREEN)
            app2_desc = Text("Use only historical data to predict future values", font_size=20, color=GRAY)
            app2_desc.next_to(app2, DOWN, buff=0.2, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            app2_group = VGroup(app2, app2_desc)
            app2_group.next_to(app1_group, DOWN, buff=0.5, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            
            self.play(Write(app2), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(app2_desc), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="Third, in audio processing and speech synthesis, generating audio samples requires "

        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(app1_group), 
            FadeOut(app2_group), 
            FadeOut(app3_group)
        )
        
        # ============================================
        # KEY BENEFITS
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(
            text="The key benefit of causal convolution is that it ensures the model makes predictions "
                 "the same way humans do: by only considering what we already know."
        ) as tracker:
            benefit_title = Text("Why Causal Convolution Matters", font_size=28, color=YELLOW)
            benefit_title.to_edge(UP, buff=2)
            
            benefits = VGroup(
                Text("✓ Prevents data leakage from the future", font_size=22),
                Text("✓ Ensures realistic prediction scenarios", font_size=22),
                Text("✓ Maintains temporal ordering integrity", font_size=22)
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            benefits.next_to(benefit_title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            # Create a box around the benefits
            benefit_box = SurroundingRectangle(
                VGroup(benefit_title, benefits),
                fill_color=BLACK,
                fill_opacity=0.3,
                stroke_color=YELLOW,
                stroke_width=2,
                buff=0.3
            )
            
            self.play(Create(benefit_box), FadeIn(benefit_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(AnimationGroup(*[FadeIn(b) for b in benefits], lag_ratio=0.2), 
                     run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(benefit_box), FadeOut(benefit_title), FadeOut(benefits))
        
        # ============================================
        # SUMMARY
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(
            text="To summarize: Causal convolution modifies standard convolution by ensuring "
                 "the kernel only accesses present and past data. This is essential for any "
                 "prediction task where using future information would be cheating."
        ) as tracker:
            summary_title = Text("Summary", font_size=40, color=YELLOW)
            summary_title.to_edge(UP, buff=1)
            
            summary_points = VGroup(
                MathTex(r"\bullet\ \text{Causal: } w[n] = 0 \text{ for } n < 0", font_size=28),
                MathTex(r"\bullet\ \text{Output depends only on } x[k] \text{ where } k \leq n", font_size=28),
                MathTex(r"\bullet\ \text{Essential for real-time prediction}", font_size=28)

            summary_points.next_to(summary_title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(summary_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(AnimationGroup(*[Write(p) for p in summary_points], lag_ratio=0.2),

        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="By applying causal constraints, you can build neural networks that make "
                 "accurate, realistic predictions without looking ahead. This improves "
                 "model reliability and ensures your predictions are practical for real-world deployment."
        ) as tracker:
            closing = Text(
                "Build reliable predictive models with causal convolutions!",

                color=GREEN
            )
            closing.next_to(summary_points, DOWN, buff=0.8)

I'm studying character-level models and want to visualize a subset of test samples. Display the model's predicted character above the actual character, with a checkmark for correct and an X for incorrect. Add confidence scores and a small per-sample annotation to illustrate where the model errs.

```python
from manim import Scene, Text, Write, FadeIn, FadeOut, TransformFromCopy, Create, Arrow, Square, Circle, VGroup, Line, DOWN, UP, LEFT, RIGHT, BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, RED, GRAY, WHITE
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService


class CharacterLevelModelScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title
        title = Text("Character Level Model", font_size=48, color=BLUE)
        subtitle = Text("Understanding Text at the Granular Level", font_size=28, color=GRAY)
        title_group = VGroup(title, subtitle).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine you have a sentence you want to understand at the most granular level — each character. How do we build a model that grasps the meaning based on individual characters rather than entire words? You are about to find out!") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(title_group))
        
        # Show a sentence and break it into characters
        sentence = Text('"Hello"', font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        sentence.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let us start with a simple word: Hello. In a character-level model, we do not treat this as one unit. Instead, we break it down into its individual characters.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(sentence), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Break into characters
        chars = ["H", "e", "l", "l", "o"]
        char_mobjects = [Text(c, font_size=40, color=YELLOW) for c in chars]
        char_group = VGroup(*char_mobjects)
        char_group.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        char_group.next_to(sentence, DOWN, buff=1)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="H, e, l, l, o. Each character becomes its own input token to the model.") as tracker:
            for i, char_mob in enumerate(char_mobjects):
                self.play(TransformFromCopy(sentence[i+1:i+2], char_mob), run_time=tracker.duration / len(chars))
        
        # Character encoding boxes
        encoding_boxes = []
        encoding_labels = []
        for i, char in enumerate(chars):
            box = Square(side_length=0.8, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.3)
            box.move_to(char_mobjects[i].get_center())
            box.shift(DOWN * 1.5)
            label = Text(f"\'{char}\'", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(box, DOWN, buff=0.2)
            encoding_boxes.append(box)
            encoding_labels.append(label)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Each character is then encoded into a numerical representation. This could be a one-hot encoding or a learned embedding vector.") as tracker:
            for i in range(len(chars)):
                self.play(
                    Create(encoding_boxes[i]),
                    Write(encoding_labels[i]),
                    run_time=tracker.duration / len(chars)
                )
        
        # Draw arrows from characters to encoding
        arrows = []
        for i in range(len(chars)):
            arrow = Arrow(
                char_mobjects[i].get_bottom(),
                encoding_boxes[i].get_top(),
                buff=0.2,
                color=WHITE
            )
            arrows.append(arrow)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Arrows represent the flow of information from raw characters to their encoded representations.") as tracker:
            self.play(*[Create(arrow) for arrow in arrows], run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Neural network representation
        nn_label = Text("Character-Level Neural Network", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        nn_label.to_edge(DOWN, buff=2)
        
        # Create a simple network visualization
        input_layer = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(3)])
        input_layer.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        hidden_layer = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)])
        hidden_layer.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        output_layer = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(3)])
        output_layer.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        network = VGroup(input_layer, hidden_layer, output_layer)
        network.arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.5)
        network.next_to(nn_label, UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # Layer labels
        input_label = Text("Input\n(Encoded Chars)", font_size=16, color=GREEN).next_to(input_layer, LEFT, buff=0.3)
        hidden_label = Text("Hidden\nLayer", font_size=16, color=YELLOW).next_to(hidden_layer, UP, buff=0.3)
        output_label = Text("Output\n(Prediction)", font_size=16, color=RED).next_to(output_layer, RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="These encoded characters feed into a neural network. The network processes them through hidden layers to learn patterns at the character level.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                Write(nn_label),
                Create(input_layer),
                Create(hidden_layer),
                Create(output_layer),
                Write(input_label),
                Write(hidden_label),
                Write(output_label),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        # Draw connections - fix opacity issue by using set_stroke
        connections = []
        for input_node in input_layer:
            for hidden_node in hidden_layer:
                line = Line(input_node.get_right(), hidden_node.get_left(), stroke_width=1, color=GRAY)
                line.set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
                connections.append(line)
        
        for hidden_node in hidden_layer:
            for output_node in output_layer:
                line = Line(hidden_node.get_right(), output_node.get_left(), stroke_width=1, color=GRAY)
                line.set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
                connections.append(line)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Connections between layers allow the model to learn complex relationships between characters, enabling it to understand spelling patterns, word boundaries, and even grammar.") as tracker:
            self.play(*[Create(conn) for conn in connections], run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Clear for summary
        self.play(
            FadeOut(sentence),
            FadeOut(char_group),
            FadeOut(VGroup(*encoding_boxes)),
            FadeOut(VGroup(*encoding_labels)),
            FadeOut(VGroup(*arrows)),
            FadeOut(network),
            FadeOut(input_label),
            FadeOut(hidden_label),
            FadeOut(output_label),
            FadeOut(nn_label),
            FadeOut(VGroup(*connections))
        )
        
        # Summary section
        summary_title = Text("Key Takeaways", font_size=40, color=BLUE)
        summary_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        takeaways = VGroup(
            Text("• Characters are the basic units of representation", font_size=24),
            Text("• Each character is encoded numerically", font_size=24),
            Text("• Neural networks learn patterns from character sequences", font_size=24),
            Text("• Models can predict next characters or classify text", font_size=24)
        )
        takeaways.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        takeaways.next_to(summary_title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="To summarize: in character-level models, individual characters become the basic units. Each character gets encoded numerically. Neural networks then learn patterns from these character sequences. These models can predict the next character or classify entire pieces of text.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(summary_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            for takeaway in takeaways:
                self.play(Write(takeaway), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
        
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Applications
        app_title = Text("Applications", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
        apps = VGroup(
            Text("• Text generation", font_size=22),
            Text("• Spelling correction", font_size=22),
            Text("• Language modeling", font_size=22),
            Text("• Code generation", font_size=22)
        )
        apps.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        app_box = VGroup(app_title, apps).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        app_box.center()
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Character-level models power applications like text generation, spelling correction, language modeling, and even code generation. By understanding text at the most fundamental level, these models can handle rare words, misspellings, and even generate entirely new words.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(summary_title),
                FadeOut(takeaways),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2
            )
            self.play(Write(app_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            for app in apps:
                self.play(Write(app), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.15)
        
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(app_box))
        
        # Closing
        closing = Text("Character-Level Models: Understanding Text One Character at a Time", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        closing.center()
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Character-level models truly understand text one character at a time, opening up powerful possibilities for AI language understanding.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(closing), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(closing))
```

from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class RealTimeTrainingDashboardScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(

        # Title

            stroke_width=3,

        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine a dashboard that displays all the metrics that tell you how well your AI is learning.") as tracker:

        # Status indicator
        status_dot = Dot(color=GREEN, radius=0.1)
        status_dot.next_to(dashboard_title, RIGHT, buff=0.5)

        status_text.next_to(status_dot, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # Create panels for different metrics

        acc_axes.move_to(acc_panel.get_center())
        acc_axes.shift(DOWN * 0.1)
        
        acc_x_label = Text("Epoch", font_size=10, color=GRAY)

        acc_y_label = Text("%", font_size=10, color=GRAY)

        with self.voiceover(text="The accuracy panel tracks how often the model makes correct predictions, rising as training progresses.") as tracker:
            self.play(

        # Animate accuracy curve

            for i, (x, y) in enumerate(acc_points):

                else:

        # Metrics Panel (Bottom)

        with self.voiceover(text="The bottom panel displays key metrics at a glance.") as tracker:

        # Metric boxes
        metric_values = [

        metric_items = VGroup()

        metric_items.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)

        with self.voiceover(text="Current epoch shows training progress. Batch displays data samples processed. Learning rate controls step size. Elapsed time tracks duration.") as tracker:
            self.play(

        # Progress bar

        # Final summary
        summary = VGroup(

messages.content: You are an expert mathematical animator and pedagogical engineer using Manim Community Edition and manim-voiceover with AOSSpeechService. Write executable, self-contained Python code that synchronizes mathematical animations with spoken educational explanations.

I'm teaching an undergrad course on sequence models and want a probabilistic sampling visualization. Animate a spinning wheel divided into character slices, landing on the next character according to the learned distribution. Show the probability weights as arc lengths and reflect the sample decision with a glow and a landing pointer. Include a short, repeatable loop with different temperature settings to compare sampling diversity.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService
import random


class ProbabilisticSamplingVisualization(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Color scheme
        STRATUM_RED = "#FF6B6B"
        STRATUM_TEAL = "#4ECDC4"
        STRATUM_BLUE = "#45B7D1"
        SAMPLE_HIGHLIGHT = "#FFD93D"
        POPULATION_GRAY = "#A0A0A0"
        
        # ============================================
        # INTRO - Title and opening question
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine you're trying to draw a sample from a complex distribution, but how do you ensure that your sample is representative?") as tracker:
            title = Text("Probabilistic Sampling", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
            subtitle = Text("Visualization of Sampling Techniques", font_size=28, color=GRAY)
            title_group = VGroup(title, subtitle).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="What if I told you there's a visual way to intuitively understand probabilistic sampling?") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeOut(title_group), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        # ============================================
        # POPULATION SETUP
        # ============================================
        # Create a grid of population members (3 strata)
        # Stratum 1 (top): Red - 30 members
        # Stratum 2 (middle): Teal - 50 members  
        # Stratum 3 (bottom): Blue - 20 members
        
        population_group = VGroup()
        stratum1_dots = VGroup()  # Red - top 30%
        stratum2_dots = VGroup()  # Teal - middle 50%
        stratum3_dots = VGroup()  # Blue - bottom 20%
        
        dot_radius = 0.12
        spacing = 0.35
        rows = 10
        cols = 10
        
        for row in range(rows):
            for col in range(cols):
                x = (col - cols/2) * spacing
                y = (row - rows/2) * spacing * 0.8
                dot = Circle(radius=dot_radius, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0)
                
                # Assign strata by row (top 30%, middle 50%, bottom 20%)
                if row < 3:
                    dot.set_fill(POPULATION_GRAY)
                    stratum1_dots.add(dot)
                elif row < 8:
                    dot.set_fill(POPULATION_GRAY)
                    stratum2_dots.add(dot)
                else:
                    dot.set_fill(POPULATION_GRAY)
                    stratum3_dots.add(dot)
                
                dot.move_to([x, y, 0])
                population_group.add(dot)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's consider a population of one hundred individuals, divided into three distinct groups.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(population_group, lag_ratio=0.02), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Color the strata
        with self.voiceover(text="The top thirty percent are group A, shown in red. The middle fifty percent are group B in teal. And the bottom twenty percent are group C in blue.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                stratum1_dots.animate.set_fill(STRATUM_RED),
                stratum2_dots.animate.set_fill(STRATUM_TEAL),
                stratum3_dots.animate.set_fill(STRATUM_BLUE),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        # Add stratum labels
        stratum_labels = VGroup(
            Text("Group A: 30%", font_size=18, color=STRATUM_RED).next_to(stratum1_dots, LEFT, buff=0.5),
            Text("Group B: 50%", font_size=18, color=STRATUM_TEAL).next_to(stratum2_dots, LEFT, buff=0.5),
            Text("Group C: 20%", font_size=18, color=STRATUM_BLUE).next_to(stratum3_dots, LEFT, buff=0.5)
        )
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Notice the different proportions. Group B is the largest, while Group C is the smallest.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(stratum_labels), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ============================================
        # RANDOM SAMPLING
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(text="Now, let's demonstrate simple random sampling. We'll randomly select ten individuals from the entire population.") as tracker:
            random_title = Text("Simple Random Sampling", font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
            self.play(
                FadeOut(stratum_labels),
                Write(random_title),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        # Random sampling - select 10 dots randomly
        random.seed(42)
        random_sample_indices = random.sample(range(len(population_group)), 10)
        random_samples = VGroup(*[population_group[i].copy() for i in random_sample_indices])
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Watch as we pick ten individuals completely at random.") as tracker:
            animations = []
            for i, idx in enumerate(random_sample_indices):
                original = population_group[idx]
                highlight = Circle(radius=dot_radius * 1.5, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=SAMPLE_HIGHLIGHT, stroke_color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
                highlight.move_to(original.get_center())
                animations.append(FadeIn(highlight, scale=1.5))
            self.play(LaggedStart(*animations, lag_ratio=0.1), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Count samples per stratum
        stratum1_count = sum(1 for idx in random_sample_indices if population_group[idx] in stratum1_dots)
        stratum2_count = sum(1 for idx in random_sample_indices if population_group[idx] in stratum2_dots)
        stratum3_count = sum(1 for idx in random_sample_indices if population_group[idx] in stratum3_dots)
        
        random_stats = VGroup(
            Text(f"Group A samples: {stratum1_count}/10", font_size=20, color=STRATUM_RED),
            Text(f"Group B samples: {stratum2_count}/10", font_size=20, color=STRATUM_TEAL),
            Text(f"Group C samples: {stratum3_count}/10", font_size=20, color=STRATUM_BLUE)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.2).to_edge(RIGHT).shift(UP * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text=f"Look at the results. We got {stratum1_count} from group A, {stratum2_count} from group B, and {stratum3_count} from group C. Notice how the smaller group C might be underrepresented purely by chance.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(random_stats), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This is the nature of random sampling. It's unbiased but can sometimes produce unrepresentative samples, especially with small sample sizes.") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.play(
                FadeOut(random_stats),
                FadeOut(random_title),
                *[FadeOut(mob) for mob in self.mobjects if mob not in [population_group, stratum1_dots, stratum2_dots, stratum3_dots]],
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3
            )
        
        # Reset population colors
        self.play(
            stratum1_dots.animate.set_fill(STRATUM_RED),
            stratum2_dots.animate.set_fill(STRATUM_TEAL),
            stratum3_dots.animate.set_fill(STRATUM_BLUE),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # ============================================
        # STRATIFIED SAMPLING
        # ============================================
        stratified_title = Text("Stratified Sampling", font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let's explore stratified sampling. Instead of sampling from the entire population at once, we first divide the population into strata, or distinct groups.") as tracker:
            # Draw boxes around strata
            stratum1_box = SurroundingRectangle(stratum1_dots, buff=0.15, color=STRATUM_RED, stroke_width=2)
            stratum2_box = SurroundingRectangle(stratum2_dots, buff=0.15, color=STRATUM_TEAL, stroke_width=2)
            stratum3_box = SurroundingRectangle(stratum3_dots, buff=0.15, color=STRATUM_BLUE, stroke_width=2)
            
            self.play(
                Write(stratified_title),
                Create(stratum1_box),
                Create(stratum2_box),
                Create(stratum3_box),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        with self.voiceover(text="We already have our three strata: A, B, and C. The key idea is to sample proportionally from each stratum to ensure representation.") as tracker:
            # Show proportional sample sizes
            prop_formula = VGroup(
                MathTex(r"	ext{Group A: } 30\% 	imes 10 = 3", font_size=22, color=STRATUM_RED),
                MathTex(r"	ext{Group B: } 50\% 	imes 10 = 5", font_size=22, color=STRATUM_TEAL),
                MathTex(r"	ext{Group C: } 20\% 	imes 10 = 2", font_size=22, color=STRATUM_BLUE)
            ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3).to_edge(RIGHT)
            
            self.play(FadeIn(prop_formula), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Sample proportionally from each stratum
        random.seed(123)
        stratum1_sample_idx = random.sample(range(len(stratum1_dots)), 3)
        stratum2_sample_idx = random.sample(range(len(stratum2_dots)), 5)
        stratum3_sample_idx = random.sample(range(len(stratum3_dots)), 2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="So we'll sample three from group A, five from group B, and two from group C. Watch as we select proportionally from each stratum.") as tracker:
            animations = []
            for idx in stratum1_sample_idx:
                highlight = Circle(radius=dot_radius * 1.5, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=SAMPLE_HIGHLIGHT, stroke_color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
                highlight.move_to(stratum1_dots[idx].get_center())
                animations.append(FadeIn(highlight, scale=1.5))
            for idx in stratum2_sample_idx:
                highlight = Circle(radius=dot_radius * 1.5, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=SAMPLE_HIGHLIGHT, stroke_color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
                highlight.move_to(stratum2_dots[idx].get_center())
                animations.append(FadeIn(highlight, scale=1.5))
            for idx in stratum3_sample_idx:
                highlight = Circle(radius=dot_radius * 1.5, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=SAMPLE_HIGHLIGHT, stroke_color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
                highlight.move_to(stratum3_dots[idx].get_center())
                animations.append(FadeIn(highlight, scale=1.5))
            
            self.play(LaggedStart(*animations, lag_ratio=0.08), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        stratified_stats = VGroup(
            Text("Group A samples: 3/10 ✓", font_size=20, color=STRATUM_RED),
            Text("Group B samples: 5/10 ✓", font_size=20, color=STRATUM_TEAL),
            Text("Group C samples: 2/10 ✓", font_size=20, color=STRATUM_BLUE)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.2).to_edge(RIGHT).shift(UP * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Perfect! Each group is represented in exact proportion to its size in the population. Group C, despite being small, has guaranteed representation.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(prop_formula),
                FadeIn(stratified_stats),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        # ============================================
        # COMPARISON
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's compare both methods side by side.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(stratified_title),
                FadeOut(stratum1_box),
                FadeOut(stratum2_box),
                FadeOut(stratum3_box),
                FadeOut(stratified_stats),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5
            )
        
        # Create comparison boxes
        comparison_title = Text("Random vs Stratified Sampling", font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="On the left, simple random sampling is easy to implement and unbiased, but it can miss minority groups by chance.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(comparison_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            
            random_box = VGroup(
                Text("Simple Random", font_size=22, color=WHITE),
                Text("✓ Easy to implement", font_size=16, color=GREEN),
                Text("✓ Unbiased", font_size=16, color=GREEN),
                Text("✗ May underrepresent", font_size=16, color=RED),
                Text("  minorities", font_size=16, color=RED)
            ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.15)
            random_box_box = SurroundingRectangle(random_box, buff=0.3, color=BLUE_B, fill_opacity=0.1)
            random_group = VGroup(random_box, random_box_box).shift(LEFT * 3.5 + DOWN * 0.5)
            
            self.play(FadeIn(random_group), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="On the right, stratified sampling guarantees representation from all groups, reduces sampling error, but requires knowing the population structure in advance.") as tracker:
            stratified_box = VGroup(
                Text("Stratified", font_size=22, color=WHITE),
                Text("✓ Guaranteed", font_size=16, color=GREEN),
                Text("  representation", font_size=16, color=GREEN),
                Text("✓ Lower variance", font_size=16, color=GREEN),
                Text("✗ Needs prior", font_size=16, color=RED),
                Text("  knowledge", font_size=16, color=RED)
            ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.15)
            stratified_box_box = SurroundingRectangle(stratified_box, buff=0.3, color=GREEN_B, fill_opacity=0.1)
            stratified_group = VGroup(stratified_box, stratified_box_box).shift(RIGHT * 3.5 + DOWN * 0.5)
            
            self.play(FadeIn(stratified_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ============================================
        # KEY TAKEAWAYS
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(text="Here are the key takeaways. Probabilistic sampling ensures every individual has a known chance of selection.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(comparison_title),
                FadeOut(random_group),
                FadeOut(stratified_group),
                FadeOut(population_group),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4
            )
            
            takeaway_title = Text("Key Takeaways", font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
            self.play(Write(takeaway_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        takeaways = VGroup(
            Text("• Random sampling: Equal chance for all", font_size=22, color=WHITE),
            Text("• Stratified sampling: Proportional representation", font_size=22, color=WHITE),
            Text("• Choose method based on population structure", font_size=22, color=WHITE),

from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService
import math

class GradientOutliersScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(

        )

        # ==========================================
        # 1. Title & Opener
        # ==========================================
        title = Text("Gradient Outliers and Training Dynamics", font_size=40)
        subtitle = Text("Understanding Their Impact on Model Training", font_size=28)
        header = VGroup(title, subtitle).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)

        with self.voiceover(
            text="Have you ever wondered why some models train beautifully while others struggle? The secret often lies in the gradients feeding into the training process. The presence of outliers in gradients can be a game changer, wreaking havoc on convergence and performance. Today, we will demystify gradient outliers and their impact on training dynamics!"
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(header), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # ==========================================
        # 2. Learning Outcomes
        # ==========================================
        lo_title = Text("Learning Outcomes", font_size=32)
        lo1 = Text("• Understand what gradient outliers are and why they matter.", font_size=24)
        lo2 = Text("• Identify how outliers affect training dynamics and model performance.", font_size=24)
        lo3 = Text("• Explore strategies to mitigate the impact of gradient outliers.", font_size=24)
        lo_group = VGroup(lo_title, lo1, lo2, lo3).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.3)
        lo_group.scale_to_fit_width(12)
        lo_group.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.8)

        with self.voiceover(
            text="By the end of this lesson, you will understand what gradient outliers are, see how they disturb training, and learn practical ways to tame them."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(header), FadeIn(lo_group), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # ==========================================
        # 3. What are gradient outliers?
        # ==========================================
        axes_grad = Axes(
            x_range=[-5, 5, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.2, 0.2],
            x_length=6,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        )
        curve = axes_grad.plot(lambda x: math.exp(-x**2), x_range=[-3, 3], color=BLUE)
        dot_l = Dot(axes_grad.c2p(-4.5, 0.05), color=RED)
        dot_r = Dot(axes_grad.c2p(4.3, 0.05), color=RED)
        outlier_label = Text("Outliers", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(dot_r, UP)
        caption_grad = Text("Most gradients cluster near zero, but a few explode outward.", font_size=22)
        dist_group = VGroup(axes_grad, curve, dot_l, dot_r, outlier_label, caption_grad)
        dist_group.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        dist_group.scale_to_fit_width(12)
        dist_group.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.8)

        with self.voiceover(
            text="During backpropagation, most gradients cluster around a typical range. But some can explode to extreme values. These are the outliers."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(lo_group), FadeIn(dist_group), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # ==========================================

        # ==========================================
        formula = MathTex(r"w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta \nabla L(w_t)", font_size=36)
        num_line = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 10, 1], length=6, include_numbers=True)

        arrow_normal = Arrow(num_line.n2p(5), num_line.n2p(6.2), buff=0, color=GREEN)
        arrow_outlier = Arrow(num_line.n2p(5), num_line.n2p(9.5), buff=0, color=RED)
        label_normal = Text("Normal step", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(arrow_normal, UP)
        label_outlier = Text("Outlier step", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(arrow_outlier, UP)
        update_group = VGroup(formula, num_line, param_dot, arrow_normal, arrow_outlier, label_normal, label_outlier)
        update_group.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        update_group.scale_to_fit_width(12)
        update_group.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.8)

        with self.voiceover(
            text="The parameter update rule depends directly on the gradient. A normal gradient gives a stable step, while an outlier injects a massive update that can overshoot the optimum."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(dist_group), FadeIn(update_group), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # ==========================================
        # 5. Impact on training dynamics — Loss curves
        # ==========================================
        axes_loss = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 8, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=6,
            y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        )
        stable = axes_loss.plot(lambda x: 3 * math.exp(-0.6 * x), x_range=[0, 8], color=GREEN)
        unstable = axes_loss.plot(lambda x: 3 * math.exp(-0.2 * x) + 0.3 * math.sin(5 * x), x_range=[0, 8], color=RED)
        legend = VGroup(
            Dot(color=GREEN, radius=0.08), Text("Stable", font_size=20),
            Dot(color=RED, radius=0.08), Text("Erratic", font_size=20)
        ).arrange_in_grid(rows=1, cols=4, buff=0.2)
        caption_loss = Text("Outliers create loss spikes and erratic convergence.", font_size=22)
        loss_group = VGroup(axes_loss, stable, unstable, legend, caption_loss)
        loss_group.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        loss_group.scale_to_fit_width(12)
        loss_group.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.8)

        with self.voiceover(
            text="In practice, this leads to erratic loss curves, slow convergence, or even outright divergence."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(update_group), FadeIn(loss_group), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # ==========================================
        # 6. Mitigation strategies
        # ==========================================
        mit_title = Text("Mitigation Strategies", font_size=32)
        s1 = VGroup(Dot(color=BLUE, radius=0.08), Text("Gradient Clipping", font_size=24)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        s2 = VGroup(Dot(color=BLUE, radius=0.08), Text("Robust Loss Functions", font_size=24)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        s3 = VGroup(Dot(color=BLUE, radius=0.08), Text("Larger Batch Sizes", font_size=24)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        s4 = VGroup(Dot(color=BLUE, radius=0.08), Text("Adaptive Optimizers", font_size=24)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        grid = VGroup(s1, s2, s3, s4).arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=2, buff=(0.8, 0.4))
        mit_group = VGroup(mit_title, grid)
        mit_group.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        mit_group.scale_to_fit_width(12)
        mit_group.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.8)

        with self.voiceover(
            text="Fortunately, we have tools to fight back. Gradient clipping caps extreme values. Robust loss functions reduce sensitivity to noise. Larger batches average out outliers. And adaptive optimizers adjust the step size per parameter."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(loss_group), FadeIn(mit_group), run_time=tracker.duration)

        # ==========================================
        # 7. Closing
        # ==========================================
        closing = Text("Keep outliers in check for reliable, efficient training!", font_size=32)
        closing.to_edge(UP, buff=2)

        with self.voiceover(
            text="Managing gradient outliers is essential for stable and efficient model training."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(mit_group), FadeIn(closing), run_time=tracker.duration)

Add a short note comparing Xavier/He-like scales and how poor initialization can distort signals.

from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class NeuralNetworkInitVisualization(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title slide
        with self.voiceover(text="Have you ever wondered how a neural network learns the best way to adjust its weights? It all starts from the initial conditions, which are crucial for training. Let's dive into how different initialization techniques affect the learning process!") as tracker:
            title = Text("Neural Network Initialization", font_size=48, color=BLUE)
            subtitle = Text("From Zero to He: Why It Matters", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
            subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            title_group = VGroup(title, subtitle)
            title_group.center()
            self.play(FadeIn(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Today we'll explore four key initialization methods and see how they impact neural network training.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(title_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Introduction to why initialization matters
        with self.voiceover(text="Weight initialization is critical because it sets the starting point for gradient descent. A poor choice can lead to vanishing or exploding gradients, making training impossible.") as tracker:
            why_text = Text("Why Initialization Matters?", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)
            why_text.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            points = VGroup(
                Text("• Sets starting point for optimization", font_size=24),
                Text("• Prevents vanishing/exploding gradients", font_size=24),
                Text("• Affects convergence speed", font_size=24),
                Text("• Determines final model performance", font_size=24)
            ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
            points.next_to(why_text, DOWN, buff=0.6)
            
            box = SurroundingRectangle(points, color=BLUE, buff=0.3)
            
            self.play(Write(why_text), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(p) for p in points], lag_ratio=0.2), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.play(Create(box), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let's examine four popular initialization techniques.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(why_text), FadeOut(points), FadeOut(box), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Method 1: Zero Initialization
        with self.voiceover(text="First, Zero initialization. Here all weights are set to zero. While simple, this creates a major problem: all neurons compute the same output, and gradients are identical. This prevents learning.") as tracker:
            zero_title = Text("1. Zero Initialization", font_size=32, color=RED)
            zero_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            zero_formula = MathTex(r"W = 0", font_size=36)
            zero_formula.next_to(zero_title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            
            zero_grid = VGroup()
            for i in range(4):
                for j in range(4):
                    sq = Square(side_length=0.4, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
                    sq.shift(RIGHT * j * 0.45 + DOWN * i * 0.45)
                    zero_grid.add(sq)
            zero_grid.next_to(zero_formula, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            
            problem_text = Text("Problem: Symmetric updates prevent learning!", font_size=22, color=RED)
            problem_text.next_to(zero_grid, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(zero_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Write(zero_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(FadeIn(zero_grid), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(problem_text), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's move to a better approach.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(zero_title), FadeOut(zero_formula), FadeOut(zero_grid), FadeOut(problem_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Method 2: Random Initialization
        with self.voiceover(text="Next, Random initialization. Weights are drawn from a small random distribution like Gaussian or uniform. This breaks symmetry but can still cause issues if the variance is too large or small.") as tracker:
            random_title = Text("2. Random Initialization", font_size=32, color=ORANGE)
            random_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            random_formula = MathTex(r"W \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)", font_size=36)
            random_formula.next_to(random_title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            
            random_grid = VGroup()
            import random
            random.seed(42)
            for i in range(4):
                for j in range(4):
                    intensity = random.uniform(0.1, 0.9)
                    sq = Square(side_length=0.4, fill_color=interpolate_color(BLACK, WHITE, intensity), fill_opacity=1, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
                    sq.shift(RIGHT * j * 0.45 + DOWN * i * 0.45)
                    random_grid.add(sq)
            random_grid.next_to(random_formula, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            
            warning_text = Text("Variance must be tuned carefully!", font_size=22, color=ORANGE)
            warning_text.next_to(random_grid, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(random_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Write(random_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(FadeIn(random_grid), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(warning_text), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's look at more sophisticated methods.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(random_title), FadeOut(random_formula), FadeOut(random_grid), FadeOut(warning_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Method 3: Xavier Initialization
        with self.voiceover(text="Xavier, or Glorot initialization, scales weights based on the number of input neurons. The formula uses the square root of one over the fan-in. This maintains proper variance of activations across layers, ideal for sigmoid and tanh.") as tracker:
            xavier_title = Text("3. Xavier (Glorot) Initialization", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
            xavier_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            xavier_formula = MathTex(r"W \sim \mathcal{U}\left[-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{n_{in}+n_{out}}}, \frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{n_{in}+n_{out}}}\right]", font_size=28)
            xavier_formula.next_to(xavier_title, DOWN, buff=0.6)
            
            xavier_alt = MathTex(r"\text{or } W \sim \mathcal{N}\left(0, \frac{2}{n_{in}+n_{out}}\right)", font_size=28)
            xavier_alt.next_to(xavier_formula, DOWN, buff=0.3)
            
            use_case = Text("Best for: sigmoid, tanh activations", font_size=22, color=GREEN)
            use_case.next_to(xavier_alt, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(xavier_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Write(xavier_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(xavier_alt), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(use_case), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Now for the method optimized for ReLU.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(xavier_title), FadeOut(xavier_formula), FadeOut(xavier_alt), FadeOut(use_case), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Method 4: He Initialization
        with self.voiceover(text="He initialization is designed for ReLU activations. It uses a variance of two over the fan-in, accounting for the fact that ReLU zeros out half the inputs. This prevents the dying ReLU problem.") as tracker:
            he_title = Text("4. He Initialization", font_size=32, color=BLUE)
            he_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            he_formula = MathTex(r"W \sim \mathcal{N}\left(0, \frac{2}{n_{in}}\right)", font_size=32)
            he_formula.next_to(he_title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            
            he_uniform = MathTex(r"\text{or } W \sim \mathcal{U}\left[-\sqrt{\frac{6}{n_{in}}}, \sqrt{\frac{6}{n_{in}}}\right]", font_size=28)
            he_uniform.next_to(he_formula, DOWN, buff=0.4)
            
            use_case_he = Text("Best for: ReLU, LeakyReLU activations", font_size=22, color=BLUE)
            use_case_he.next_to(he_uniform, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(he_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Write(he_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(he_uniform), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(use_case_he), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let's visualize how these different initializations affect convergence in a loss landscape.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(he_title), FadeOut(he_formula), FadeOut(he_uniform), FadeOut(use_case_he), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Gradient Bowl Visualization
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine this bowl represents our loss surface. The bottom is the global minimum we want to reach. Each initialization starts at a different point on this surface.") as tracker:
            bowl_title = Text("Loss Landscape: The Gradient Bowl", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
            bowl_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)

            self.play(FadeIn(min_dot), Write(min_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Show different initialization paths

Xavier provides a balanced start for symmetric activations. He initialization works best for ReLU, quickly finding the minimum.") as tracker:
            # Zero path - gets stuck

from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService


class BackwardPassLogSoftmaxScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title
        title = Text("Backward Pass Through Log Softmax", font_size=40, color=BLUE)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="Imagine you're training a neural network to recognize cats and dogs. "
                 "You have a softmax function that provides probabilities for these classes. "
                 "But how do you adjust the weights during training when you deal with the log softmax? "
                 "Let's dive into this crucial concept!"
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Section 1: Understanding Softmax and Log Softmax
        section1_title = Text("1. Softmax vs Log Softmax", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        section1_title.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="First, let's understand the softmax and log softmax functions."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(section1_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Softmax formula
        softmax_formula = MathTex(
            r"\text{softmax}(x_i) = \frac{e^{x_i}}{\sum_{j} e^{x_j}}",
            font_size=36
        )
        softmax_formula.next_to(section1_title, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        softmax_label = Text("Softmax: Converts logits to probabilities", font_size=22, color=GRAY)
        softmax_label.next_to(softmax_formula, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="Softmax converts raw logits into probabilities that sum to one."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(Write(softmax_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(FadeIn(softmax_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Log Softmax formula
        log_softmax_formula = MathTex(
            r"\text{log\_softmax}(x_i) = x_i - \log\left(\sum_{j} e^{x_j}\right)",
            font_size=36
        )
        log_softmax_formula.next_to(softmax_label, DOWN, buff=0.6)
        log_softmax_label = Text("Log Softmax: Numerically stable log probabilities", font_size=22, color=GRAY)
        log_softmax_label.next_to(log_softmax_formula, DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(
            text="Log softmax is simply the logarithm of softmax. It provides better numerical stability "
                 "and is often used with negative log-likelihood loss in classification tasks."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(Write(log_softmax_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(FadeIn(log_softmax_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Clear for next section

            text="Now let's see why we need the backward pass."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(section1_title),
                FadeOut(softmax_formula),
                FadeOut(softmax_label),
                FadeOut(log_softmax_formula),
                FadeOut(log_softmax_label),
                run_time=tracker.duration
            )
        
        # Section 2: The Backward Pass

        section2_title.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        with self.voiceover(

                 "This is where the backward pass comes in."
        ) as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(section2_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
