messages.content: You are an expert mathematical animator and pedagogical engineer using Manim Community Edition and manim-voiceover with AOSSpeechService. Write executable, self-contained Python code that synchronizes mathematical animations with spoken educational explanations.
I'm teaching a model regularization module and want a visualization showing how batch normalization reduces reliance on dropout, with validation loss curves illustrating the regularizing effect.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService


class BatchNormalizationScene(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # ============================================
        # INTRODUCTION
        # ============================================
        
        title = Text("Batch Normalization & Regularization", font_size=40)
        subtitle = Text("Stabilizing Deep Neural Networks", font_size=28, color=BLUE)
        subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Welcome to this exciting lecture on Batch Normalization and Regularization!") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Have you ever wondered why some neural networks perform poorly while others shine brightly?") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The answer often lies in the methods we use to stabilize and improve our models. Today, we will dive into how these techniques can elevate your AI game!") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(title), FadeOut(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ============================================
        # PART 1: THE PROBLEM - INTERNAL COVARIATE SHIFT
        # ============================================
        
        problem_title = Text("The Problem: Internal Covariate Shift", font_size=32, color=RED)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="First, let us understand the problem. In deep neural networks, as training progresses, the distribution of each layer's inputs changes.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(problem_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.play(problem_title.animate.to_edge(UP), run_time=0.5)
        
        # Neural network diagram showing the problem
        input_layer = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.25, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(3)])
        hidden1 = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.25, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)])
        hidden2 = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.25, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)])
        output_layer = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.25, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(2)])
        
        input_layer.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3).shift(LEFT * 4)
        hidden1.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3).shift(LEFT * 1.5)
        hidden2.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3).shift(RIGHT * 1)
        output_layer.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3).shift(RIGHT * 3.5)
        
        # Labels
        input_label = Text("Input", font_size=18).next_to(input_layer, DOWN)
        h1_label = Text("Layer 1", font_size=18).next_to(hidden1, DOWN)
        h2_label = Text("Layer 2", font_size=18).next_to(hidden2, DOWN)
        out_label = Text("Output", font_size=18).next_to(output_layer, DOWN)
        
        nn_group = VGroup(input_layer, hidden1, hidden2, output_layer, 
                         input_label, h1_label, h2_label, out_label)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This phenomenon is called internal covariate shift. Each layer must continuously adapt to new distributions, slowing down training.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(input_layer), Create(hidden1), Create(hidden2), Create(output_layer), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.play(Write(input_label), Write(h1_label), Write(h2_label), Write(out_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        # Draw connections
        connections = VGroup()
        for il in input_layer:
            for h1 in hidden1:
                connections.add(Line(il.get_right(), h1.get_left(), stroke_width=1, color=GRAY))
        for h1 in hidden1:
            for h2 in hidden2:
                connections.add(Line(h1.get_right(), h2.get_left(), stroke_width=1, color=GRAY))
        for h2 in hidden2:
            for ol in output_layer:
                connections.add(Line(h2.get_right(), ol.get_left(), stroke_width=1, color=GRAY))
        
        with self.voiceover(text="As data flows through layers, distributions shift, making it harder for subsequent layers to learn effectively.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(connections), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Show distribution shift visualization
        shift_text = Text("Distribution Shifts → Slow Training", font_size=22, color=ORANGE)
        shift_text.next_to(nn_group, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This requires lower learning rates and careful initialization, making training slower and less stable.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(shift_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="So how do we solve this? Enter Batch Normalization!") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(nn_group), FadeOut(connections), FadeOut(shift_text), FadeOut(problem_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ============================================
        # PART 2: BATCH NORMALIZATION FORMULA
        # ============================================
        
        bn_title = Text("Batch Normalization: The Solution", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
        bn_title.to_edge(UP)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Batch Normalization normalizes the inputs to each layer, stabilizing the learning process.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(bn_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Step 1: Compute Batch Mean
        mean_formula = MathTex(r"\mu_B = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} x_i")
        mean_formula.shift(UP * 1.5)
        mean_label = Text("Step 1: Calculate batch mean", font_size=20, color=BLUE).next_to(mean_formula, DOWN)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Step one: we calculate the mean of the current batch.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(mean_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.play(FadeIn(mean_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        # Step 2: Compute Batch Variance
        var_formula = MathTex(r"\sigma_B^2 = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} (x_i - \mu_B)^2")
        var_formula.next_to(mean_formula, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        var_label = Text("Step 2: Calculate batch variance", font_size=20, color=BLUE).next_to(var_formula, DOWN)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Step two: we calculate the variance of the batch.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(var_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.play(FadeIn(var_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        # Step 3: Normalize
        norm_formula = MathTex(r"\hat{x}_i = \frac{x_i - \mu_B}{\sqrt{\sigma_B^2 + \epsilon}}")
        norm_formula.next_to(var_formula, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        norm_label = Text("Step 3: Normalize", font_size=20, color=BLUE).next_to(norm_formula, DOWN)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Step three: we normalize each input by subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(norm_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.play(FadeIn(norm_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        # Step 4: Scale and Shift
        scale_formula = MathTex(r"y_i = \gamma \hat{x}_i + \beta")
        scale_formula.next_to(norm_formula, DOWN, buff=0.8)
        scale_label = Text("Step 4: Scale and shift with learnable parameters", font_size=20, color=BLUE).next_to(scale_formula, DOWN)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Finally, we apply learnable scale and shift parameters, gamma and beta, allowing the network to undo normalization if needed.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(scale_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.play(FadeIn(scale_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        formula_group = VGroup(mean_formula, mean_label, var_formula, var_label, 
                              norm_formula, norm_label, scale_formula, scale_label)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="These four steps form the complete batch normalization process.") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let us see the benefits!") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(formula_group), FadeOut(bn_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ============================================
        # PART 3: BENEFITS OF BATCH NORMALIZATION
        # ============================================
        
        benefits_title = Text("Benefits of Batch Normalization", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
        benefits_title.to_edge(UP)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Batch Normalization provides several key benefits to neural network training.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(benefits_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Create benefit items
        benefits = VGroup(
            Text("✓ Enables higher learning rates", font_size=22),
            Text("✓ Reduces internal covariate shift", font_size=22),
            Text("✓ Acts as a regularizer", font_size=22),
            Text("✓ Makes training faster and more stable", font_size=22),
            Text("✓ Reduces dependence on initialization", font_size=22)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        benefits.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="First, it enables higher learning rates, speeding up convergence.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(benefits[0]), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="It directly addresses internal covariate shift.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(benefits[1]), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Interestingly, it also acts as a regularizer, reducing overfitting slightly.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(benefits[2]), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Training becomes faster and more stable overall.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(benefits[3]), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="And finally, it reduces the network's sensitivity to weight initialization.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeIn(benefits[4]), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Now, let us transition to another crucial technique: Regularization.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(benefits), FadeOut(benefits_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ============================================
        # PART 4: REGULARIZATION
        # ============================================
        
        reg_title = Text("Regularization: Combating Overfitting", font_size=32, color=PURPLE)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Regularization techniques help prevent overfitting, where models perform well on training data but poorly on new data.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(reg_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.play(reg_title.animate.to_edge(UP), run_time=0.5)
        
        # Overfitting visualization
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 10, 1],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            x_length=6,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        axes_labels = axes.get_axis_labels(x_label="Epochs", y_label="Error")
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Consider this typical overfitting scenario.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(axes), Write(axes_labels), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Training error - goes down
        train_error = axes.plot(lambda x: 5 * np.exp(-x/3) + 0.5, x_range=[0, 10], color=GREEN)
        train_label = Text("Training Error", font_size=18, color=GREEN).next_to(axes.c2p(8, 1), RIGHT)
        
        # Validation error - goes up after some point
        val_error = axes.plot(lambda x: 5 * np.exp(-x/3) + 0.5 + 0.3 * x, x_range=[0, 10], color=RED)
        val_label = Text("Validation Error", font_size=18, color=RED).next_to(axes.c2p(8, 4), RIGHT)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The training error keeps decreasing, but validation error starts increasing after a certain point.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(train_error), Write(train_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(Create(val_error), Write(val_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        overfit_text = Text("Overfitting Zone →", font_size=20, color=RED)
        overfit_arrow = Arrow(axes.c2p(6, 0), axes.c2p(8, 0), color=RED)
        overfit_group = VGroup(overfit_text, overfit_arrow)
        overfit_group.next_to(axes, DOWN)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This gap indicates overfitting. The model memorizes training data instead of learning general patterns.") as tracker:
            self.play(GrowArrow(overfit_arrow), Write(overfit_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Regularization helps reduce this gap. Let us explore the main techniques.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(axes_labels), FadeOut(train_error), FadeOut(train_label),
                     FadeOut(val_error), FadeOut(val_label), FadeOut(overfit_group), 
                     FadeOut(reg_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ============================================
        # PART 5: REGULARIZATION TECHNIQUES
        # ============================================
        
        techniques_title = Text("Regularization Techniques", font_size=32, color=PURPLE)
        techniques_title.to_edge(UP)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here are the most common regularization techniques used in deep learning.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(techniques_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # L1 and L2 Regularization
        l1_title = Text("L1 Regularization (Lasso)", font_size=24, color=BLUE).shift(UP * 1.5 + LEFT * 3)
        l1_formula = MathTex(r"L_{reg} = L + \lambda \sum |w_i|").scale(0.9).next_to(l1_title, DOWN)
        l1_desc = Text("Encourages sparsity", font_size=18).next_to(l1_formula, DOWN)
        
        l2_title = Text("L2 Regularization (Ridge)", font_size=24, color=BLUE).shift(UP * 1.5 + RIGHT * 3)
        l2_formula = MathTex(r"L_{reg} = L + \lambda \sum w_i^2").scale(0.9).next_to(l2_title, DOWN)
        l2_desc = Text("Penalizes large weights", font_size=18).next_to(l2_formula, DOWN)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="First, L1 and L2 regularization add penalty terms to the loss function based on weight magnitudes.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(l1_title), Write(l2_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Write(l1_formula), Write(l2_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Write(l1_desc), Write(l2_desc), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
        
        # Dropout
        dropout_title = Text("Dropout", font_size=24, color=ORANGE).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        dropout_desc = Text("Randomly drops neurons during training", font_size=20).next_to(dropout_title, DOWN)
        dropout_rate = MathTex(r"\text{Dropout Rate} = 0.5").next_to(dropout_desc, DOWN)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Dropout randomly deactivates neurons during training, preventing co-adaptation and forcing robust feature learning.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(dropout_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(dropout_desc), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.4)
            self.play(Write(dropout_rate), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        # Early Stopping
        early_title = Text("Early Stopping", font_size=24, color=GREEN).shift(DOWN * 2.5)
        early_desc = Text("Stop training when validation loss stops improving", font_size=20).next_to(early_title, DOWN)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Early stopping monitors validation performance and halts training before overfitting begins.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(early_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(early_desc), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
        
        reg_group = VGroup(l1_title, l1_formula, l1_desc, l2_title, l2_formula, l2_desc,
                          dropout_title, dropout_desc, dropout_rate, early_title, early_desc)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="These techniques, when combined, create more generalizable models.") as tracker:
            self.wait(tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let us see how to implement these in TensorFlow.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(reg_group), FadeOut(techniques_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ============================================
        # PART 6: TENSORFLOW IMPLEMENTATION
        # ============================================
        
        code_title = Text("TensorFlow Implementation", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        code_title.to_edge(UP)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here is how you can implement batch normalization and regularization in TensorFlow and Keras.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(code_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
```

```python
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Why do some weights seem to stick, while others shift dramatically during learning?") as tracker:
            subtitle = Text("Why do some weights get stuck while others shift?", font_size=24, color=GRAY)
            subtitle.next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.3)
            self.play(FadeIn(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="In this lecture, we will dive into the fascinating concept of hook behavior, where specific patterns in weight changes can influence the performance of your neural networks.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(subtitle), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        # ============================================
        # NEURAL NETWORK VISUALIZATION
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's start with a simple neural network. We have input neurons, hidden layers, and output neurons, all connected by weights.") as tracker:
            # Create neurons as circles
            input_layer = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.25, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3) for _ in range(3)])
            hidden_layer = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.25, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.3) for _ in range(4)])
            output_layer = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.25, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.3) for _ in range(2)])
            
            input_layer.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.6)
            hidden_layer.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
            output_layer.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.8)
            
            input_layer.shift(LEFT * 4)
            hidden_layer.shift(LEFT * 1)
            output_layer.shift(RIGHT * 2)
            
            # Labels
            input_label = Text("Input", font_size=20, color=BLUE).next_to(input_layer, LEFT)
            hidden_label = Text("Hidden", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(hidden_layer, UP, buff=0.3)
            output_label = Text("Output", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(output_layer, RIGHT)
            
            self.play(
                FadeOut(title),
                Create(input_layer),
                Create(hidden_layer), 
                Create(output_layer),
                Write(input_label),
                Write(hidden_label),
                Write(output_label),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.8
            )
        
        # Create weight connections
        with self.voiceover(text="These connections carry weights. During training, these weights update to minimize error.") as tracker:
            weights_ih = VGroup()
            for inp in input_layer:
                for hid in hidden_layer:
                    line = Line(inp.get_right(), hid.get_left(), color=YELLOW, stroke_width=1.5)
                    weights_ih.add(line)
            
            weights_ho = VGroup()
            for hid in hidden_layer:
                for out in output_layer:
                    line = Line(hid.get_right(), out.get_left(), color=ORANGE, stroke_width=1.5)
                    weights_ho.add(line)
            
            self.play(Create(weights_ih), Create(weights_ho), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        network_group = VGroup(input_layer, hidden_layer, output_layer, 
                               weights_ih, weights_ho, input_label, hidden_label, output_label)
        
        # ============================================
        # HOOK BEHAVIOR DEMONSTRATION
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(text="But here is where hook behavior emerges. Some weights, shown in red, become stuck and barely change, while others, in bright yellow, shift dramatically.") as tracker:
            # Highlight some stuck weights (red, thin) and shifting weights (bright yellow, thick)
            stuck_weights = VGroup(*weights_ih[:4])
            shifting_weights = VGroup(*weights_ih[4:8])
            
            self.play(
                stuck_weights.animate.set_color(RED).set_stroke_width(3),
                shifting_weights.animate.set_color(YELLOW).set_stroke_width(4),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7
            )
        
        with self.voiceover(text="These stuck weights are hooked. They resist updates due to poor initialization or vanishing gradients, limiting the network's ability to learn.") as tracker:
            hook_text = Text("Hooked Weights", font_size=24, color=RED)
            hook_text.next_to(network_group, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            self.play(Write(hook_text), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.4)
        
        # ============================================
        # WEIGHT DISTRIBUTION
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(text="To understand this better, let's look at weight distributions. A healthy distribution is centered around zero with reasonable variance.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(network_group),
                FadeOut(hook_text),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3
            )
            
            # Draw axes for distribution
            axes = Axes(
                x_range=[-3, 3, 1],

        with self.voiceover(text="But with hook behavior, weights cluster at extremes. Some get stuck near zero, others saturate at high magnitudes, creating an unhealthy U-shaped distribution.") as tracker:
            # U-shaped distribution (hooked)

            self.play(Write(dist_label), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ============================================
        # OPTIMIZATION IMPACT
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let's see how initialization and optimization affect hook behavior.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(axes),
                FadeOut(x_label),
                FadeOut(y_label),
                FadeOut(normal_curve),
                FadeOut(dist_label),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3
            )
            
            # Create comparison boxes
            bad_init_box = Rectangle(width=3, height=3.5, color=RED)
            good_init_box = Rectangle(width=3, height=3.5, color=GREEN)
            
            bad_init_box.shift(LEFT * 2)

            bad_label = Text("Poor Init", font_size=20, color=RED).next_to(bad_init_box, UP, buff=0.2)
            good_label = Text("Proper Init", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(good_init_box, UP, buff=0.2)
            
            self.play(
                Create(bad_init_box),
                Create(good_init_box),

            )
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Poor initialization leads to many hooked weights, shown as tangled red lines, limiting information flow through the network.") as tracker:
            # Draw tangled lines in bad init box
            bad_lines = VGroup()
            for i in range(8):
                start = bad_init_box.get_center() + LEFT * 1 + UP * (1.2 - i * 0.35)
                end = bad_init_box.get_center() + RIGHT * 1 + UP * (1.2 - i * 0.35) + DOWN * 0.3 * (i % 3)
                line = Line(start, end, color=RED, stroke_width=2)
                bad_lines.add(line)
            
            self.play(Create(bad_lines), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Proper initialization, like Xavier or He initialization, creates balanced weights that update smoothly during training, avoiding hook behavior.") as tracker:
            # Draw clean lines in good init box
            good_lines = VGroup()
            for i in range(8):
                start = good_init_box.get_center() + LEFT * 1 + UP * (1.2 - i * 0.35)
                end = good_init_box.get_center() + RIGHT * 1 + UP * (1.2 - i * 0.35)

                good_lines.add(line)
            
            self.play(Create(good_lines), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # ============================================
        # LEARNING OUTCOMES
        # ============================================
        with self.voiceover(text="Let's summarize the key insights.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(bad_init_box),
                FadeOut(good_init_box),
                FadeOut(bad_label),
                FadeOut(good_label),
                FadeOut(bad_lines),
                FadeOut(good_lines),
                run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5
            )
        
        with self.voiceover(text="First, weight distribution directly affects training. A normal distribution around zero promotes healthy learning.") as tracker:
            takeaway1 = Text("1. Weight distribution affects training", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
            takeaway1.to_edge(UP, buff=1)
            self.play(Write(takeaway1), run_time=tracker.duration)
```

messages.content: You are an expert mathematical animator and pedagogical engineer using Manim Community Edition and manim-voiceover with AOSSpeechService. Write executable, self-contained Python code that synchronizes mathematical animations with spoken educational explanations.

I'm studying BN and want to visualize the forward pass of a BN layer with a mini-batch of 4 samples. Animate each sample's path through mean/variance estimation, scaling, and shifting by gamma/beta, then show the resulting outputs and a summary of batch statistics.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class BatchNormalizationForwardPass(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Title
        with self.voiceover(text="Have you ever wondered how deep learning models stabilize their training process and achieve faster convergence? Batch normalization is a key player in this game!") as tracker:
            title = Text("Batch Normalization", font_size=48, color=BLUE)
            subtitle = Text("Forward Pass Visualization", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
            title_group = VGroup(title, subtitle).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
            self.play(Write(title_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Buckle up, because in this lecture, you will dive into the intricacies of how batch normalization works during the forward pass and witness its powerful effects firsthand!") as tracker:
            self.play(title_group.animate.scale(0.6).to_edge(UP), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        # Setup - Input batch data visualization
        with self.voiceover(text="Lets begin by understanding what batch normalization does. Imagine we have a mini-batch of activation values from a neural network layer.") as tracker:
            batch_label = Text("Input Batch (m samples):", font_size=24, color=YELLOW).to_edge(LEFT).shift(UP * 2)
            self.play(FadeIn(batch_label), run_time=0.5)
            
            # Create sample data points (bars representing activations)
            sample_values = [2.5, 1.8, 3.2, -0.5, 2.0, 1.2, 3.5, -1.0]
            bars = VGroup()
            bar_labels = VGroup()
            
            for i, val in enumerate(sample_values):
                bar = Rectangle(
                    height=abs(val) * 0.4,
                    width=0.4,
                    color=BLUE if val >= 0 else RED,
                    fill_opacity=0.7
                ).shift(DOWN * 0.5 + RIGHT * (i - 3.5) * 0.6 + UP * (val * 0.2 if val >= 0 else 0))
                
                label = MathTex(f"x_{{{i+1}}}", font_size=20).next_to(bar, DOWN, buff=0.1)
                bars.add(bar)
                bar_labels.add(label)
            
            self.play(*[GrowFromCenter(bar) for bar in bars], 
                     *[FadeIn(label) for label in bar_labels],
                     run_time=tracker.duration - 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 1: Calculate Mean
        with self.voiceover(text="First, we compute the mean of the batch. This tells us where the center of our data lies.") as tracker:
            mean_formula = MathTex(r"\mu = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} x_i", font_size=28, color=GREEN)
            mean_formula.next_to(batch_label, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            self.play(Write(mean_formula), run_time=1.0)
            
            # Show mean line
            mean_value = sum(sample_values) / len(sample_values)
            mean_line = DashedLine(LEFT * 4, RIGHT * 4, color=GREEN, dash_length=0.1)
            mean_line.shift(UP * mean_value * 0.4 + DOWN * 0.5)
            mean_label = MathTex(f"\mu = {mean_value:.2f}", font_size=20, color=GREEN).next_to(mean_line, RIGHT)
            
            self.play(Create(mean_line), FadeIn(mean_label), run_time=tracker.duration - 1.0)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 2: Calculate Variance
        with self.voiceover(text="Next, we calculate the variance to understand how spread out our data is from the mean.") as tracker:
            var_formula = MathTex(r"\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} (x_i - \mu)^2", font_size=28, color=ORANGE)
            var_formula.next_to(mean_formula, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            self.play(Write(var_formula), run_time=1.0)
            
            # Show variance visualization
            variance = sum((x - mean_value) ** 2 for x in sample_values) / len(sample_values)
            var_text = MathTex(f"\sigma^2 = {variance:.2f}", font_size=20, color=ORANGE).next_to(var_formula, RIGHT)
            self.play(FadeIn(var_text), run_time=tracker.duration - 1.0)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Clear and move to normalization
        with self.voiceover(text="Now comes the crucial step: normalization. We center the data by subtracting the mean, and scale it by dividing by the standard deviation.") as tracker:
            self.play(
                FadeOut(bars), FadeOut(bar_labels), FadeOut(mean_line), 
                FadeOut(mean_label), FadeOut(batch_label), FadeOut(var_text),
                mean_formula.animate.scale(0.7).to_corner(UL).shift(DOWN * 0.5),
                var_formula.animate.scale(0.7).next_to(mean_formula, DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT),
                run_time=0.8
            )
            
            norm_formula = MathTex(r"\hat{x}_i = \frac{x_i - \mu}{\sqrt{\sigma^2 + \epsilon}}", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
            norm_formula.move_to(ORIGIN + UP * 1.5)
            self.play(Write(norm_formula), run_time=tracker.duration - 0.8)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Visualization of before and after
        with self.voiceover(text="Watch how this transforms our data. On the left is the original distribution with its spread, and on the right is the normalized version.") as tracker:
            norm_formula_scaled = norm_formula.copy().scale(0.7).to_corner(UR).shift(DOWN * 0.5 + LEFT * 0.3)
            self.play(Transform(norm_formula, norm_formula_scaled), run_time=0.5)
            
            # Before distribution
            before_label = Text("Before:", font_size=22, color=BLUE).shift(LEFT * 3.5 + UP * 0.5)
            before_bars = VGroup()
            for i, val in enumerate(sample_values[:4]):
                bar = Rectangle(
                    height=abs(val) * 0.5 + 0.1,
                    width=0.5,
                    color=BLUE,
                    fill_opacity=0.6
                ).shift(LEFT * 4 + RIGHT * i * 0.7 + UP * (val * 0.25 if val >= 0 else -val * 0.25))
                before_bars.add(bar)
            
            # After normalization
            after_label = Text("After:", font_size=22, color=GREEN).shift(RIGHT * 1.5 + UP * 0.5)
            after_bars = VGroup()
            normalized_values = [(x - mean_value) / ((variance + 1e-8) ** 0.5) for x in sample_values[:4]]
            for i, val in enumerate(normalized_values):
                bar = Rectangle(
                    height=abs(val) * 0.5 + 0.1,
                    width=0.5,
                    color=GREEN,
                    fill_opacity=0.6
                ).shift(RIGHT * 1 + RIGHT * i * 0.7 + UP * (val * 0.25 if val >= 0 else -val * 0.25))
                after_bars.add(bar)
            
            arrow = Arrow(LEFT * 1.5, RIGHT * 0.5, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
            arrow_label = MathTex(r"\frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(arrow, UP, buff=0.1)
            
            self.play(FadeIn(before_label), FadeIn(before_bars), run_time=0.6)
            self.play(Create(arrow), FadeIn(arrow_label), run_time=0.5)
            self.play(FadeIn(after_label), FadeIn(after_bars), run_time=tracker.duration - 1.6)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 4: Scale and Shift
        with self.voiceover(text="But normalization alone would restrict our network. So we add learnable parameters gamma and beta to scale and shift the normalized values.") as tracker:
            # Clear previous visualization
            self.play(
                FadeOut(before_label), FadeOut(before_bars), FadeOut(after_label), 
                FadeOut(after_bars), FadeOut(arrow), FadeOut(arrow_label),
                run_time=0.5
            )
            
            affine_formula = MathTex(r"y_i = \gamma \hat{x}_i + \beta", font_size=32, color=PURPLE)
            affine_formula.move_to(ORIGIN + UP * 1)
            self.play(Write(affine_formula), run_time=tracker.duration - 0.5)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Visual summary
        with self.voiceover(text="This gives the network flexibility to learn the optimal distribution for each layer while maintaining stable training.") as tracker:
            # Move formulas to show complete pipeline
            step1 = Text(r"1. Compute Mean \& Variance", font_size=20, color=GREEN).shift(LEFT * 4 + UP * 1)
            step2 = Text("2. Normalize", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).shift(UP * 1)
            step3 = Text(r"3. Scale \& Shift", font_size=20, color=PURPLE).shift(RIGHT * 4 + UP * 1)
            
            arrows = VGroup(
                Arrow(step1.get_right(), step2.get_left(), buff=0.2, color=WHITE),
                Arrow(step2.get_right(), step3.get_left(), buff=0.2, color=WHITE)
            )
            
            self.play(FadeIn(step1), FadeIn(step2), FadeIn(step3), run_time=0.6)
            self.play(*[Create(arrow) for arrow in arrows], run_time=tracker.duration - 0.6)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Benefits summary
        with self.voiceover(text="Batch normalization reduces internal covariate shift, allows higher learning rates, and acts as a regularizer. This leads to faster convergence and improved model performance.") as tracker:
            benefits = VGroup(
                Text("-- Faster Training", font_size=18, color=GREEN),
                Text("-- Higher Learning Rates", font_size=18, color=GREEN),
                Text("-- Reduced Internal Shift", font_size=18, color=GREEN),
                Text("-- Regularization Effect", font_size=18, color=GREEN)
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
            benefits.shift(DOWN * 1.5)
            
            self.play(*[FadeIn(benefit) for benefit in benefits], run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Summary
        with self.voiceover(text="You now understand the mechanics of batch normalization: computing statistics, normalizing, and then scaling and shifting. This technique has become a cornerstone of modern deep learning architectures.") as tracker:
            summary = Text("Batch Normalization: Stable | Fast | Effective", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
            summary.shift(DOWN * 2.5)
            self.play(Write(summary), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(1)
```

I'm teaching undergrads ML and want to compare three learning rates on a shared loss landscape. Show 0.001, 0.01, and 0.1 paths starting from the same initial point, highlighting divergence, optimal convergence, and slow progress, with a side-by-side panel of the loss vs steps.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class LearningRateComparison(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # === TITLE SECTION ===
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine training a machine learning model and realizing it takes too long to converge, or fails completely. The learning rate plays a crucial role in your model's ability to learn effectively.") as tracker:
            title = Text("Comparing Learning Rates", font_size=48, color=BLUE)
            subtitle = Text("in Machine Learning", font_size=32, color=GRAY)
            title_group = VGroup(title, subtitle).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
            self.play(Write(title_group), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="What happens if you choose a rate that's too high or too low? Let's uncover the secrets of learning rates in this lecture!") as tracker:
            question = Text("Too high? Too low? Let's find out!", font_size=28, color=YELLOW)
            question.next_to(title_group, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            self.play(FadeIn(question), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(title_group), FadeOut(question))
        
        # === COST FUNCTION SECTION ===
        with self.voiceover(text="First, let's recall the cost function. It measures how far our predictions are from the actual values. We want to minimize this.") as tracker:
            cost_title = Text("Cost Function", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            cost_title.to_edge(UP)
            
            cost_formula = MathTex(r"J(\theta) = \frac{1}{2m} \sum_{i=1}^{m} (h_\theta(x^{(i)}) - y^{(i)})^2", font_size=32)
            cost_formula.next_to(cost_title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            self.play(Write(cost_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
            self.play(Write(cost_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(cost_title), FadeOut(cost_formula))
        
        # === GRADIENT DESCENT SECTION ===
        with self.voiceover(text="Gradient descent updates our parameters by moving in the direction opposite to the gradient. The learning rate alpha controls how big each step is.") as tracker:
            gd_title = Text("Gradient Descent Update", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            gd_title.to_edge(UP)
            
            gd_formula = MathTex(r"\theta := \theta - \alpha \nabla J(\theta)", font_size=40)
            gd_formula.next_to(gd_title, DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            # Highlight alpha
            alpha_box = SurroundingRectangle(gd_formula[0][7:8], color=YELLOW, buff=0.1)
            
            self.play(Write(gd_title), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
            self.play(Write(gd_formula), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(Create(alpha_box), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(gd_title), FadeOut(gd_formula), FadeOut(alpha_box))
        
        # === VISUALIZATION SECTION ===
        with self.voiceover(text="Now let's visualize what happens with different learning rates. We'll use a simple convex cost function.") as tracker:
            # Create axes
            axes = Axes(
                x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
                y_range=[0, 5, 1],
                axis_config={"include_tip": False, "include_numbers": True},
                x_length=10,
                y_length=5
            )
            axes.to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            x_label = MathTex(r"\theta", font_size=24).next_to(axes.x_axis, RIGHT)
            y_label = MathTex(r"J(\theta)", font_size=24).next_to(axes.y_axis, UP)
            
            # Cost function: a simple parabola
            graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, color=WHITE, x_range=[-3, 3])
            
            self.play(Create(axes), Write(x_label), Write(y_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
            self.play(Create(graph), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.5)
        
        # === SMALL LEARNING RATE ===
        with self.voiceover(text="With a very small learning rate, we take tiny steps. We eventually reach the minimum, but it takes many iterations. This is slow convergence.") as tracker:
            # Starting point
            start_x = 2.5
            small_lr = 0.3
            
            small_label = Text("Small α = 0.3", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
            small_label.to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)
            self.play(Write(small_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.1)
            
            # Starting dot
            current_x = start_x
            dot = Dot(axes.c2p(current_x, 0.5 * current_x**2), color=GREEN, radius=0.1)
            self.play(FadeIn(dot), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.1)
            
            # Animate gradient descent steps
            for i in range(6):
                gradient = current_x  # derivative of 0.5*x^2 is x
                next_x = current_x - small_lr * gradient
                next_y = 0.5 * next_x**2
                
                if abs(next_x) > 3:
                    break
                
                next_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(next_x, next_y), color=GREEN, radius=0.1)
                arrow = Arrow(axes.c2p(current_x, 0.5 * current_x**2), 
                             axes.c2p(next_x, next_y), 
                             buff=0.1, color=GREEN, stroke_width=2)
                
                self.play(Create(arrow), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.1)
                self.play(Transform(dot, next_dot), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.1)
                
                current_x = next_x
            
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(small_label), FadeOut(dot))
        
        # === OPTIMAL LEARNING RATE ===
        with self.voiceover(text="With an optimal learning rate, we converge quickly and smoothly to the minimum. This is the sweet spot we aim for.") as tracker:
            current_x = start_x
            optimal_lr = 0.8
            
            optimal_label = Text("Optimal α = 0.8", font_size=24, color=BLUE)
            optimal_label.to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)
            self.play(Write(optimal_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.1)
            
            dot = Dot(axes.c2p(current_x, 0.5 * current_x**2), color=BLUE, radius=0.1)
            self.play(FadeIn(dot), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.1)
            
            for i in range(4):
                gradient = current_x
                next_x = current_x - optimal_lr * gradient
                next_y = 0.5 * next_x**2
                
                if abs(next_x) > 3:
                    break
                
                next_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(next_x, next_y), color=BLUE, radius=0.1)
                arrow = Arrow(axes.c2p(current_x, 0.5 * current_x**2), 
                             axes.c2p(next_x, next_y), 
                             buff=0.1, color=BLUE, stroke_width=2)
                
                self.play(Create(arrow), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.15)
                self.play(Transform(dot, next_dot), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.15)
                
                current_x = next_x
            
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(optimal_label), FadeOut(dot))
        
        # === LARGE LEARNING RATE ===
        with self.voiceover(text="But with a learning rate that's too large, we overshoot the minimum. The steps are so big that we bounce around, possibly diverging entirely.") as tracker:
            current_x = start_x
            large_lr = 1.5
            
            large_label = Text("Large α = 1.5 (Diverges!)", font_size=24, color=RED)
            large_label.to_edge(UP, buff=0.3)
            self.play(Write(large_label), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.1)
            
            dot = Dot(axes.c2p(current_x, 0.5 * current_x**2), color=RED, radius=0.1)
            self.play(FadeIn(dot), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.1)
            
            for i in range(4):
                gradient = current_x
                next_x = current_x - large_lr * gradient
                next_y = 0.5 * next_x**2
                
                next_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(next_x, next_y), color=RED, radius=0.1)
                arrow = Arrow(axes.c2p(current_x, 0.5 * current_x**2), 
                             axes.c2p(next_x, next_y), 
                             buff=0.1, color=RED, stroke_width=2)
                
                self.play(Create(arrow), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.15)
                self.play(Transform(dot, next_dot), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.15)
                
                current_x = next_x
                
                if abs(current_x) > 3:
                    # Show divergence
                    explosion = Text("DIVERGES!", font_size=36, color=RED)
                    explosion.next_to(dot, RIGHT)
                    self.play(Write(explosion), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.2)
                    break
            
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(large_label), FadeOut(dot), FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(x_label), FadeOut(y_label), FadeOut(graph))
        
        # === SUMMARY SECTION ===
        with self.voiceover(text="To summarize: a small learning rate gives slow but stable convergence. An optimal rate converges quickly. And a large rate causes overshooting and divergence.") as tracker:
            summary_title = Text("Key Takeaways", font_size=40, color=BLUE)
            summary_title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
            
            # Two column layout for takeaways
            left_col = VGroup(
                Text("Small α:", font_size=24, color=GREEN),
                Text("Slow, stable", font_size=20, color=WHITE),
                Text("Many iterations", font_size=20, color=GRAY)
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
            
            middle_col = VGroup(
                Text("Optimal α:", font_size=24, color=BLUE),
                Text("Fast, smooth", font_size=20, color=WHITE),
                Text("Quick convergence", font_size=20, color=GRAY)
            ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
            
            right_col = VGroup(
                Text("Large α:", font_size=24, color=RED),
                Text("Overshooting", font_size=20, color=WHITE),
```

I’m learning about long-range dependencies in sequences and want to visualize the required context size for matching parentheses.
Animate a nested parenthesis string and show how many preceding tokens are needed to correctly pair each opening with its closing symbol.
Use a sliding window with a toggle to vary context length and show success/failure of matching in real time.
Add an intuition panel explaining how depth grows context requirements and how different models would cope.

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class LongRangeDependencies(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # Opening title
        with self.voiceover(text="Imagine reading a novel -- the storyline often references events that happened many pages earlier.") as tracker:
            title = Text("Long Range Dependencies in Sequences", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            self.play(Write(title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Just as you need to recall past information to grasp the plot fully, AI models also need to learn from long-range dependencies within sequences.") as tracker:
            self.play(title.animate.scale(0.6).to_edge(UP), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        # Book analogy visualization
        with self.voiceover(text="Think about this sentence: The cat sat on the mat. It was happy.") as tracker:
            # Create book page representation
            page = Rectangle(width=8, height=5, color=WHITE, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=0.7)
            page.to_edge(DOWN, buff=0.5)
            
            sentence_text = Text('"The cat sat on the mat. It was happy."', font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
            sentence_text.move_to(page.get_center())
            
            self.play(Create(page), FadeIn(sentence_text), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="To understand what It refers to, we need to connect back to cat -- a dependency spanning several words.") as tracker:
            self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Transition to sequence dependency view
        with self.voiceover(text="This is the challenge of long-range dependencies in sequences.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(page), FadeOut(sentence_text), FadeOut(title), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        # Sequence visualization with connections
        with self.voiceover(text="In sequence modeling, tokens or words need to influence each other over long distances.") as tracker:
            new_title = Text("Sequence Dependencies", font_size=28, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP)
            self.play(Write(new_title), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        tokens = ["The", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat", ".", "It", "was", "happy", "."]
        token_mobjects = []
        token_boxes = []
        token_texts = []
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Here is a sequence of words. The word It at position eight depends on cat at position two -- that is a six-word gap.") as tracker:
            for i, token in enumerate(tokens):
                box = Square(side_length=0.6, color=WHITE)
                if i == 1:
                    box.set_color(GREEN)
                elif i == 7:
                    box.set_color(RED)
                box.shift(RIGHT * (i - len(tokens)/2) * 0.8 + UP * 0.5)
                text = Text(token, font_size=14).move_to(box.get_center())
                token_boxes.append(box)
                token_texts.append(text)
                token_mobjects.append(VGroup(box, text))
            
            self.play(*[Create(box) for box in token_boxes], *[Write(t) for t in token_texts], run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="This long-range connection is crucial for understanding context in language.") as tracker:
            connection = CurvedArrow(token_boxes[1].get_top() + UP*0.1, token_boxes[7].get_top() + UP*0.1, angle=-1.5, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=3)
            self.play(Create(connection), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # RNN Challenge section
        with self.voiceover(text="Traditional recurrent neural networks, or RNNs, process sequences step by step.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(*token_mobjects), FadeOut(connection), FadeOut(new_title), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="They pass information from one time step to the next, but struggle to maintain connections over long distances.") as tracker:
            rnn_title = Text("The RNN Challenge", font_size=28, color=RED).to_edge(UP)
            self.play(Write(rnn_title), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        hidden_states = []
        rnn_arrows = []
        num_steps = 8
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Each step in an RNN maintains a hidden state that should carry information forward.") as tracker:
            for i in range(num_steps):
                circle = Circle(radius=0.25, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
                circle.shift(LEFT * 2.8 + RIGHT * i * 0.7 + DOWN * 0.5)
                h_label = MathTex(r"h_{{" + str(i+1) + r"}}", font_size=16).move_to(circle.get_center())
                hs_group = VGroup(circle, h_label)
                hidden_states.append(hs_group)
            
            for i in range(num_steps - 1):
                arrow = Arrow(hidden_states[i][0].get_right(), hidden_states[i+1][0].get_left(), buff=0.1, color=BLUE)
                rnn_arrows.append(arrow)
            
            self.play(*[Create(hs) for hs in hidden_states], run_time=tracker.duration/2)
            self.play(*[Create(arr) for arr in rnn_arrows], run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="But information gets diluted across many steps. This is called the vanishing gradient problem.") as tracker:
            fade_anims = [hidden_states[i].animate.set_opacity(0.3) for i in range(3)]
            fade_anims += [rnn_arrows[i].animate.set_opacity(0.15) for i in range(3)]
            self.play(*fade_anims, run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="By the time we reach step eight, the information about the early steps has nearly vanished.") as tracker:
            self.play(hidden_states[0].animate.set_opacity(0.1), hidden_states[1].animate.set_opacity(0.1), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Solutions section
        with self.voiceover(text="Modern AI has developed solutions to better capture long-range dependencies.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(*hidden_states), FadeOut(*rnn_arrows), FadeOut(rnn_title), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Techniques like L S T Ms, attention mechanisms, and transformers all address this challenge.") as tracker:
            solution_title = Text("Solutions: Attention", font_size=26, color=GREEN).to_edge(UP)
            self.play(Write(solution_title), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        # Create attention visualization
        src_dots = []
        tgt_dots = []
        with self.voiceover(text="Attention mechanisms allow the model to directly connect any position to any other position.") as tracker:
            for i in range(5):
                dot = Dot(radius=0.12, color=WHITE)
                dot.shift(LEFT * 2 + UP * 1.5 - UP * i * 0.5)
                src_dots.append(dot)
            for j in range(5):
                dot = Dot(radius=0.12, color=WHITE)
                dot.shift(RIGHT * 2 + UP * 1.5 - UP * j * 0.5)
                tgt_dots.append(dot)
            self.play(*[Create(d) for d in src_dots + tgt_dots], run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Every word can now attend to every other word, creating direct paths for information flow.") as tracker:
            attention_lines = []
            for i in range(5):
                for j in range(5):
                    line = Line(src_dots[i].get_right(), tgt_dots[j].get_left(), color=BLUE, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.2)
                    attention_lines.append(line)
            strong = Line(src_dots[1].get_right(), tgt_dots[4].get_left(), color=YELLOW, stroke_width=3)
            self.play(*[Create(l) for l in attention_lines], run_time=tracker.duration/2)
            self.play(Create(strong), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Summary section
        with self.voiceover(text="Today, you have learned about long-range dependencies in sequences.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(solution_title), FadeOut(*src_dots), FadeOut(*tgt_dots), FadeOut(*attention_lines), FadeOut(strong), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="You can now recognize why they matter for AI models, understand the challenges RNNs face, and identify solutions like attention mechanisms.") as tracker:
            summary_title = Text("Key Takeaways", font_size=28, color=BLUE).to_edge(UP)
            self.play(Write(summary_title), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        
        takeaways = [
            "- Long-range dependencies connect distant elements",
            "- RNNs struggle due to vanishing gradients",
            "- Attention mechanisms create direct connections",
            "- Critical for NLP tasks like translation"
        ]
        takeaway_texts = []
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Long-range dependencies connect distant elements in sequences. RNNs struggle with these due to vanishing gradients. Attention mechanisms create direct connections. Understanding these dependencies is critical for natural language processing tasks.") as tracker:
            for i, takeaway in enumerate(takeaways):
                text = Text(takeaway, font_size=20, color=WHITE)
                text.shift(UP * 1.2 - UP * i * 0.6)
                takeaway_texts.append(text)
            self.play(*[Write(t) for t in takeaway_texts], run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Mastering long-range dependencies is essential for building AI systems that truly understand context.") as tracker:
            final_box = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(*takeaway_texts), color=GREEN, buff=0.4)
            self.play(Create(final_box), run_time=tracker.duration/2)
        self.wait(1)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Thank you for watching.") as tracker:
            self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(*takeaway_texts), final_box, summary_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
```

```python
from manim import *
from manim_voiceover import VoiceoverScene
from tools.aos_speech_service import AOSSpeechService

class IteratingOnMLExperiments(VoiceoverScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.set_speech_service(
            AOSSpeechService(voice="alba", cache_dir="voiceover_cache")
        )
        
        # ==================== OPENING ====================
        with self.voiceover(text="Welcome, aspiring data scientists!") as tracker:
            welcome = Text("Iterating on Machine Learning Experiments", 
                          font_size=42, color=BLUE)
            self.play(Write(welcome), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Have you ever wondered why some machine learning models excel while others fail?") as tracker:
            question = Text("Why do some ML models excel while others fail?",
                           font_size=28, color=YELLOW).next_to(welcome, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            self.play(FadeIn(question), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="The secret often lies in the power of iteration!") as tracker:
            secret = Text("The Secret: ITERATION", font_size=32, 
                         color=GREEN, weight=BOLD).next_to(question, DOWN, buff=0.6)
            self.play(Write(secret), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(welcome), FadeOut(question), FadeOut(secret))
        
        # ==================== THE ITERATIVE CYCLE ====================
        with self.voiceover(text="Let us explore the iterative cycle that drives successful machine learning experiments.") as tracker:
            cycle_title = Text("The Iterative ML Cycle", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            self.play(Write(cycle_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Create the cycle diagram
        self.play(cycle_title.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Define cycle steps
        steps = [
            ("Hypothesis", BLUE),
            ("Experiment", GREEN),
            ("Results", ORANGE),
            ("Analysis", PURPLE),
            ("Refine", RED)
        ]
        
        cycle_nodes = VGroup()
        arrows = VGroup()
        
        # Create nodes in a circle
        radius = 2.2
        for i, (step, color) in enumerate(steps):
            angle = i * TAU / 5 - PI / 2
            x = radius * np.cos(angle)
            y = radius * np.sin(angle) - 0.3
            
            circle = Circle(radius=0.6, color=color, fill_opacity=0.3)
            label = Text(step, font_size=20, color=color).move_to(circle.get_center())
            node = VGroup(circle, label).move_to([x, y, 0])
            cycle_nodes.add(node)
        
        # Create arrows between nodes
        for i in range(5):
            start = cycle_nodes[i].get_center()
            end = cycle_nodes[(i + 1) % 5].get_center()
            direction = end - start
            direction = direction / np.linalg.norm(direction)
            
            arrow_start = start + direction * 0.7
            arrow_end = end - direction * 0.7
            
            arrow = Arrow(arrow_start, arrow_end, color=WHITE, buff=0.1, stroke_width=2)
            arrows.add(arrow)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="We start with a hypothesis about what might improve our model.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(cycle_nodes[0]), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Then we design and run an experiment to test it.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(arrows[0]), Create(cycle_nodes[1]), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="We collect the results from our experiment.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(arrows[1]), Create(cycle_nodes[2]), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Next, we analyze these results to understand what worked and what did not.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(arrows[2]), Create(cycle_nodes[3]), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Finally, we refine our approach and the cycle begins again.") as tracker:
            self.play(Create(arrows[3]), Create(cycle_nodes[4]), Create(arrows[4]), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.6)
        
        # Closing the loop animation
        with self.voiceover(text="Each iteration brings us closer to an optimal solution.") as tracker:
            loop_arrow = CurvedArrow(cycle_nodes[4].get_top(), cycle_nodes[0].get_top(), 
                                    angle=-0.5, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=3)
            self.play(Create(loop_arrow), run_time=tracker.duration * 0.7)
            self.wait(tracker.duration * 0.3)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(cycle_title), FadeOut(cycle_nodes), FadeOut(arrows), FadeOut(loop_arrow))
        
        # ==================== KEY METRICS ====================
        with self.voiceover(text="To iterate effectively, we need to track the right metrics.") as tracker:
            metrics_title = Text("Key Metrics to Track", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            self.play(Write(metrics_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.play(metrics_title.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Create metric cards in two columns
        metrics_left = VGroup(
            Text("• Accuracy", font_size=22, color=GREEN),
            Text("• Precision", font_size=22, color=GREEN),
            Text("• Recall", font_size=22, color=GREEN)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4).shift(LEFT * 2.5 + DOWN * 0.3)
        
        metrics_right = VGroup(
            Text("• F1 Score", font_size=22, color=ORANGE),
            Text("• Loss Curve", font_size=22, color=ORANGE),
            Text("• Validation Score", font_size=22, color=ORANGE)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4).shift(RIGHT * 2 + DOWN * 0.3)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="For classification tasks, monitor accuracy, precision, and recall.") as tracker:
            self.play(LaggedStart(*[Write(m) for m in metrics_left], lag_ratio=0.3), 
                     run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Also track F1 score, loss curves, and validation performance.") as tracker:
            self.play(LaggedStart(*[Write(m) for m in metrics_right], lag_ratio=0.3), 
                     run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Metric importance box

            insight = Text("Goal: Better Generalization, Not Just Better Numbers!",
                          font_size=24, color=YELLOW).next_to(metrics_left, DOWN, buff=0.8)
            box = SurroundingRectangle(insight, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)

        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(metrics_title), FadeOut(metrics_left), FadeOut(metrics_right), 
                 FadeOut(insight), FadeOut(box))
        
        # ==================== BEST PRACTICES ====================
        with self.voiceover(text="Now, let us look at best practices for documenting and analyzing experiments.") as tracker:
            practices_title = Text("Best Practices", font_size=36, color=BLUE)
            self.play(Write(practices_title), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        self.play(practices_title.animate.to_edge(UP))
        
        # Best practices in two columns
        practices_left = VGroup(
            Text("1. Version Control", font_size=22, color=BLUE),
            Text("   Track code & data", font_size=18, color=GRAY),
            Text("2. Experiment Logging", font_size=22, color=BLUE),

            Text("6. Visualization", font_size=22, color=GREEN),
            Text("   Plot results clearly", font_size=18, color=GRAY)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.25).shift(RIGHT * 2.5 + DOWN * 0.2)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Always use version control for your code and data.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(practices_left[0]), FadeIn(practices_left[1]), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Log every experiment with all its parameters.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(practices_left[2]), FadeIn(practices_left[3]), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Ensure reproducibility by setting random seeds.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(practices_left[4]), FadeIn(practices_left[5]), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Compare against baseline models to measure progress.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(practices_right[0]), FadeIn(practices_right[1]), run_time=tracker.duration)
        
        with self.voiceover(text="Use ablation studies to isolate the impact of each change.") as tracker:
            self.play(Write(practices_right[2]), FadeIn(practices_right[3]), run_time=tracker.duration)
```
